body:
## Why

The coordinator needs memory to plan well across sessions. User memory holds standing preferences that carry to every trip, such as "we never eat at chains". Trip memory holds notes about this trip, such as why the user picked a lodge, so a later session doesn't ask again (technical spec 3.1). The `memory` MCP server gives the coordinator the four tools that read and write it. How memory is stored is already built: `MemoryWriter` and `MemoryReader` in `src/persistence/`.

These are among the first tools, so Joe reviews each server in its own PR: its description, its tools' descriptions, their input schemas, and what they return.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 3.1.
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1, 2.2, and 4.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 8.8, for the memory classes the tools call.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Make the `memory` MCP server. It holds all four memory tools.
- Make a new server for each session, built with that session's user and trip. No memory tool takes a user ID or trip ID as an input, so an agent can't reach another user's memory, even with a made-up ID (tool design, section 4).
- Follow the `trip` server's code (PR #44). `createTripServer()` in `src/tools/trip-server.ts` makes the server for one session from a `TripSession` (`src/tools/trip-session.ts`). The tools and their tests are in `src/tools/trip-brief-tools.ts` and `trip-brief-tools.test.ts`.

## Done when

- Tests with fake repositories (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, such as `src/persistence/fake-memory-store.ts`) cover the four tools as tool design section 2.2 describes them. Examples: one user can't read, update, or forget another user's items through them, and the error is the same as for an ID that doesn't exist. An add over the maximum memory items or the maximum memory item length (technical spec section 10) is refused, and the error gives the limit.
- The PR shows the server's description, and each tool's description, input schema, and an example of what it returns. As in PR #44, take them from an MCP client connected to the real server object, so the schema is the JSON Schema the model sees.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment ([DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), section 7), and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

---

Moved from phase 13b of the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md).
title: The memory server

body:
**Starts** once #117 is merged.

## Why

The coordinator is the agent the user talks to. It runs the planning conversation and calls the workers (technical spec 1). This issue adds it with only the trip brief and memory tools. Then its conduct, the trip brief it sets up, and its memory rules can be tried in the terminal, before the browser chat (#52) exists.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 1, 5.1, 5.2, and 10.
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 4.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 6.

## Open questions

- ~~How does the coordinator know the maximum trip length? Technical spec 5.2 puts the maximum daily driving in its instructions, but not the maximum trip length, and the `update_trip_brief` input descriptions give neither. So the coordinator learns the limit only when an update is refused, which costs a round trip. Example: the user asks for "about three weeks", and it sends 21 days. Raised in PR #44's fourth review.~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: the maximum is in both the instructions and the input descriptions, filled in from the settings when the app starts. See "Do".
- ~~Where does the started-trip rule for memory go? The `memory` server's instructions (PR #116) say: "Once the trip has started, its trip memory can't change, and user memory still can. When a change is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why." The first sentence is about what memory means, so it may belong with the memory rules in the coordinator's instructions (technical spec 5.2) instead. Tool design section 4 puts a rule that covers several tools in the server's instructions, so moving it would change that section too. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while reviewing PR #116.~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: no MCP server sends instructions anymore. A rule that covers several tools goes in each agent's system prompt instead, and #117 makes that change. The started-trip sentence is dropped, so the model learns that rule from the error, as with the `trip` server. See #117's open questions, and "Do" below.
- ~~How can Joe see, in one place, everything the coordinator is told? The model reads its system prompt, each MCP server's instructions, and each tool's name, description, and input schema as one unit. Today they're spread over several files, such as `src/tools/memory-tools.ts`, `memory-input.schema.ts`, and `memory-server.ts`. The schemas are built from Zod, and some limits are filled in from `settings.json`. So comparing two versions, such as before and after a change an evaluation (#53) tests, means reading several diffs. Two ways to fix it:~~
  - ~~Keep all the text in one config file, such as YAML, that the code reads.~~
  - ~~Keep the code as it is, and add a test that writes what each agent sees, as an MCP client gets it, into one checked-in file per agent. The test fails when the file is out of date. Then a PR's diff of that one file is the change to what the model sees, with the JSON Schema and the limits as the model gets them. Claude Code's suggestion, since it needs no rewrite. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23.~~

  Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: the second way, a test that checks a file per agent is up to date, with `npm run agent-views` to rewrite it. It's its own issue, #118, after this one. Server instructions are gone too (#117).

## Do

- Add the coordinator, with only the tools on the `trip` server (`src/tools/trip-server.ts`, PR #44) and the `memory` server (#47). Its instructions cover conduct, the trip brief items to establish, the memory rules, and comfortable driving hours (technical spec, section 5.2).
- Put these rules for the `trip` and `memory` tools in the coordinator's instructions, word for word. They were the servers' instructions until #117 removed them, and tool design section 4 now says they go in the system prompt:
  - "Every tool that changes the trip makes the whole change or none of it. If any part is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why. Each of these tools replies with the feasibility check results the change made new or gone, anywhere in the trip."
  - "When a memory change is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why."
- Give each trip brief item in the coordinator's instructions by the name the tools use, such as `tripLengthInDays`, with what it means (tool design, section 4). The `update_trip_brief` input descriptions say only how to pass each value, so the meanings are in no tool. Functional spec 5.2 gives most of them. It doesn't give these, which the input descriptions said before PR #44 trimmed them:
  - Interests and must-sees are in the user's words, with why they matter. A must-see can be one place, an area, a road, or an activity.
  - The rest days item records what the user asked for. It doesn't mark any day.
  - The default tier is the budget tier for lodging and meals when no budget rule covers them.
- Add a `coordinatorModel` setting to `settings.json`, set to the exact model ID `claude-opus-5-5`, and give it to the Agent SDK. A short name such as "opus" would move to newer models on its own, so a later run could use a different model. Write the setting into technical spec section 10. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-18.
- Give the coordinator the maximum trip length (functional spec 5.2). Add a trip length bullet next to comfortable driving hours in its instructions (technical spec 5.2): it gives the maximum, and says that when the user asks for more, explain the limit and propose a version that fits. Also give the limits in the `update_trip_brief` input descriptions: `tripLengthInDays` gets "from 1 to" the maximum trip length, and `comfortableDrivingInHours` gets "at most" the maximum daily driving. Fill in every number, in the instructions and the descriptions, from `settings.json` when the app starts, as the memory tools do for the item length. Never write a number into the text, so a changed setting can't leave stale text. Write this into technical spec 5.2 and 10, and tool design section 4. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-23.
- Add today's date to user messages, and the line after a resume, as technical spec section 5.2 says.
- Log each `mirror_error` message, with the session's ID and the error, and do nothing more. The Agent SDK sends the app that message when it drops transcript lines after 3 failed tries to save them (persistence design section 6). A few transcript lines out of order after a retry are accepted. Write both into persistence design section 6. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-18.
- Add a dev script to chat with the coordinator in the terminal, against the local database.

## Done when

Joe runs these conversations by hand in the terminal. Claude Code runs each one first, to catch problems before Joe's run, and the PR quotes the lines that show it.

- A discovery conversation fills in the trip brief, and `read_trip_brief` shows every item.
- "We never eat at chains" goes to user memory, and "skip I-35 this time" goes to trip memory.
- On a second trip, the coordinator confirms the user's usual driving hours instead of asking from scratch (functional spec 11, S9).
- Asked for 14 hours of driving a day, the coordinator pushes back, and sets no more than the maximum daily driving (technical spec section 10).

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Move the remaining work from `plan/` into GitHub issues, one issue at a time, with Joe's agreement on each. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-19.

## Do

- Make an issue for each phase not yet done, and each open item still open. Titles and bodies don't use phase numbers, except for the phase 13 issues (#47, #48). Refer to other work by its issue number.
- In the plan doc, strike out each moved phase or item, and add "Moved to #N."
- Close open item 8 with no design doc change: "**Closed 2026-10-19:** not needed. Accepted on a development server." Do it in one of this work's PRs, not a PR of its own.
- Add an issue template with the sections the phase issues use: Design, Open questions, Do, Done when, Ends in, and Settled in.
- Delete `plan/batch-4.md`.
- Freeze `plan/`: add a line at the top of each file saying it's frozen and work is tracked in the project. Update CLAUDE.md and DEVELOPMENT.md so new work goes in issues, and `plan/` is read only to look up an old phase or open item.

## Done when

- Every phase not yet done, and every open item still open, has an issue or a closed line.
- CLAUDE.md and DEVELOPMENT.md no longer send new work to `plan/`.

## Ends in

PRs that change only `plan/`, CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, and the issue template.

**Settled in:** chat.

body:
**Starts** once #48 is merged.

## Why

This is the first version Joe can use. Until now, the coordinator runs only in the terminal (#48). This issue lets a signed-in user plan a trip in the browser, with trips and sessions saved, so a conversation can be left and picked up again.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 3 and 4.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 8.2 and 8.5.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 2, 3, and 10.1.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add the endpoints: list the user's trips, with name, dates, and last updated; start a trip from the "New trip" form; list a trip's sessions; send a message, with the reply streamed back over Server-Sent Events; and resume a session.
- Check that the signed-in user owns the trip before making a session's MCP servers (tool design, section 4).
- Keep a turn running when the browser disconnects.
- Refuse to start or resume a session, or take a message, once the trip has started. Check before each message.
- Add the home screen: the user's trips, and "New trip."
- Add the trip page: its sessions, with date and title, each with resume, plus "start a new session." Add the chat view, showing the reply as it streams in.

## Done when

- Tests with a fake in place of the Agent SDK (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) show that another user's trip is refused.
- A stream closed partway through a turn still leaves the whole turn in the transcript.
- A started trip refuses a new message.
- On the deployed site after the merge (systems design, section 7), Joe signs in, starts a trip, and goes through discovery.
- After a reload, resuming the session restores the conversation.
- A new session on the same trip knows the trip brief and memory.
- The second test user, which Joe added in Supabase for isolation tests, sees none of Joe's trips, and the coordinator knows none of his preferences (functional spec 11, S8).
- Closing the tab partway through a reply, then coming back, shows the finished reply.

## Ends in

A PR. This is the first version Joe can use.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

body:
**Evaluate** when #132 is done.

## Why

When this is done, the agent's behavior can be checked again after any change to its instructions, its tools, or its model, by running a set of evaluations. Without them, the only way to tell whether a change made the agent better or worse is Joe testing by hand.

## Design

- [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), section 5.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 3.1 (tests).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 11.

## Open questions

- Which framework runs the evaluations? promptfoo is the likely choice. Check its current docs, and that it can run the app's coordinator through the Agent SDK on the Claude Max plan (systems design, section 5).
- How is each result scored: by what was saved, such as the trip brief and memory, by a model reading the reply, or both?
- How much of the Claude Max plan does one run of the evaluations use?
- How do the simulated user (#66) and the acceptance tests (#69) fit with the evaluations?
- ~~Do #66, #67, #68, and #69 still make sense as written? They're the testing and checking work after the workers, and they were planned before the evaluations in Phoenix and the evaluation issues, such as #167, #177, and #185. Look at them again together with this issue and those. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-28.~~ Settled 2026-11-04 in chat: #66 becomes the setup for a simulated user on any harness and model, such as Codex with a GPT model. It chats through `npm run live-chat` (#251), a terminal client for the app's API, signed in as its own Supabase user, and is shaken out with a whole San Francisco trip on the local stack. #67 and #68 become the first trips recorded on the live site for the corpus. They check how the simulated user behaved and what was saved to the trip brief, not that the itinerary matches domain model section 5, since live places and the workers' picks change from run to run. #69 stays as written. Traces in the `road-trip-agent-local` Phoenix project are throwaway, and the `road-trip-agent` project holds the sessions to evaluate.
- Which evaluations watch for these `update_trip_brief` mistakes? Tool descriptions start lean, with no example of a whole call. One is added only when an evaluation shows a mistake it would fix. The mistakes:
  - Sending every item on every call, when only one changed.
  - Splitting one change into a call per item.
  - Summarizing the user in a text item, such as `mustSeesText`, instead of using their words.
- Should an evaluation cover how an agent judges a place's budget tier, value, mid-range, or posh, at the edges between tiers? A place could fit two tiers, depending on how it's looked at. Nothing defines where one tier ends and the next starts yet (#60). Raised while going through the coordinator's view file, `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`.
- ~~Should an evaluation check that the coordinator keeps itinerary facts out of trip memory? No fact is kept in both (functional spec 5.2). In Joe's terminal run on 2026-10-23, the coordinator saved "Trip starts and ends in Austin. The user flies out of Austin the night of Sunday, February 14, 2027" to trip memory. The start and end places and the dates belong in the itinerary. The flight that evening belongs in memory, since the itinerary can't hold it. #55 changes the coordinator's memory instructions to say so. It also adds `update_itinerary`, so the evaluation can't run before #55 is merged. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while settling #55's open questions.~~ Moved to #209 on 2026-10-28.
- May the coordinator add a note for itself to a memory item, beyond the user's words? In all five runs of the #132 spike, it did. "We never eat at chains" became "Never eats at chain restaurants. Suggest only independent, local places for meals." "Skip I-35 this time" became "Avoid I-35 on this trip. Plan routes out of Austin that don't use it, and set waypoints if a leg would default onto it." The judge's rubric didn't say whether that counts as a rule the user didn't state, so it graded the same wording both ways ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.5). Raised by the #132 spike on 2026-10-24.
- Should functional spec 10.2's example change? It gives "no chain restaurants" as trip memory, but the #48 check expects "we never eat at chains" in user memory. The "never" is what makes it a standing preference. Raised by the #132 spike on 2026-10-24.
- ~~How do the user's message and the right token counts get into each turn's trace? The Agent SDK instrumentation shows the streamed prompt as `{}`, and leaves cache tokens out of its input count, so a 48,255-token turn shows as 8. The spike branch fixes both with spans from our own code in place of the instrumentation: one for the turn, and one for each model call and each tool call, with each call's thinking and tokens. Workers aren't covered yet ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), sections 2.2 and 3). Raised by the #132 spike on 2026-10-24.~~ Moved to #135 on 2026-10-25.
- ~~How is `@arizeai/phoenix-client` installed for good? It names `@anthropic-ai/sdk` `^0.35.0` as an optional peer, and the app has 0.135.0, so `npm install` fails without `--legacy-peer-deps`. The spike tested an `overrides` entry in `package.json` that fixes it with no flag ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 3). Raised by the #132 spike on 2026-10-24.~~ Moved to #282 on 2026-11-05.
- Where do experiments send their traces and results? The #132 spike ran Phoenix on Joe's machine, under the `evals` Compose profile. #135 runs one Phoenix on the server, reached from Joe's machine through an SSH tunnel, with the server's traces in the `road-trip-agent` project and local ones in `road-trip-agent-local`. So the experiments could use that Phoenix too, through the tunnel, or a local Phoenix of their own. Raised on 2026-10-25, while writing #135.
- Which evaluations check how the coordinator finds a place the user names? #152 adds `find_in_trip`, which searches the trip's own places, next to `find_place`, which searches Google. So there are two tools for a place the user names. The coordinator should call `find_in_trip` first, and `find_place` only for a place that isn't in the trip (technical spec 5.2). `find_in_trip` always returns the 5 closest places, so the coordinator also has to notice when none is the place meant. Example: the user wants a new restaurant, Desert Rose Grill, and the closest match is the Desert Pearl Inn. It should ask, not select the inn. And when `select_user_place` says the place is also a candidate on another stop (#56), it should notice, and fix the pick or ask. Raised on 2026-10-26, from #129 ([research/itinerary-read-size.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/itinerary-read-size.md), sections 6.3 and 6.4).
- Should the agents' prompts go in Phoenix's prompt registry? It keeps versions of a prompt, and its playground and experiments can run one against saved spans. It doesn't link a prompt to traces by itself: the app would set `llm.prompt_template.version` on the spans. #194 puts the app's commit SHA on each turn's span, and the view files at that commit show each agent's prompt and tools, so a registry version isn't needed just to see what an agent read. Our prompts are built in code, so the registry would hold a second copy. Raised on 2026-10-28, while settling #194. The judge prompts fit better. A rubric is one model call with a few slots, which is what Phoenix's playground runs. So rubric versions could be tried there against the judge's dataset, turns labeled by Joe, and compared turn by turn. Raised on 2026-11-03, in chat.
- Should a walkthrough of the prompts decide which behaviors get an evaluation? The design walkthroughs (reviews/walkthroughs/) had a fresh agent read only the design docs and play the user and every agent through the San Francisco and Moab trips, and they found many design gaps before any code existed. The same could be done with the agents' instructions and tool descriptions, as the view files show them: give an agent a view file and a trip, and have it say what it would call, and why. A problem that's clearly a wording mistake gets fixed, since a clear fix goes in without an evaluation. One where it's unclear whether a change helps becomes an evaluation candidate. Running it with a smaller model, such as Sonnet, may show where the wording leans on Opus to fill gaps. Caveat: a model saying what it would do isn't the same as what it does deep in a real conversation, so this finds wording problems, not behavior. Running the real coordinator with faked tool replies and a model playing the user would show behavior.
- When should real traces be scored after the fact? Phoenix can run evaluators over traces that already exist, and attach the scores to their spans, with nothing run again. Code would pick out the suspect cases, and a judge model would decide the fuzzy ones. Example: code finds each `find_place` call with no earlier `find_in_trip` call in the session. A judge then decides whether the place was one the user named, and whether an earlier search was for the same place, such as "Desert Rose" and "Desert Rose Grill". Some mistakes need only code, such as an `update_trip_brief` call that resends an item with the value it already had. A score over traces is a rate, such as 3 of 40 turns, not a pass or fail. There are few real traces today, so this waits until simulations or walkthroughs make more. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-03, in chat.
- How are the evaluations built up? This is a provisional plan, not a commitment. It's what we're working toward, and it can change as we go. Sketched by Joe and Claude in chat on 2026-11-03, after running Phoenix's built-in evaluators on the Bar Harbor session:
  - Joe learns more of Phoenix first, through its tutorials.
  - Record more sessions to build a corpus. Joe and his wife each plan a trip. Simulated users play the San Francisco and Moab trips on the live site (#66, #67, #68). Any harness and model can play one, such as Claude Code, a GPT model through Codex, or an open-weight model.
  - A simulated user gets a trip file, a persona file, and its instructions, with no hooks steering it (#66). The trip file holds the facts it knows (dates, places, budget, driving limits), things it hasn't decided, and changes partway through, such as skipping Denver once the first draft is done. The persona file says how it talks, such as curt or impatient. Its prompt says to answer only what's asked, give one or two facts at a time, and stick with any answer it makes up. The trip file also works as an answer key, to check what the agent saved to the trip brief.
  - Write one general evaluator first, to learn the process. It covers how the agent does on any turn, not one behavior. Phoenix's built-in rubrics don't fit a long planning conversation: on Bar Harbor, correctness marked 22 of 23 turns incorrect. So the rubric is our own, using the built-ins only as a starting point. Start with "grounded in the record": every place, hour, distance, or price in a reply comes from a tool result or the trip record. Two strong models, such as Opus and a GPT 6.1 model, label turns from the corpus, each on its own. Code compares their labels, and Joe looks only at the turns where they disagree. No turns are labeled by hand. Then compare the judge's labels to theirs, and refine the rubric until they agree. Decided by Joe on 2026-11-05, in chat. The corpus is the sessions with a `corpus` session annotation in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project: 21 sessions, 3 `real_user` and 18 `simulated_user`, labeled on 2026-11-05. The first general evaluator, "grounded in the record", moved to #282 on 2026-11-05, with what it checks, what the judge reads, and how the labeling runs. Two or three general evaluators may follow, such as these:
    - "Request handled": the reply does what the user asked.
    - "The reply is for the user": it tells the user what they need to know, and doesn't think out loud. On a new trip, one reply began "I need to read brief and memory first." That's a note the coordinator wrote to itself, before its tool calls, and the user saw it. #65 adds a line to the instructions against it. This evaluator shows whether it still happens. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat.
    - "Fits the trip": what the reply says makes sense given the itinerary. In #282's sample, a Moab reply chose a hotel and said "after a day of hiking, you'll also have a pool and a hot breakfast there". Its Day 2 leaves the hotel at 5:30 a.m. and doesn't come back until 8:02 p.m., so the hot breakfast doesn't fit that day. Each fact had a source, so "grounded in the record" passes it. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-06, in chat, while reviewing #282's first set.
    - "Tool use": it picks the right tool, with the right inputs, and doesn't call tools it doesn't need. Phoenix's built-in evaluators for tool use didn't work well on Bar Harbor, so the rubric is our own. It also answers a question moved from #65 on 2026-11-04: are about two dozen tools too many for the coordinator? If it chooses badly, merge the add, update, and remove tools for each kind of item.
  - The judge sees what the agent saw: the coordinator's system prompt from the commit on the turn's span, and the earlier turns with their tool calls. On Bar Harbor, adding that context changed tool response handling from 21 of 23 turns incorrect to 10.
  - Then write the behavior evaluations: the issues labeled "Eval Canidate", plus the ones listed in this issue. They can start from recorded sessions with `npm run run-turn` (#245), before any simulation exists.
  - Then run more simulated sessions (#66) to grow the corpus. Run both kinds of evaluation on them. A general evaluator gives a rate over many turns, such as 3 of 40. A behavior evaluation passes or fails on a case built to trigger the behavior.
- Do the evaluations run as Phoenix experiments, written in TypeScript? A dataset row would name a recorded turn (session, turn, and message) and what's expected of it. The experiment's task runs that turn with `npm run run-turn`, and code checks and judges score the result. Phoenix keeps each experiment's results, so a run before a prompt change and a run after it can be compared case by case. Joe leans toward TypeScript for the real evaluations, since they'd reuse app code such as `run-turn`, even though his Phoenix tutorials are in Python. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-03, in chat.

## Do

- Set up the framework, and a command that runs the evaluations against the local stack (systems design, section 6), outside `npm run check`.
- Start an evaluation of one turn from a recorded session with `npm run run-turn` (#245). It gives the coordinator the recorded conversation and the trip as it stood, and runs the turn on today's code. Leave the copied transcript lines as they are. The API drops each of the coordinator's earlier thinking blocks once anything before it in the conversation changes. In #245, rewriting the first message's date line dropped all 17 of them in the Bar Harbor session's turn 5 (persistence design, section 8.9).
- Watch the runs for the coordinator reacting to the two lines Claude Code adds that the recorded turn didn't have: its date change line, and an environment line with the local working folder (persistence design, section 8.9). #245 accepted both. If the coordinator reacts to either, look at it again.
- Turn the checks in #48 into evaluations: discovery fills in the trip brief, user or trip memory, confirming the usual driving hours on a second trip, and pushing back on 14 hours of driving.
- Write how the evaluations run into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, in place of "How they run is settled when the first one is written."

## Done when

A PR.

body:
**Starts** once #48 is merged.

## Why

The coordinator can't plan stays and stops until it can read the trip it's building, and look up places. `read_itinerary` gives it the whole trip, or one part of it, as short lines (technical spec 7.2). `find_place` and `read_place` let it turn a name, such as "Moab", into a place, and answer questions about that place.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`read_itinerary`), 2.3 (`find_place` and `read_place`), and 4.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 7.2.

## Open questions

- ~~What's the size limit on an in-process MCP tool's result? Claude Code may cut off large results. The limit for MCP tools is believed to be 25,000 tokens, but it hasn't been checked for in-process servers.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the limit is 25,000 tokens. That's the default in the Claude Code that SDK 0.3.301 ships (2.1.301), and nothing found in it treats in-process servers differently. A result over it is saved to a file, and the model gets the file's path and a short preview. The coordinator has no Read tool, so for it the result is cut off. So `read_itinerary` checks its own reply, and returns an error instead of a reply over 25,000 tokens. A full read is fine while trips stay under the limit. If one goes over, the fix is to rethink the four uses of a full read (technical spec 5.2), not to raise the limit.
- ~~How does `read_itinerary` get its check results? A read runs `FeasibilityChecker.workOut()` and `compare()`, and saves nothing (domain model 4.8). But `TripReader.read()` hands back only the trip. PR #35 creates the checker only inside `TripWriter`'s finish, from the settings, the clock, and the write's calendar. The read tool needs the same: a calendar and a checker for the trip it read. Raised in PR #35.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the tool makes them, the way `look_up_stay_weather` does in `src/tools/weather-tools.ts`. It reads the trip with `TripReader.read()`, and gets the calendar from `calendarAndServicesFor(trip, settings, now)`. Then it creates a `FeasibilityChecker` from the trip brief, the settings, and that calendar, runs `workOut()` on the itinerary, and runs `compare()` against the itinerary's saved check results. The comparison marks each result new or already known. Nothing is saved. `TripSession` (`src/tools/trip-session.ts`) gets the full `settings` in place of `limits`, plus `now`, as `WeatherSession` has. `TripReader` stays as it is. This keeps the layers one way: tools use persistence and the domain, persistence uses the domain, and the domain uses neither.
- ~~Put the itinerary into the line the app adds after a resume. Technical spec 5.2 gives the line as "This session was resumed. Read the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory first." Until `read_itinerary` exists, the coordinator can't read the itinerary, so #48 left it out. Its line, `RESUMED_LINE` in `src/agent/app-lines.ts`, says "Read the trip brief and memory first." The coordinator's instructions say the same in their section on reading the trip brief and memory. Both get the itinerary added here. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while #48 was being built.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat:
  - `RESUMED_LINE` becomes technical spec 5.2's line word for word: "This session was resumed. Read the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory first." The comment above it about #54 comes out.
  - The instructions section "Reading the trip brief and memory" in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` becomes "Reading the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory". Its first bullet becomes "At the start of a session, before your first reply, read the trip brief, the whole itinerary, and memory." Its second becomes "After a resume, read all three again before changing anything. Another session may have changed the trip, and a session of another trip may have changed user memory." Its third, on reading memory again, stays.
  - The section gets one more bullet, on warnings still open from an earlier session (technical spec 5.2), such as: "In your first reply, briefly mention warnings that are still open, such as 'Still open from last time: the trip is 4 days, and you asked for 5.'"
  - The offer to rerun the weather worker when a forecast is now available waits for #64, which builds that worker.

## Do

- Add `find_place` and `read_place` on the `places` server, and give them to the coordinator. `read_place` checks the place belongs to the session's trip.
- Add `read_itinerary`, for the whole trip or scoped to a day, stay, or stop. Leave out route lines.
- Add the itinerary to the resume line and to the coordinator's instructions on reading at the start of a session, and the bullet on open warnings, as open question 3 says.
- Measure a full read of a 14-day trip: its characters, and its tokens as the API counts them.
- Make `read_itinerary` return an error when its reply would be over 25,000 tokens, such as "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return." The tool can't count tokens without calling the API, so it checks the reply's characters. Set that limit from the measured characters per token, with room to spare, so the tool stops before Claude Code's limit would.

## Done when

- In a chat with the coordinator, it resolves "Moab," and answers "is Milt's open on Mondays?" from `read_place`. Milt's is a stop on Moab Day 2, in the example trip in domain model section 5.2.
- Tests on the example trips (domain model, section 5) show what each scope returns.
- The measured size, the 25,000-token limit, and the error are written into tool design section 2.1. If the 14-day trip's full read is near the limit, Joe hears about it before #55 starts.
- A test shows a read over the limit returns the error.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

body:
**Starts** once #54 is merged.

## Why

The skeleton is the trip's frame: its stays, the nights at each, and the legs between them with their drive times (technical spec 4.2). These tools let the coordinator build it, and see each leg's drive time, so it can tell the user when a plan doesn't fit. The rest of the planning hangs off the skeleton.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`update_itinerary`, `add_stay`, `update_stay`, `remove_stay`, `update_day`, `set_waypoints`) and 2.4.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.1, 4.2 (discovery, shape, and skeleton), and 5.2.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.8.

## Open questions

- ~~How do the two sentences #48 put in the coordinator's instructions fit into the full bullet on broken feasibility rules (technical spec 5.2)? In #48's terminal runs, every `update_trip_brief` reply carried "The trip is 1 day, and the brief asks for 9," since no stays exist during discovery, and the coordinator raised it in reply after reply. So #48 added a "Check results" section, `CHECK_RESULTS` in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`: "While the days aren't laid out yet, don't raise a warning that comes only from that, such as the trip length. Stay quiet about check results marked already known." Both come from that bullet. Holding the warning back in code, by skipping the trip length check while there are no stays, was turned down. It covers only the start of the skeleton, and code can't tell when the skeleton is finished. Agreed by Joe on 2026-10-23, while #48 was being built.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the full bullet replaces #48's two sentences, split into short points. #48's sentences become the third and seventh points. "Until the skeleton is finished" stands in for the spec's "while the skeleton is still being built", so it also covers discovery, before any stay exists. The point on "may be too early" comes in now, though stops come only in #56. The point on the "changed" mark comes from this issue's Do list. Tune the wording after real runs if needed. The section:

  > ## Check results
  >
  > - When a feasibility rule fails, say which rule and by how much, then offer two or three trade-offs.
  > - Raise warnings at the end of the turn, for those still open, once no change is still being discussed with the user.
  > - Until the skeleton is finished, don't raise warnings that come only from it being unfinished, such as the trip length and the last day's driving.
  > - Hold an opening-hours warning marked "may be too early" until every stop before it on its day has a selected place. The write that clears the mark returns the warning as new.
  > - Raise each warning once. "Already known" means an earlier write returned it, not that the user heard it. Raise any warning you held back once the change is settled, whatever its mark.
  > - A result marked changed was already known, but its text is different now. Example: after the user lowers their driving hours, a daily driving warning gives the new limit. Decide whether the user needs to hear it.
  > - Otherwise, stay quiet about check results marked already known.
  > - When the user turns down a note, such as a faster stop order, save that to trip memory, so a note that goes away and comes back isn't raised again.
- ~~How do the coordinator's instructions keep itinerary facts out of trip memory? With only the trip brief and memory tools (#48), the coordinator saved the start and end places and the dates to trip memory, such as "Trip starts and ends in Austin. The user flies out of Austin the night of Sunday, February 14, 2027." Once this issue adds `update_itinerary`, those belong in the itinerary, since no fact is kept in both (functional spec 5.2). The memory section of the instructions (`MEMORY` in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`) says trip memory holds notes "that don't fit the trip brief". It would need to say the itinerary too. Seen in Joe's terminal run on 2026-10-23.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: two changes to the memory section. Its first paragraph says trip memory holds notes for this trip only "that don't fit the trip brief or the itinerary," matching functional spec 10.2, with the same examples. "Writing memory" gets one more bullet: "Don't save what the trip brief or the itinerary holds, such as the start and end places or the dates. Save what they can't hold about it, such as 'flies out of Austin the night of Sunday, February 14.'" The itinerary has the last day's date, but not the flight that evening. No design doc changes, since functional spec 10.2 already says this. An evaluation for it is an open question in #53.
- ~~How does the coordinator read a long trip, when a whole read is too large to return? #54 measured a whole `read_itinerary` of a 14-day trip with 8 stays, five stops a day, and 312 candidates (`src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`). It came to 72,264 characters, which the API counts as 38,271 tokens for `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude Code returns at most 25,000 tokens of a tool result, so the tool refuses any reply over 40,000 characters, with "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return. Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead." (tool design 2.1). At that density, a whole read fits a trip of about a week. Technical spec 5.2 has the coordinator read the whole itinerary at the start of a session, after a resume, and for "what's left to decide?". On a longer trip it now gets the error, and has to read the trip a stay or a day at a time. Raising the limit isn't the fix: a result Claude Code cuts off would give the coordinator part of the trip, with nothing to say so. Two ways to go: a whole read that shows each stop's selected place and a count of its other candidates, leaving the full list to a read of the stay or stop; or instructions that have the coordinator read a long trip a stay at a time in those cases. Raised in PR #128 on 2026-10-23.~~ Moved to #129 on 2026-10-23, a spike on whole itinerary reads of long trips.

  The parts of the trip that only a whole read shows today, raised in PR #128's review, moved to #129 on 2026-10-24.
- ~~How does `compute_route` give the place each plain name matched? Tool design 2.4 says it returns "the place each plain name resolved to", so the coordinator can spot a bad match, such as "Dewey Bridge, UT" landing in Salt Lake City. But Google Routes never says what a name matched: it gives a Google place ID and coordinates, with no name or address. The Geocoding API would, but the server key allows only Routes, Places, and Weather.~~ Settled 2026-10-24 in chat: code matches each plain name with a Places Text Search for the best match, asking only for its ID, name, and address, which makes it a Pro call. It routes by the match's place ID, and the reply gives each match's name and address. Nothing is saved. Written into tool design 2.4 and Google design 2.1, 2.4, and 5.

## Do

- Add these tools and `compute_route`. Each write's reply is built from what the write hands back, as tool design section 2.1 says.
- Report check results whose text changed. Today a result that's still there after a write is "already known", so the reply leaves it out unless the write touched its subject, even when its text changed. Example: the user lowers their driving hours from 6 to 5, and Day 2's warning now gives the new limit, but the reply doesn't show it. Make `FeasibilityChecker.compare()` mark a known result whose text differs from its saved match as "changed". Each write's reply lists changed results anywhere in the trip, like new ones. The coordinator decides whether to raise one. Write it into domain model 4.8 and tool design 2.1. Then take out `touchedBy()` in `src/tools/trip-brief-tools.ts`, which PR #44 added for the driving hours only. Raised in PR #44's third review.
- Add the coordinator's instructions for anchors and stretches, the shape and skeleton rounds, broken feasibility rules, and changes to stays.

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- The coordinator sets up the Moab trip from domain model section 5.2: start and end places, start date, Moab for 3 nights, Torrey for 1, and the Dewey Bridge waypoint. A read shows each leg's drive time.
- Asked for Seattle to Miami in five days at four hours a day, it says how far short the plan falls and offers trade-offs (functional spec 11, S3).

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

**Starts** once #55 and #150 are merged. #150 writes the design for the line in `select_user_place`'s reply.

## Why

Laying out a day means adding its stops: meals, attractions, and quick looks along the way. Often the user names some of the places, and these tools let the coordinator add and select them without a worker. San Francisco Day 1, in domain model section 5.1, has five such places.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`add_stops`, `update_stop`, `move_stop`, `remove_stops`, `select_candidate`, `select_user_place`, `reject_places`).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (must-sees) and 5.2.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add these tools.
- Add the coordinator's instructions for must-sees, places the user names, visit times, rejections, and moving stops.
- Add the end of technical spec 5.2's bullet on a stay that moves to a different town, which #55 left out since it needs `reject_places`. #55's "Changes to stays" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` ends at "Remove the stops that no longer fit." Add, word for word: "Reject the hotel if it no longer fits, with a reason such as \"the stay moved to Bakersfield.\" Example: moving from Monterey to Carmel keeps every stop and the hotel. Skipping Monterey to drive I-5 to Bakersfield removes every stop on its days and rejects the hotel."
- Give `select_user_place`'s reply a line for each other stop or stay where the place is a candidate, as tool design 2.1's `select_user_place` row says, such as "Oscar's Cafe is also a candidate for Day 1, Stop 4 (stop_…), meal: \"dinner\"." Name each stop or stay as `find_in_trip` does. #152 builds `find_in_trip`, and may be built at the same time. If it's merged first, use its function that names where a place sits. If not, write that function so #152 can use it. Added on 2026-10-26, from #129.
- Add the rule in technical spec 5.2, "When `select_user_place` says the place is also a candidate elsewhere", to the coordinator's instructions.
- Add the last sentence of technical spec 5.2's bullet "When the user names a place", which #152 left out since it names `select_candidate` and `select_user_place`. #152 adds a "Places the user names" section to `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`. Add this as a bullet at its end, word for word: "A place that's already a candidate on the stop or stay the user means is selected with select_candidate, not select_user_place." #152's functions that name a stop or stay are `stopName()` and `stayName()` in `src/tools/spot-names.ts`. Added on 2026-10-26, from #152.
- Name the `after` input in the descriptions of `add_stops` and `move_stop`, and say what "first" does, as `add_stay` does (tool design 2.1, "Where an item goes"). Such as: "Give after the ID of the stop it follows on that day, or \"first\" to put it before every other stop on the day." Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- A stop's set time takes "none", for no set time (tool design 2.1, "Times are clock times"). #156 renamed `NO_TIME` in `src/tools/skeleton-input.schema.ts` to `DEFAULT_START_TIME`, which is "default", since a day's start time was its only use. Add a constant for "none" for the stop tools. Don't reuse `DEFAULT_START_TIME`. Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- A meal's `tierRule` input gives only its format, as `add_stay`'s does: "In a few words, such as \"the default tier\"." What the rule means is in the coordinator's instructions (tool design, section 4). Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- Use the terms in the tool descriptions as the coordinator's instructions define them, in the section "The itinerary", such as stop, set, search area, waypoint, and road time. Don't define them again in a description, and add a line to that section for any new line a read or reply shows (tool design, section 4). Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- Change `compute_route`'s reply from "Drive times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer." to "Road times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer.", so it uses the name "The itinerary" section gives this figure. Change tool design 2.4 if it quotes the reply. Added on 2026-10-26, from #160.
- Fix the "Leg" and "Day" terms in the coordinator's "The itinerary" section, so they fit the first and last days. The "Leg" term says a leg runs "from where the party slept to where it sleeps that night", but Day 1's leg starts at the start place, and the last day's leg ends at the end place, where the party doesn't sleep. The "Day" term says a day "either moves to a new stay, or stays put", but the last day does neither. As a starting point, a leg runs "from where the day starts, the start place or a stay, to where it ends, a stay or the end place", and the "Day" term covers the last day too. Change technical spec 5.2 to match. Added on 2026-10-26, from #160.

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- San Francisco Day 1 is laid out with the five places the user names, all selected, with times close to domain model section 5.1. No worker is needed.
- Making the Boardwalk visit five hours gives a warning that the Whaling Station dinner is late, and the coordinator raises it.
- "No Sardine Factory" rejects it, with the user's reason. The Sardine Factory is a Monterey restaurant. It isn't in the example, so it's only there to be ruled out.

And in the tests:

- `select_user_place` with a place that's a candidate on another stop or stay succeeds, and its reply names each of those stops or stays.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
