body:
**Starts** once #191, #197, #198, and #199 are merged. #59, #56, #182, and #184 are already merged.

#197 runs the coordinator as a named agent. #198 builds how every worker is started and what it returns. #199 adds the workers' tools on the `trip` server. This issue builds the stay researcher on top of them.

## Why

The stay researcher is the first worker. It finds lodging for a stay, and fills the stops near it with candidates, so the coordinator can offer the user choices (technical spec 6.1). It's also the first time the coordinator hands work to another agent.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (fill), 5.3, 6.1, 6.4, and 6.5 (how a worker is started, its brief, its result, and the hooks and settings).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1 (the `worker` server), 2.1 (the candidate tools and `read_worker_brief_facts`), 2.6 (`report_result`), and 3.
- [Web search design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/web-search.md).

## Open questions

- ~~What exact fields go in a worker brief and in a worker's result? Technical spec section 5.3 lists the contents, not the fields. Proposed on 2026-10-27: the result goes through a worker tool with a schema, checked by hooks, and the worker reads its brief's facts from code, so the coordinator writes only what needs its judgment. #182 says the pattern in full, and checks it against the SDK.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #191,** which designs the worker's setup from what #182 found.
- ~~Can a session resume when its transcript ends in a worker call that never got its result? A restart can leave it that way. If the SDK won't resume, the transcript adapter (`src/persistence/transcript-adapter.ts`) drops the unfinished line. #182 checks it.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in PR #189:** the SDK resumes as is, and adds a result saying the call was interrupted, so the transcript adapter needs no change. #191 writes it into persistence design section 7.
- ~~May a worker run in the background? Each subagent definition has a `background` option. In a check in PR #23, a background helper finished after the coordinator's turn ended, and the SDK started a second turn on its own, in the same `query()` call. Raised in PR #23. #136 found that the `Agent` tool itself runs a worker in the background unless the model sets its `run_in_background` input to `false`. With two workers, the coordinator left it out. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`, in the Claude Code process's environment, keeps every worker in the foreground, and two still ran at the same time ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.7, once PR #138 merges). #182 finds the setting that keeps workers in the foreground.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in PR #189:** no. A background worker's own text skips the result pattern. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` keeps every worker in the foreground. #191 writes it into the design.
- ~~Meal coverage: recommend every meal, or only lunch and dinner by default? It depends on data quality. From the functional spec. Moved from open item 1 in the development plan.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** by default, the coordinator gives each day a lunch stop and a dinner stop. On a driving day, lunch is along the leg. Breakfast gets a stop only when the trip brief's meal preferences say local breakfast, not hotel breakfast. Anything the user asks for changes the default, such as "we'll picnic on the drive" or pie at Gifford Homestead, saved to trip memory for this trip or user memory for a standing habit. A fixed default makes a trip with the same brief get the same meals, so a missing meal in a trace is a bug or a user request, not a model choice. It costs a card for every lunch and dinner, which is accepted, since choosing where to eat is a big part of a road trip. When a worker finds fewer than three good places, it adds the ones it found and says so in its result. When it finds none, the coordinator tells the user. Write it into technical spec 5.2, under laying out a day, and functional spec 7.3.
- ~~What does each budget tier, value, mid-range, and posh, mean? The coordinator's instructions name the tiers but don't say. Functional spec 7.1 says the agent infers a place's tier from descriptions, reviews, and price signals, such as "$$", but not where one tier ends and the next starts. The stay researcher is the first agent that picks places by tier. Raised while going through the coordinator's view file, `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`.~~ More, raised by Joe on 2026-10-27 from the Natick to Bar Harbor trip (session `session_5hf47qpn`): **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat,** in the parts below. #184 makes a tier a label on each place, not a target, and #60 builds on it.
  - ~~A tier can't be a dollar amount, since a posh hotel in Ohio may cost less than a value one in San Francisco. A proposal to weigh: a tier is where a place sits among comparable places in its area, described by the experience rather than price. Value is simple and clean, such as a chain motel or counter service. Mid-range is comfortable and full service, such as a typical sit-down restaurant. Posh is the best the area offers, such as a boutique hotel or a chef-driven restaurant that needs a reservation.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** A tier is a label on each place, not a target. #184 makes the change: it defines each tier by what staying or eating there is like, has the worker label each lodging and meal candidate with its own tier, and drops the stored tier and rule on stays and meal stops. A worker aims for what the user's own words in its brief say. For #60: `add_lodging_candidates` and `add_stop_candidates` take a required tier for each lodging or meal candidate, judged by the worker. When the area has nothing that fits the brief, such as upscale lodging in Torrey, the worker offers the closest it finds, labeled with their real tier, and says so in its result, and the coordinator tells the user. **How a worker searches.** `search_near` sends the worker's words to Google as written, ranked by how well places match them, so a search for "restaurant" returns whatever is popular nearby. The stay researcher's instructions say to put words in the query that fit what the brief asks for, such as "fine dining" or "boutique hotel" for upscale, "diner" or "budget motel" for value, or "lobster shack"; to search again with other words when the results don't fit; and, for the area's best, to try web search and look each place up with `find_place`. It reports that nothing fits only after more than one search. A price-level filter and a second page of results stay out for now (tool design 2.3), and can be added if evaluations show workers missing good places.
  - ~~Joe doesn't want to label hotels and restaurants by hand, and doesn't want tiers left wholly to the model's judgment. An evaluation could check consistency instead of right answers: does a restaurant's tier agree with Google's price level where there is one, are a town's posh candidates never at a lower price level than its value ones, and does the same place get the same tier across runs? A user's "Higher tier" or "Lower tier" on a card is also a sign that a tier missed for them.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #185,** an evaluation that checks the stay researcher's tiers for consistency, scored in code: price level, order within a town, and the same tier across runs. The clicks aren't used, since there are too few.
  - ~~Users mean different things by the same tier, so the user's own words may matter more than the tier. Technical spec section 4 says a worker gets the tier and a short rule, "never the rule text." In that trip, the coordinator gave the Camden stay the rule "upscale hotel or B&B in Camden," which says the tier again plus a lodging preference, "B&B," that a stay has nowhere else to hold. Other rules only said the tier again in words, such as "meals upscale or posh." So: should a worker get the user's own words with the tier, and where does a stay's lodging preference, such as a B&B, belong?~~ **Partly settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** a worker gets the user's own words that apply, for budget, meals, and lodging, in place of a tier and a rule. The coordinator can add its own reading where a rule is clear. #184 writes it into technical spec 5.3.
  - ~~Where does a stay's lodging preference belong, such as "a B&B could be a good option in one of them" on the Bar Harbor trip? Today a stay has nowhere to hold it, so the coordinator put it in the tier rule, which #184 removes.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** the trip brief's budget item is replaced by a lodging preferences item, in the user's words, beside meal preferences, and the B&B wish goes there. Spending on food goes in meal preferences. A lodging wish that comes up later in chat goes in trip memory. The coordinator passes the preferences and memory that apply into each worker brief, and keeps track of a wish that covers more than one stay. "Hotels only" includes B&Bs and inns listed on Google. #184 makes the change.
- ~~How are the stay researcher's turns traced in Phoenix? #135 traces only the coordinator, with spans from our own code. By default, the Agent SDK sends the coordinator only a subagent's tool calls and results, not its text or thinking. Whether its stream events come through, with its tokens, needs checking ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 3). Raised on 2026-10-25, while writing #135.~~ Moved to #136 on 2026-10-25.
- ~~How do the workers get `search_near` and `search_along_leg`? #59 added both tools, but put them on no MCP server. The coordinator's places server (`createPlacesServer()` in `src/tools/places-server.ts`) holds only `find_place` and `read_place`, so the coordinator doesn't see the searches. The SDK's subagents share the main query's MCP servers unless an `AgentDefinition` gives its own `mcpServers`, and the coordinator's `allowedTools` likely only refuses a call to a tool it sees, rather than hiding it (not checked). So the stay researcher likely needs its own places server, with `find_place` and `search_near`, and the leg scout (#61) one with `search_along_leg` too. Raised on 2026-10-26, in PR #159. #182 checks a worker's own server, and which tools the coordinator sees.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #191.**
- ~~What do the stay researcher's instructions say about each field the candidate tools take? Their input descriptions give only the format (tool design section 4), so what each means goes in the instructions: `howFound`, which is "google" for a place found with `search_near`, and "webSearch" for one found by web search and then looked up with `find_place`; `sourceLink`, the place's Google Maps link from the search result, or the web page's link; the rationale, one or two sentences on why the place fits, never naming the trip's dates (technical spec 6.4); `notes`, given as "" when there are none; and `visitTimeInMinutes`, the worker's own estimate. #199 built the tools, and tool design 2.1 has what they take. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #199 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** the instructions say this about each field:
  - **`howFound` and `sourceLink` go together.** "google" goes with the place's Google Maps link, the first link on its "Links:" line in the search result. "webSearch" goes with the page's link, when a web page is what led the worker to the place, which it then looked up with `find_place`. When a place turned up both ways, the web page wins, since the option card links to it, and a page such as Atlas Obscura's tells the user more than a Maps pin.
  - **The rationale** is one or two sentences on why this place fits this stop, tied to the user's words in the worker brief, such as "Walkable to the barbecue spots." It doesn't repeat what the card already shows, such as the rating, price level, or tier. It never names the trip's dates or nights.
  - **Notes** are practical things to know before going, such as "closed Mondays", "reservations advised", or "cash only", or "" when there are none. A clash with the trip's dates, such as "closed Wednesdays, and Day 4 is a Wednesday", goes in `report_result` as a problem, not in the notes.
  - **`visitTimeInMinutes`** is the worker's estimate of the time spent at the place, not the drive there, sized to what the user cares about. A hiker at Arches' Windows section might get 90, and a quick look 30. The day's schedule is built from it, so a realistic time beats a short one. No data source gives a visit time, so it stays the model's own judgment, and gets tuned once we see how it works.

  The leg scout (#61) takes the same fields, so this is one block of instruction text it can reuse word for word. The domain model's rationale example, "Walkable to the barbecue spots, fits mid-range.", drops "fits mid-range", since that repeats the tier.
- ~~**What do the workers' instructions say a problem and a question are, for `report_result`?** Tool design 2.6 says a problem is something the coordinator should know, and a question needs the user's decision, since a worker can't ask the user anything. #198 left that out of the tool's description, since what an item means goes in the instructions (tool design section 4). Proposed: one block of instruction text, with the examples from tool design 2.6, that the leg scout (#61) and the weather worker (#64) reuse word for word. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28, in #60's PR:** one block of instruction text, `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`, that every worker's instructions include word for word. A problem is something the coordinator should know that it can't tell from what the worker saved, such as a closure on the trip's dates, fewer than three places that fit, or nothing at the tier the worker brief asked for. A question needs the user's decision, and the worker asks one only when it can't do an item well without the answer. Each is a short sentence that names stops and stays as the tools do. The worker doesn't list what it saved, or say that all went well, and gives empty lists when there's nothing to report. Technical spec 6.4 has the text.

## Do

- Add the stay researcher's instructions.
- Write what the instructions say about each candidate field (the settled question above) as one block that the leg scout (#61) can reuse word for word. Change the domain model's rationale example to "Walkable to the barbecue spots." wherever it appears in `design/`.
- Give the stay researcher a definition as technical spec 6.5 says, with the type `stay-researcher` and its tools from tool design section 3. Add its view file, and list its type's description and tools in the coordinator's view (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).
- Draft the worker brief's outline (technical spec 5.3), for Joe to review in the PR. #198 drafts the result's wording.
- Give the coordinator `Agent(stay-researcher)`, so the stay researcher is the only agent type it can start (technical spec 6.5).
- Add the coordinator's instructions for the fill round. They include what each worker brief carries from the user's meal and lodging preferences, interests, and memory, and how the coordinator keeps track of a wish that covers more than one stay (technical spec 5.3 and section 9). #184 wrote those into the design, but left them out of the prompt, since there were no workers yet.
- Add the sentence from technical spec 5.2's bullet on a stay that moves to a different town that needs workers, which #55 left out. It goes after the hotel sentence that #56 adds to the "Changes to stays" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`. Word for word: "Then send workers for any lodging or stop whose candidates no longer fit."

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- On the Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2), with lodging preferences that ask for a comfortable mid-range hotel, the stay researcher adds three lodging candidates that fit, each labeled with its tier, and fills the stops near the Moab stay.
- The coordinator sees one line per candidate, not full records.
- The coordinator's `Agent` tool offers the stay researcher and no other agent type.
- ~~The answer to the resume question above is checked, and written into persistence design section 7.~~ Done in #191.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-27-the-stay-researcher).
title: The stay researcher

body:
**Starts** once #60 is merged. #59, #197, #198, and #199 are its other needs, and #60 waits for them too.

The leg scout's code doesn't need the stay researcher's. It waits for #60 because both workers share the coordinator's side: #60 writes the fill-round instructions, the worker brief outline, and the text on each candidate field, and the leg scout uses all three. Built at the same time, both PRs would write those, and Joe would review two versions of each. Waiting also lets what the first worker shows feed the second. And the last "Done when" item needs both workers.

## Why

The leg scout fills the stops along a day's drive, such as lunch on the way or a viewpoint, with candidates and their detour times (technical spec 6.2). It's the second worker. During the fill round, it runs at the same time as the stay researchers, all saving to the same trip.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 6.2 and 6.5 (how a worker is started, its brief, its result, and the hooks and settings).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (detour times and `read_worker_brief_facts`), 2.6 (`report_result`), 3, and 4.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.7.

## Open questions

- ~~What timeout does each Google call get, and what time limit does the whole write get? One write can make several calls, such as selecting Moab lodging, which re-routes four days. Measure real writes first.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** keep the 10-second timeout each Google call already has (`TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS` in `src/google/routes-client.ts` and `src/google/places-client.ts`), add no time limit for the whole write, and keep the lock wait at 5 seconds and 3 tries (persistence design section 4). Real writes were measured against Google and the local Postgres. Only Routes calls run while a write holds the trip's lock. `LegsService.updateLegs()` re-routes the days in parallel, and a write is at most 3 calls deep: a route, the best-order check, and one more route. Selecting Moab lodging (Days 1, 2, and 4, 6 or 7 calls) held the lock 0.3 seconds at most, and only about 14 ms of that was the app and the database. A leg scout's `add_stop_candidates` with 3 detour times held it about 0.1 seconds. The slowest single Routes call was 0.26 seconds. A leg scout and two stay researchers writing to one trip at once waited 0.2 seconds at most for the lock, and nothing was refused. A whole-write limit isn't needed, since 3 calls deep at 10 seconds each already caps a write's Google time at 30 seconds, and the limit would need a cancel signal passed through the route code. It's now a point under "Do".

## Do

- Add the leg scout and its instructions. Use #60's text on each candidate field, and on problems and questions, word for word: `CANDIDATE_FIELDS` and `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`. Its instructions name the worker brief's headings from `WORKER_BRIEF_HEADING` in the same file. The leg scout gets no `WebFetch`, so a place it finds on Atlas Obscura takes the page's link from the search result. #199 already built the detour times in `add_stop_candidates`.
- Extend the coordinator's fill-round instructions and the worker brief outline from #60 to cover the leg scout's worker brief. Replace the last point of the "Workers" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, which #60 added while there was no leg scout: "Stops along a leg, or near the start or end place, have no worker yet. Leave them empty, and tell the user they can name a place for one." Drop the sentence about it from technical spec 5.2's bullet on when to send work to a worker too.
- Give the leg scout a definition as technical spec 6.5 says, with its tools from tool design section 3, and add `leg-scout` to the coordinator's `Agent(...)` entry. #198 already puts `search_along_leg` on the `places` server, hidden from the coordinator.
- Add a model setting and an effort setting for the leg scout, like the stay researcher's, and pass both into its definition. Each agent has its own, so one agent's model or effort can change and be evaluated alone. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat, in place of #208. Both start as the stay researcher's do: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `medium`. It does the same kind of work as the stay researcher: it judges tiers and fits places to the user's words, and several run at once in the fill round. Add the two rows to technical spec section 10, as "Leg scout model" and "Leg scout effort". Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.
- Add the hook that denies a leg scout's web search unless it's limited to `atlasobscura.com`.
- In persistence design section 4, change both places that say a write holds the lock "a few seconds at most" (in "The cost is waiting" and "A write waits 5 seconds for the lock") to say it holds it well under a second: 0.3 seconds at most, when real writes were measured on 2026-10-28 (the settled question above). Leave the timeouts and the lock wait as they are.
- Say in the leg scout's instructions that nobody reads its own messages, and that the coordinator gets only what its tool calls saved and what it passes to `report_result`. The stay researcher's instructions say this in their "Your work, in order" section (`src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts`). Claude Code adds a note to every worker's system prompt that pulls the other way: "Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create." Settled in #194.

## Done when

- The leg scout for San Francisco Day 2 (domain model, section 5.1) fills Point Lobos, Bixby Creek, and lunch with candidates that have detour times.
- A test shows the hook denies a leg scout's search with no domain limit.
- Two stay researchers and a leg scout run at once, and none loses another's candidates.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-28-the-leg-scout).
title: The leg scout

body:
**Starts** once #60 and #57 are merged.

## Why

Option cards let the user choose among a stop's or stay's candidates with a click, instead of only in chat (functional spec 7.5). The card actions also ask for more options or a different budget tier.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 7.1, 7.5, and 7.6.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (refine), 7.2, and 9.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.9.

## Open questions

- ~~Which attractions show a rating and review count? A national park or a historic plaque shows none (functional spec 7.5).~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** every place shows its rating and review count when Google has one, attractions included, and nothing when it has none. Hiding them would take a list of Google place types, such as `national_park` and `historical_landmark`, and Google has dozens of attraction types, with edge cases such as a state park or a scenic overlook. A rating on a park does no harm, and the review count shows when a rating is thin, such as "5.0 stars, 3 reviews". Write it into functional spec 7.5, in place of "Attractions show them only where a rating means something…", and into Google design 2.2's "Rating and review count" row.
- ~~Do Google's terms require the "Summarized with Gemini" label wherever a Places summary appears?~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** no label, since the app never shows a Places summary to the user. Summaries go only to the workers, in search results, and the card shows the worker's own rationale and notes (functional spec 7.5). Google's [Places API policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/policies) apply when a summary is shown: its full text, unchanged, with Google's disclosure text just below it, an "About this summary" link, and a "Report summary" link. A review summary also needs a "Review summary" heading and a "See reviews" link. Write into Google design 2.2 that any screen that ever shows a Places summary follows those rules.

  The same page has two rules that do apply to the cards, since they show Google's name, type, rating, and review count away from the Google map. Places data shown without a Google map needs Google Maps attribution, the Google Maps logo, or the text "Google Maps" where space is short, always visible and never changed. Google says to put it "near the top or bottom of the content, and within the same visual container", so a page footer doesn't count, but one logo can cover every card in one panel. A card that stands alone, such as one in the chat, needs its own. And Google's content, such as the rating, must be set apart from ours, such as the rationale. Write both rules into Google design 2.2, not a fixed layout, since the layout may change in #204.

## Do

- Show an option card for the newest candidate set of each stop and stay with nothing selected, with each candidate's details. Select, More options, Higher tier, and Lower tier each send a message to the coordinator.
- Show no card for new options on a stop or stay that already has a pick. Functional spec 7.5 says one opens, and goes away on a reload. That's fiddly screen code: the browser would have to notice the new set and forget it on a reload. A rule on saved data, such as "the newest set is newer than the pick's", would come back after a reload, and stay open when the user picks from an older set in chat. Instead, the coordinator names the new options in chat, and the user picks there. Change functional spec 7.5 to match. Add a line to the coordinator's instructions: when the stop or stay already has a pick, there's no card, so name the new options in chat, and say which one you'd recommend. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat, as a start: how the cards look isn't settled yet, so it may change once they're built.
- Show one Google Maps attribution in each container that shows option cards, and set Google's content, such as the rating, apart from ours, such as the rationale (Google design 2.2, from the settled question above).
- Add the coordinator's instructions for card actions. "Higher tier" and "Lower tier" are requests, such as "something nicer than these", sent to a worker. Nothing is stored (technical spec section 9).
- Fix technical spec section 9's "Higher tier" and "Lower tier" bullet to match 5.2: sending a worker for them takes no read, since the worker reads the candidates already offered itself, with `read_worker_brief_facts` (#191). Section 9 still says "The coordinator reads the stop or stay, and sends a worker." Changed on 2026-10-28, in place of an older item from #129 that asked for the read.
- Add the end of technical spec 5.2's bullet "When the user turns down a place", which #56 left out since it needs option cards and workers. #56's "Rejecting places" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` has a first bullet that ends "whether or not it's selected." Add after it, word for word: "The card then shows what's left, so a worker is needed only when no candidates are left or the user asks for more options." Added on 2026-10-26, from #56.

## Done when

On the deployed site (systems design, section 7), on the Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2):

- Each stop and stay with candidates and nothing selected shows a card with its newest set. Each option shows its tier where it has one, and its rating and review count where Google has one. No option shows a price.
- "Higher tier" is hidden on a card where every option is upscale, and "Lower tier" on one where every option is value.
- Each container with cards shows the Google Maps attribution.
- "Higher tier" then Select updates the itinerary, and the coordinator confirms in chat (functional spec 11, S6).

What the workers pick for S5 (functional spec 11) is checked in #60, and the whole scenario in #69. Changed on 2026-10-28, since #184 made tiers labels and dropped the budget rule.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-29-option-cards).

Before 7 a.m. local time, the first day is yesterday. The client asks for 10 days and picks each date by its `displayDate`. Written into Google design section 3.
- ~~Should the tool's name start with a verb, as the other tools' names do?~~ Settled 2026-10-21 in chat: yes, `look_up_stay_weather`. Not `get_stay_weather`, since next to `set_stay_weather` it would read as getting the saved text. Written into tool design 2.5 and section 3.

title: Weather data

body:
**Starts** once #60 and #57 are merged.

## Why

The weather worker writes each stay's weather and what to wear, from a forecast or from seasonal averages (technical spec 6.3, functional spec 8). It's the last worker.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 1 (agent types), 4.2 (weather and clothing), 5.2, 5.3 (the weather worker's worker brief), 6.3, and 6.5 (how a worker is started, its result, and the hooks).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`set_stay_weather` and `read_worker_brief_facts`), 2.5 (`look_up_stay_weather`), 2.6 (`report_result`), and 3.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 8 and 9.6.

## Open questions

- ~~**How does the weather worker tell that an activity is far from the stay's town?** `look_up_stay_weather` takes either the stay's town or an attraction far from it, such as Tuolumne Meadows on a Yosemite stay (tool design 2.5). `read_worker_brief_facts` gives each activity's place with its short line (technical spec 7.2), and the short line's town is the worker's best clue. But the short line has no town when Google's address has none, as for "Delicate Arch Trail, Utah, USA" (`Place.town` in `src/domain/place.ts`). Park attractions, the ones most likely to be far away, often have no town. Raised on 2026-10-28, from a review note on #201.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** code adds the distance, and the worker judges. Each activity line from `read_worker_brief_facts` adds how far its place is from the stay's town, as the crow flies, such as "about 18 miles from Yosemite Valley". Both places' coordinates are stored, and `milesBetween()` in `src/tools/search-result-lines.ts` works it out. An activity with no place yet gets no distance. The weather worker's instructions say to look up an activity's own weather when its weather could differ from the town's: by height, such as Tuolumne Meadows at about 8,600 feet against about 4,000 in Yosemite Valley, or by a local climate, such as the coast against inland. The distance tells the worker where the place is when its name and address don't. The model knows the height and local climate of well-known places. Two choices were left out. A distance limit in code would be wrong both ways, since height and local climate matter more than distance, and it's a fiddly rule. Looking up every activity makes many calls that mostly repeat the town's weather, and takes away the judgment worth watching in a trace. This leans on the model's judgment, local climates most of all. Whether that gives good results is to be seen in traces, and tuned only if it's a problem.
- ~~**What does `set_stay_weather` call its stay ID input?** #198's hooks record each `mcp__trip__set_stay_weather` call, and read the stay it saved from the input's `stayId`, the name `add_lodging_candidates` uses (`src/agent/worker-calls.ts`). The result lists the stays the weather worker read but saved nothing for, so a different name would list every stay as missing. Proposed: name it `stayId`, as the other tools do. If it's named otherwise, change the hook's schema in the same PR. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** `stayId`. It was never really open: #198's hook already reads that name, and every other tool that takes a stay uses it. It's now a point under "Do".
- ~~**How does the `weather` server get into the session?** `createWeatherServer()` exists (`src/tools/weather-server.ts`), but the query's `mcpServers` doesn't hold it yet, so no agent can be sent `look_up_stay_weather`. #198 left it out, since no agent used it yet. Proposed: add it to the query's `mcpServers`, and `mcp__weather` to `allowedTools`, with its access in `CoordinatorGiven` and `coordinatorAccessFor()`, as the other servers are. Technical spec 6.5 says every server is in the session, and the definitions pick who gets each tool. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** as proposed. Technical spec 6.5 already says so, and only the weather worker's definition lists `look_up_stay_weather` (tool design section 3), so the coordinator doesn't get it. It's now a point under "Do".

## Do

- Add `set_stay_weather`, the weather worker, and its instructions. Its instructions include #60's text on problems and questions word for word: `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts` (technical spec 6.4).
- Name `set_stay_weather`'s stay input `stayId`, as the other stay tools do. #198's hook in `src/agent/worker-calls.ts` reads the saved stay by that name.
- Add the `weather` server to the query's `mcpServers` and `mcp__weather` to `allowedTools`, and build its access in `CoordinatorGiven` and `coordinatorAccessFor()`, as the other servers are. Only the weather worker's definition lists `look_up_stay_weather` (tool design section 3).
- Add each activity's distance from the stay's town to its line in `read_worker_brief_facts`, and to the tool's description, and write it into tool design 2.1 and 2.5 (the settled question above). Drop the comment in `src/tools/activity-lines.ts` that says #64 settles how the worker tells.
- Give the weather worker a definition as technical spec 6.5 says, with the type `weather-worker` and its tools from tool design section 3, and add `weather-worker` to the coordinator's `Agent(...)` entry. Its worker brief holds only stay IDs, and it calls `read_worker_brief_facts` first, as the other workers do.
- Write the weather worker's worker brief as the "Fill:" heading (`WORKER_BRIEF_HEADING.fill` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`), with one stay ID per line, and no other heading. Add a line to the "Worker briefs" section of `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` that says so, since that section says every worker brief has every heading. The weather worker's instructions name only that heading. Write it into technical spec 5.3. The other headings are always there so a stay researcher or leg scout never wonders whether one was left out, and the weather worker uses none of them. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.
- Add a model setting and an effort setting for the weather worker, like the stay researcher's, and pass both into its definition. Each agent has its own, so one agent's model or effort can change and be evaluated alone. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat, in place of #208. Both start as the stay researcher's do: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `medium`. Its text is short, but it leans on the model knowing the height and local climate of places, such as Tuolumne Meadows against Yosemite Valley, which a smaller model is weaker at. It can be tried on a smaller model later, with an evaluation. Add the two rows to technical spec section 10, as "Weather worker model" and "Weather worker effort". Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.
- Add the coordinator's rules for when to run and rerun it. One is in the session-start bullet of technical spec 5.2: when the full read at the start of a session shows a stay whose seasonal averages could now be a forecast, offer to rerun the weather worker for it. #54 left this out of the instructions, since the worker didn't exist yet.
- Show each stay's weather and clothing text in the itinerary view, with its label, an out-of-date mark, and its credit: the Open-Meteo credit on seasonal averages (Open-Meteo design section 4), and "Includes data from Google Maps" on a forecast. Put each at the bottom of that stay's weather block. Google's [Weather API policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/weather/policies) give that text for "entirely new content" made from the data, and the worker's text is its own reading of the forecast. The credit goes "near the top or bottom of the content, and within the same visual container", always visible, and never changed. Write the rule into Google design section 3, with the link. #62 adds a Google Maps credit to the option cards, so whichever merges second reuses the first one's. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat.

## Done when

- The Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2) gets weather and clothing text for both stays, and Torrey's covers freezing-night stargazing.
- Moving the trip one day later doesn't mark seasonal averages out of date.
- Adding a stay marks it out of date.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-31-the-weather-worker).
title: The weather worker

body:
## Why

Each earlier issue added the coordinator's instructions for its own tools. Nobody had checked the whole prompt against the spec since. A gap check on 2026-11-04 did that: an agent compared technical spec sections 4.1, 4.2, 5.2, and 9 with the coordinator's view file (`src/agent/coordinator.view.md`). Of about 70 things the spec says the coordinator does, 64 were covered. This issue fixes the gaps it found, and three found earlier, so the recorded trips (#66, #67, #68) don't run into problems we already know about.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 and 5.2.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 1 and 2: the contiguous United States.

## Open questions

- ~~Are about two dozen tools too many for the coordinator? If it chooses badly, merge the add, update, and remove tools for each kind of item.~~ Moved to #53 on 2026-11-04, as the "tool use" general evaluator. Only recorded sessions can show whether the coordinator picks badly.
- ~~Do the instructions say clearly enough what the trip tools' "new or gone" check results mean? Today the prompt says only that each tool "replies with the feasibility check results the change made new or gone, anywhere in the trip." A tool reply then says, for example, "No new or gone check results." "Gone" means a result that was there before the change and isn't after it, such as a warning the change fixed, or one about a stop the change removed. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking the raw view from #125.~~ Moved to #252 on 2026-11-04. The fix changes how a write's reply is laid out, which is code, not only the instructions.
- ~~Should the instructions tell the coordinator not to describe its own steps to the user? On a new trip, its reply began "I need to read brief and memory first." That's a note to itself, written as reply text before its tool calls, so the user sees it as the reply's first line. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking #123.~~ Settled 2026-11-04 in chat: yes, it's in "Do". #53 also gets a general evaluator, "the reply is for the user", to show whether it still happens.
- ~~Does the "changed" mark on check results (#55) come back too often to be useful? A check result is changed when its text differs from the saved one (domain model 4.8). A daily driving warning's text names its day, such as "Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." So adding or removing a stay before that day renumbers it, and the warning comes back changed, though nothing about it got worse. In #55's Moab chat on 2026-10-24, adding the Moab stay gave "Changed warning: The trip is 4 days, and the brief asks for 5" and "Changed warning: Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." The coordinator stayed quiet about both, since the skeleton wasn't finished. If later runs show it raising renumbered warnings, compare the results without the day number, or leave the day number out of the text.~~ Dropped 2026-11-04 in chat. Nothing has shown it to be a problem. In the one chat that saw it, the coordinator stayed quiet.
- ~~Should the instructions say the app plans trips only in the contiguous United States? Functional spec sections 1 and 2 say so, and list Canada as out of scope, but neither the coordinator's instructions nor technical spec 5.2 says it. So going through 5.2 alone won't catch it. In Joe's session on the live site on 2026-10-28 (agent session `0f63f3da-4112-4943-93ec-af8fe6576296`), the coordinator offered to plan the Niagara stay on the Canadian side, and added a stay in Niagara Falls, Ontario. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-28.~~ Settled 2026-11-04 in chat: yes, it's in "Do".

## Do

Add each of these to the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and the files next to it), in the section it fits:

- **"What's left to decide?"** How to answer it, from technical spec 5.2: a whole read and trip memory, then the stops and lodging still empty or proposed, the open warnings, and the open items in trip memory. Mention approved exceptions briefly. Nothing in the instructions covers it today.
- **The contiguous United States only.** The app plans trips only there, as functional spec sections 1 and 2 say. Don't offer, or add, a stay or stop outside it, such as Niagara Falls, Ontario.
- **Replies are for the user.** Don't write notes to yourself as reply text, such as "I need to read brief and memory first."
- **A standing preference also goes to user memory,** even when the trip brief holds it for this trip. Technical spec 5.2, "Writing memory", has the rule and its example: "we never drive more than 5 hours, on any trip" sets comfortable driving hours, and is saved to user memory too. Today the Memory section has only the trip memory half of the rule: don't save to trip memory what the trip brief or the itinerary holds.
- **Stops the user chose decide their own part of the road.** If they're inland, the leg runs inland there, and the coordinator doesn't question it (technical spec 4.2, "The route preference is for the stretches nobody has decided"). The instructions cover only the waypoints half.
- **A stop whose purpose says how long:** when telling the user what it pushes later in the day, use the same rough timing as the worker brief (technical spec 5.2). Today the instructions don't tie the two together, so they could differ.

Also:

- Fix technical spec 4.2's step 4, "Fill". It says a stay researcher goes to a stay with "lodging not yet selected". Section 5.2, and the instructions, send one only for lodging with no candidates yet. 5.2 is right: lodging that already has candidates doesn't need another researcher. Change 4.2 to match.
- The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, so the coordinator's view file shows the changes.

## Done when

- The PR description lists each item in "Do", with the part of the instructions that now covers it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-32-finish-the-coordinators-instructions). Reworked on 2026-11-04, after the gap check. The real-agent tests for a new session's opening line and "what's left to decide?" came out. They're evaluations now. #69 covers both, with acceptance scenario S7, "Resume and new session" (functional spec 11).
title: Finish the coordinator's instructions

body:
**Starts** once #251 is merged.

**Joe's setup is done** for the harness this issue uses, Claude Code with Sonnet (2026-11-04). The bot user is `claude-code-sonnet@jjk3.com`, user ID `d37cc40c-3a8f-4ece-ba59-f1309c7b3e39`, from `whoami`. Its account file is `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/claude-code-sonnet.env`. Claude Code's own config folder, `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude/`, is signed in, and its command timeout is raised and checked. So the work needs nothing more from Joe, unless a fix changes the design.

## Why

Agent evaluations (#53) need recorded sessions to score, and planning a whole trip by hand takes a long conversation. A **simulated user** is a coding agent harness, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode, with a chosen model, that plays a user planning a trip. It chats with the app through `npm run live-chat` (#251), the terminal client that does what the browser does. Different harnesses and models play a user a little differently, which gives the evaluations more varied sessions than Joe and his family can make by hand.

This issue sets up how a simulated user works, and shakes it out with one whole trip on the local stack, where traces are throwaway. #67 and #68 then record the first trips on the live site, for the corpus.

**The two Phoenix projects have different jobs here.** `road-trip-agent-local` is for development and tests, and its traces are throwaway. `road-trip-agent`, the server's project, holds the sessions to be evaluated, annotated, and scored (systems design, section 10). So shakedown runs point `live-chat` at the local stack, and recorded trips point it at the live site.

## Design

- [Agent evaluations](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/issues/53), the bullet "How are the evaluations built up?" in its open questions: what a scenario file holds, and how the simulated user should act.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 3 (sign-in) and section 10 (traces).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 5.1: the San Francisco trip.

Terms used here:

- **Harness:** the coding agent program that runs the model, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode.
- **Bot user:** a Supabase user made for one harness and model pair, such as one for Codex with a GPT model. Its email is named harness-model, so it's clear which one it is. Each turn's span in Phoenix has the user's ID (`user.id`), so the bot user tells which harness and model played a session.
- **Trip file:** what the user knows and does on one trip: the facts, what's not decided yet, the changes partway through, and when the trip counts as planned.
- **Persona file:** how the user talks, on any trip, such as curt or impatient. A run pairs one trip file with one persona file, so any persona can play any trip.
- **Run folder:** a folder outside the repo, made for one run of one bot user on one trip with one persona. The harness starts there, and the folder holds only what that run needs.

## Open questions

- ~~Does the simulated user run in the repo, or in a folder outside it? In the repo, it can read the coordinator's prompts, the design docs, and the example trips, so it could know more than a real user would. It could also run other commands, such as against the local database. Outside the repo, it would get only its scenario file and its instructions, plus a short script that runs `npm run live-chat` from the repo. Joe isn't sure it's needed. Raised on 2026-11-04, in chat.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat: outside the repo, in a run folder of its own. Harnesses poke around their working folder, so a folder holding every trip and persona would let a simulated user read the ones it isn't playing. And a folder inside the repo loads the repo's `CLAUDE.md` on its own, since Claude Code reads every `CLAUDE.md` from its folder up. The setup is in Do.
- ~~How does a scenario run that needs a later date, such as "on May 8, 2027, the user opens the trip again"? The live site always uses today's date, and nothing sets it. Until this is settled, scenarios leave such steps out. Raised on 2026-11-04, in chat.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat: the San Francisco and Moab trip files leave out steps tied to a date, and nothing fakes the date. Faking it would take fake weather too, since Google gives forecasts only for the real next 10 days or so. And Claude Code's own date line, from the real clock, would show the coordinator two different dates, which technical spec 5.2 rules out. The forecast offer, which those steps were for, gets a trip of its own that starts for real a few days after the run (#259).

## Do

- Make a `simulated-users/` folder in the repo. It holds:
  - `instructions.md`, what every simulated user gets.
  - `trips/`, one trip file per trip.
  - `personas/`, one persona file per persona.
  - `bot-users.md`, each bot user's ID with its email.
  - `README.md`, how to add a bot user, set up a run, and start each harness. Joe refers to it, so it has to work on its own.
- A trip file holds:
  - the facts the user knows, such as dates, places, budget, and driving limits.
  - things the user hasn't decided yet.
  - changes to make partway through, and when, such as skipping Denver once the first draft is done.
  - when the trip counts as planned, so the simulated user knows when to stop.

  The facts also work as an answer key, to check what the coordinator saved to the trip brief. A persona file holds only how the user talks and acts, with nothing about any one trip.
- Add a setup script that makes a run folder, such as `npm run sim-setup -- codex-gpt-5 moab curt`, for a bot user, a trip, and a persona. It also takes the site, local or live. The folder goes in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/`, named for the three, such as `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/codex-gpt-5-moab-curt/`. It stops if that folder is already there, so an old run's files never mix with a new one. The folder gets:
  - `instructions.md`, and copies of the trip file and the persona file named plainly `trip.md` and `persona.md`, so nothing in the folder hints at other trips.
  - `account.env`, the bot user's email and password from `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, plus `LIVE_CHAT_SITE` for the site. It uses the names `live-chat` already reads: `LIVE_CHAT_SITE`, `LIVE_CHAT_EMAIL`, and `LIVE_CHAT_PASSWORD`.
  - `chat.sh`, which loads `account.env` and runs `npm run live-chat` in the repo, passing its arguments and standard input through. Values set in the shell win over the repo's `.env`, so the bot user's values are the ones used.
- The instructions say how to use `./chat.sh`: starting the trip, sending messages, looking at the option cards and the itinerary, and using the card buttons. They also say how to act: answer only what's asked, give one or two facts at a time, and stick with any answer it makes up. A web user sees the cards and the itinerary beside the chat without asking, so the instructions say to look at them as a user would, such as after a reply says a card is open.
- Write down how to add a harness:
  - Joe makes one bot user per harness and model pair, in the Supabase dashboard (systems design, section 3). Its email and password go in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, outside the repo, so they can't be committed.
  - Keep a list in the repo of each bot user's ID with its email, starting with the bot user above, so a session in Phoenix can be traced to who played it. Phoenix shows only the user's ID. Each line comes from running `npm run live-chat`'s `whoami` as that bot user. No passwords in the list.
  - Each harness starts in the run folder, so it doesn't load the repo's `CLAUDE.md`. Joe's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` still loads for some harnesses, so the README gives each one's start command:
    - Claude Code: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude --model <model>`. Its own config folder keeps out Joe's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, and memory. Joe signs in once in that config folder.
    - Codex: `codex -m <model>`. It reads only `AGENTS.md`, and Joe has none.
    - opencode: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 opencode -m <model>`. opencode falls back to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when it has no `AGENTS.md` of its own.

    Every harness then gets the same opening prompt, such as "Read instructions.md, trip.md, and persona.md, then plan the trip."
  - Check the harness lets a shell command it waits on run at least 5 minutes, since a turn with workers can take about 4. Ask it to run `python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(330)'; echo done` in the foreground, without setting a timeout itself. If it doesn't print "done", raise the harness's command timeout in its settings, and try again. Don't use `sleep` for the check: Claude Code refuses a foreground `sleep`, and runs it in the background, where there's no limit to test. Claude Code cuts a command off after 2 minutes by default. Its config folder's `settings.json` raises that with `"env": { "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000", "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000" }`. Checked on 2026-11-04 with Claude Code 2.1.318.
- Write the San Francisco trip file, from domain model section 5.1, with changes partway through, and one persona file. The trip is planned in one session. A change may start a new session right away, but never on a later day, so leave out changes such as the user opening the trip again on May 8, 2027. Joe decided on 2026-11-04, in chat, that coming back to a trip later isn't tested here. The San Francisco changes in the design walkthroughs' last prompt (`reviews/walkthroughs/prompt-6.md`, section "Changes to make along the way") are a starting point. That prompt is out of date, so check each change still fits the current design.
- Run the whole San Francisco trip with Claude Code and Sonnet against the local stack (`npm run dev`), signed in as its bot user. The implementer starts it, headless, in the run folder: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude -p --model sonnet --allowedTools "Bash(./chat.sh:*)"`, in the background, and reads the session when it ends. Give the opening prompt on standard input, since `--allowedTools` takes a list and would read a prompt after it as one more tool. Allow more tools only if the run shows the simulated user needs them. Fix the problems it finds in the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions. File any app bug as a new issue. A fix that changes the design goes to Joe first.
- In DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, point to `simulated-users/README.md` for how to run a simulated user.

## Done when

- One harness plays the San Francisco trip from start to finish against the local stack, and stops when the trip file says the trip is planned.
- Each problem the run found is fixed, or filed as an issue.
- A new harness can be added, and a run set up and started, from `simulated-users/README.md`, with no other help.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-33-the-simulated-user). Reworked on 2026-11-04: the simulated user moved from a script that runs Claude as the user to any harness and model, through `npm run live-chat`. The report comparing the final itinerary with domain model section 5 came out, since #67 and #68 no longer check that. Later on 2026-11-04: the scenario file split into a trip file and a persona file, and each run got its own folder outside the repo.
title: The simulated user

body:
**Starts** once #66 is merged.

## Why

This is the first trip a simulated user (#66) plans on the live site. It does two things. It checks that the simulated user works well enough to record sessions for the corpus. And it leaves a whole planned trip in the server's Phoenix project, `road-trip-agent`, for agent evaluations (#53) to score.

The final itinerary isn't checked against domain model section 5.1. Places come from live Google results and from the workers' picks, so two good runs can pick two different motels. What's checked is how the simulated user behaved, and what the coordinator saved to the trip brief.

## Design

- [Simulated users README](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/simulated-users/README.md): how to set up, start, and check a run. Its sections "Set up a run", "Start a harness", and "Check a run" cover this issue.
- [The simulated user](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/issues/66): the San Francisco trip file, `simulated-users/trips/san-francisco.md`.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 5.1: the San Francisco trip.

## Open questions

- ~~How much of the Claude Max plan (systems design, section 5) does a planning session use? Check the plan's usage bars in Claude's settings before and after the run. For a rough size, #66's local runs of this trip took 30 to 36 of the simulated user's messages, and 10 to 17 minutes.~~ Settled on 2026-11-04 in chat: not measured. Joe found that the local test sessions each used very little of the plan, and this run plays on Sonnet, which uses less.

## Do

- Run the San Francisco trip file with Claude Code and Sonnet, as the bot user `claude-code-sonnet`, with the `easygoing` persona, on the live site (`https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`). Set it up and start it headless, as the README says. First remove `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/claude-code-sonnet-san-francisco-easygoing/`, left from #66's local runs, since `npm run sim-setup` stops while it's there.
- Check the session as the README's "Check a run" says. There are three checks: the simulated user stuck to the trip file, it acted like a user, and the trip brief matches the trip file's facts. The README also says where to read the final trip brief, and which differences between runs are fine.
- If the session fails a check because of the setup, fix the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions, and run again. Mark the failed run in Phoenix, as the README says.
- File each app bug the run finds as a new issue. Don't fix it here.

## Done when

- A simulated session of the San Francisco trip is in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project.
- The simulated session passes the three checks above, and the results are in the PR.
- The app bugs found are filed as issues.

## Ends in

A PR, with any changes to the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-34-walk-the-san-francisco-trip). Reworked on 2026-11-04, from walking the trip to match domain model section 5.1, to recording it for the corpus.

nodes.body:
## Results

**The session is in Phoenix.** One run, on 2026-11-04 from 19:59 to 20:12 UTC, about 13 minutes. Trip `trip_mfvyzu8x`, with two app sessions, `session_x684eqc8` and `session_3rberk77`. In the `road-trip-agent` project they're the Phoenix sessions `6a5a3840-2911-46d0-8579-aae28f06961b` (22 turns) and `aa5d567a-ce94-4333-8c68-9307e17c9b33` (2 turns). Every `coordinator.turn` span has `user.id` `d37cc40c-3a8f-4ece-ba59-f1309c7b3e39`, which is `claude-code-sonnet` in `bot-users.md`. The simulated user used 33 messages and about $0.42. Another user was planning a trip on the live site at the same time. Their turns are in their own traces, and neither session showed the other's trip.

**It stuck to the trip file: passed.** Every fact it gave matches the trip file. Where the trip file had no answer, it made up ones that fit: Sunday works for Mike, and a bit more for a Big Sur hotel is fine. All seven changes were made, in order, at the points the trip file says. The Sardine Factory couldn't come back, since a rejection can't be taken back (functional spec section 2), so it kept The Whaling Station, as the trip file says.

**It acted like a user: passed, with three small slips.**

- It held back one must-see. Asked for must-sees, it gave three, and brought up the Madonna Inn cake later, as a dessert stop.
- It tried a pipe once (`./chat.sh cards ... | sed ...`). The permission check refused it, and it ran `./chat.sh cards` alone.
- On "Take the second one," the planner took Garden Street Inn, the second hotel in its own list. The simulated user meant the second on the card, Petit Soleil. It said Garden Street "was the third one in your list," which was true of the card but not the list, and the planner switched. Its final note calls this the planner's mistake, but both readings are fine.

**The trip brief matches the trip file's facts: passed.** From the last `mcp__trip__read_trip_brief` span, at 20:12:10 UTC, on the new session's first turn:

| Trip file | Brief |
|---|---|
| Highway 1, San Francisco to Los Angeles | focus: California coast, San Francisco to Los Angeles |
| 3 days (went to 4 and back) | tripLengthInDays: 3 |
| coast views, aviation, good food | interestsText: coast views, seafood and tri-tip, old planes |
| Boardwalk, Bixby, elephant seals, Madonna Inn cake | mustSeesText: Boardwalk, Bixby, elephant seals |
| about 4 hours a day | comfortableDrivingInHours: 4 |
| scenic | routePreference: scenic |
| 8 a.m. | usualStartTime: 8:00 a.m. |
| local café breakfasts, casual lunches, nicer dinners | mealPreferencesText: the same |
| mid-range | lodgingPreferencesText: mid range hotels |

The cake isn't in `mustSeesText`, since the user didn't give it as a must-see, but it's a stop on Day 2. The rest is in the itinerary: May 13, 2027, San Francisco to Mike's place in Silver Lake, and the fastest route on Day 3.

**App bugs filed:** one, #265, `live-chat` printing a picked place's reason and source on one line. The run also showed the stay researcher's candidate calls refused 7 times. That's agent behavior, not an app bug, so it's in its own Triage issue, #266.

**Checked by hand:** the run's log, every message the simulated user sent, and the spans above, read from the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project through the SSH tunnel. `npm run check` passes.
Done. The run passed all three checks, and the results are in the comment above. No changes to the setup were needed, so there's no PR.

nodes.body:
## Results: Moab trip, `curt` persona, Claude Code with Sonnet

The run passes every check. It played on the live site as `claude-code-sonnet`, on 2026-11-04 from 22:13 to 22:27 UTC. The simulated user took 42 turns and cost $0.54.

**IDs**

- Trip: `trip_msv3pfby`
- Session 1: `session_36mqyhky`, Phoenix session `7f9743d3-b36d-477a-a1f2-b605daedbf4d` (30 turns)
- Session 2: `session_kereu595`, Phoenix session `0d815c58-00a1-4728-8979-c5552b9cb146` (3 turns)

The trip ended as 4 days, Monday October 11 to Thursday October 14, 2027. It has 2 nights at Hampton Inn Moab and 1 night at Motel Torrey.

### Checks

**It stuck to the trip file: pass.** No fact contradicts the trip file. Every place the user already wanted made it into the plan: Fisher Towers, Moab Brewery at 6, the Windows, Love Muffin, Milt's at noon, Corona Arch, Desert Bistro at 7, the rest day with The Spoke at 6:30, Gifford Homestead, and Capitol Gorge. It asked the planner to suggest the Grand Junction breakfast, and picked Dream Cafe. Comfortable driving (4 hours) and the 8 a.m. start were never given by the user. The coordinator took the 4 hours from the user memory left by the San Francisco run, and 8 a.m. is the default. Both match the trip file.

**It acted like a user, as its persona says: pass, with slips.** Most messages were a few lowercase words. Its first reply to the three route sketches was "too long. none of those." It made the changes at the right points:

- Changes 1 and 2 (Milt's, the pie): skipped. The planner never said Milt's or Gifford Homestead was closed. Gifford was planned for 2:54, and it closes at 4:30.
- Change 3 (a longer day): it agreed to about 5 hours on the Moab to Torrey day. Picking Panorama Point for stargazing pushed it to 5½ hours, and it agreed again.
- Change 4 (a day later): made right after the weather and packing advice appeared.
- Change 5 (one night less): it cut Moab to 2 nights and asked for the 5-hour Arches hike. It then dropped the rest day and its meals, and took Devils Garden after the sunrise hike. The Windows and Love Muffin went to make room.
- Change 6 (new session): it asked "why did we pick that moab hotel?", then what's left to decide. It settled what the planner raised, and thanked it.

Slips:

- Its fourth message gave six facts at once: "mid-range in moab, cheap in torrey. day 2 starts 5:30am, delicate arch sunrise. yes rest in torrey. day 5 start at 10. also goblin valley on the way to torrey". Four answered the planner's questions. The Delicate Arch sunrise and Goblin Valley weren't asked in that turn, though the first turn had asked for must-sees.
- It tried to pipe `./chat.sh itinerary` through `sed`. The harness refused it, and it ran the plain command instead.
- Its final note calls the long drive "Day 4's". After change 5 it's Day 3.

**The trip brief matches the trip file's facts: pass.** The last brief, read at the start of session 2:

```
focus: red rock parks of Utah
tripLengthInDays: 4
interestsText: red rock parks, hiking, dark skies
mustSeesText: Arches, dark skies
comfortableDrivingInHours: 4
routePreference: scenic
usualStartTime: 8:00 a.m.
mealPreferencesText: casual local food, good breakfasts
lodgingPreferencesText: mid-range in moab, cheap in torrey
```

The start, end, and start date are in the itinerary: Grand Junction to Salt Lake City, from October 11. The trip file's must-sees aren't in `mustSeesText`. That's because of how the user gave them. It never answered the first turn's must-see question. It later gave the Delicate Arch sunrise, Goblin Valley, and the 1 a.m. stargazing as plans for a day, and the coordinator added each as a stop. Capitol Reef came in only as Capitol Gorge and the pie. All of them are in the final itinerary.

### Refused tool calls

There were 2, both `add_stop_candidates` calls for a meal stop that sent `visitTimeInMinutes`. One came from the stay researcher and one from the leg scout. Both fixed the call and went on. I added them to the refusal issue, "The stay researcher sends keys its candidate tools refuse" (#266), since they show the leg scout does it too.

### Issues filed

None. The run found no app bugs.

### Worth knowing for the evaluations

- **Stale trip memory.** At change 5, the coordinator updated its note about the moon, but not its note that said "3 nights in Moab". In session 2 it read that note, saw it didn't match the itinerary, and asked the user. The user said to fix it, and it did.
- **The moon.** In the first session, the coordinator said the nearly full moon would set around 1 to 3 a.m. After the date change, it corrected itself, and said the moon would still be up at 1 a.m. The user kept the plan.
- **A stop that kept an old length.** Capitol Gorge took the place of the "hike in Capitol Reef, about 3 hours" stop, but with a 2-hour visit. The coordinator raised that in session 2, and the user kept 2 hours.
- **A question already answered.** After change 5, the coordinator asked whether to keep Corona Arch, though the user had just said to keep it.

Codex's run of the same trip and persona, "Record the Moab trip with Codex" (#276), has no results yet. So that issue will compare the two harnesses.

Design the fix loop that runs after the CI review. When a review has findings marked "fix", another Claude Code run in CI fixes them and pushes, and the push starts the next review. After three fix rounds, a fourth review runs, and the PR goes to Joe with a "ready for Joe" label.

PR #39 showed the loop needs two limits: a rule for which findings get fixed, and a cap on rounds. It went seven rounds without either, and most of its 36 findings were minor (`research/code-review-evaluation.md`, section 10).

The work to build it is split into #75 (the review agent), #76 (the fix agent), and #77 (the loop).

## Design

- The code review design, `design/code-review.md`, is on the branch `code-review-design`. Section 3 holds the rules for which findings get fixed. Section 4 holds the loop's design, agreed in chat on 2026-10-19.

## Open questions

- ~~Is the code review design finished and merged first, in its own PR, before the loop is built?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes. This issue's PR merges before #75 starts.
- ~~Do the loop's open questions stay in the design doc's section 4.5, or move into this issue?~~ Settled 2026-10-19: they moved here, since CLAUDE.md puts a question an open issue will answer in that issue.

- ~~Does the fixer read the decisions comment?~~ Moved to #76.

- ~~Should "the PR doesn't do what its task says" be a rule in the bar (design section 3.1)?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes (design section 3.1).

- ~~Does a push by Joe reset the count of fix rounds?~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: no (design section 4.6).
