9. **Nothing tells the coordinator to keep IDs out of chat.** Technical spec 7.1 says "Users never see IDs." Every read and write reply is full of them, such as `stop_k7m2x9qa`, and the only rule about IDs in the instructions is for memory items. Example: "I moved breakfast (stop_k7m2x9qa) to Day 3." Fix: add to Conduct, such as "Never show IDs to the user. Name places, days, and stops in words." Add it to the conduct bullet in technical spec 5.2.

10. **"Where the road is still open" reads as a road closure.** The skeleton bullet says "set waypoints on scenic legs where the road is still open". It means the part of a leg that no stop the user chose already decides (technical spec 4.2: "The route preference is for the stretches nobody has decided"). "Open" also means an unsettled warning elsewhere in the instructions. Example: the coordinator checks for seasonal closures, and sets scenic waypoints on a leg whose road the user's own stops already chose. Fix: say "where no stop the user chose already decides the road", and change technical spec 4.2 to match.

11. **`find_place` says "Every match is saved to the trip."** Item 2 uses "in the trip" to mean in the itinerary, and `find_in_trip` searches only the itinerary. A place `find_place` saved isn't in it. Example: after a `find_place` lookup, the coordinator expects `find_in_trip` to find the place later, and it doesn't. Fix: "Every match is stored, so its place ID works in the other tools. That doesn't add it to the itinerary."

12. **`remove_stay` says it's "Refused while any stop is on its days, or any stop anywhere is near it."** "Near it" sounds like distance on a map. It means a stop on another day whose search area is this stay. Fix: say that.

13. **Some text is repeated between the instructions and the tool descriptions,** which tool design section 4 says never to do, since the copies can drift apart:
    - "Stays can't be added until all three are set" in the discovery round, and `add_stay`'s "Needs the itinerary's start place, end place, and start date first."
    - "Only a day that starts and ends at the same stay can be a rest day" in "Days and approvals", and the same in `update_day`.
    - "Removing a night always removes the stay's last day" in "Changes to stays", and `update_stay`'s "Changing the nights adds or removes days at the end of the stay's days."
    - The `tierRule` input's "The rule that produced the tier", which says what the item means. By tool design section 4 that belongs only in the instructions, which already say it in the skeleton bullet on tiers. The input gives only the format.

    Fix: keep each fact in one place. Where a rule in the instructions depends on one, such as the advice on losing a different day when a night is removed, it can rely on the description instead of repeating it.

14. **The rule for a refused trip brief update conflicts with the limit rules.** It says "If the error gives a limit, such as the maximum daily driving, send the whole update again with that item at the limit, and tell the user it's set to the maximum." The rules on trip length and comfortable driving hours say to push back instead: propose a trip that fits, or recommend fewer hours and ask what's comfortable. The refusal only happens once the coordinator has already ignored the limit in its instructions and in the input's description, and the error gives the limit too. So a fourth place that says what to do adds nothing, and the coordinator can judge what to do next. Fix: drop that sentence. Keep "nothing in it was saved", which tells the coordinator to send the other items again. That's specific to this tool, so move it into `update_trip_brief`'s description, and drop the bullet from the instructions. Change technical spec 5.2 and the `setComfortableDriving()` refusal in domain model 4.2, which says "so the coordinator can send it again at the limit", to match.

15. **The coordinator can't see whether "the route already goes through" an area.** The skeleton bullet on must-see areas says to add a waypoint "unless the route already goes through." No tool returns a route's path, only times and distances. Fix: say it's a judgment from the coordinator's own knowledge of the roads, such as UT-24 running through Capitol Reef, and to add the waypoint when it isn't sure.

16. **Nothing says what to do when the user asks to forget a trip brief item.** The instructions say "Trip brief items can be changed, but not forgotten," and that when the user asks to forget an item, forget it, which is about memory. Fix, as a starting point:

    > When the user asks to forget a trip brief item, explain that it can be changed but not forgotten. For restDaysText or budgetRulesText, change its text to say there's none, such as "no budget rules."

    Only these two optional text items can say there's none. A required item can't, as item 17 says.

17. **Nothing says what "required" means for a trip brief item.** The instructions say each item is required except three, and to establish each one. They don't say what to do when the user says "we don't really have any interests" or "no must-sees". A model could save "none" and move on. The app plans trips to see and do things, not only routes between hotels, so "none" isn't an answer for a required item. Fix, as a starting point:

    > Required means a real answer. When the user has none, help them find one, such as by suggesting what the focus is known for. Don't save "none".

18. **"Confirm it and push back" can read as accept it.** The rule on comfortable driving hours says "When the user gives more than 6, confirm it and push back." "Confirm" can mean accept and save it. It means check that they mean it. Fix: "check that they mean it, and push back". Change functional spec 5.2 and technical spec 5.2, which say "confirms it and pushes back", to match.

More items are added here as the review goes on.

## Open questions

- None. The implementer writes a first draft of all new wording, and Joe gives feedback on it in the PR.

## Do

- Write a first draft of the new wording for each item, including item 1's itinerary section. Wording given in any item is a starting point, not settled text.
- Make each item's fix in the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`), the tool descriptions, and the design doc each one belongs in.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- The coordinator's view file shows each item's fix.
- The design docs match the instructions and tool descriptions.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Coordinator prompt and tool description fixes

body:
## Why

PR #158 (#156) was merged with two review notes left open. Both are about wording the coordinator reads. Neither makes the agent plan wrong, but both go against what #156 set out to do: name each idea one way, and define the itinerary's terms exactly. Notes are Joe's call (code review design section 3.2), so they're written down here until he decides.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2: the coordinator's itinerary section.
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.4: `compute_route`.

## Items

1. **`compute_route`'s reply says "Drive times".** Its reply still says "Drive times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer." Its description now says "road time", and the coordinator's itinerary section defines "Road time" as the name for this figure. So the coordinator reads a third name for the same numbers. Fix: "Road times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer." ([review note](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/pull/158#discussion_r4383234036))
2. **The "Leg" and "Day" terms don't fit the first and last days.** The "Leg" term says a leg runs "from where the party slept to where it sleeps that night". Day 1's leg starts at the start place, where the party didn't sleep. The last day's leg ends at the end place, where it doesn't sleep. The "Day" term says a day "either moves to a new stay, or stays put", but the last day does neither. Fix, as a starting point: a leg runs "from where the day starts, the start place or a stay, to where it ends, a stay or the end place", and the "Day" term covers the last day too. ([review note](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/pull/158#discussion_r4383234167))

## Open questions

- Fix these on their own, or fold them into #56, which adds to the same itinerary section?

## Do

- Fix both items in the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`) and `compute_route`'s reply, and change technical spec 5.2 and tool design 2.4 to match.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- The coordinator's view file shows both fixes.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

nodes.body: Folded into #56: both items are now in its Do list, word for word.

title: Wording left from #156's review: road time in compute_route's reply, and the Leg and Day terms

body:
## Why

Each place's Google Maps link ends in a long tracking parameter, such as `https://maps.google.com/?cid=8720190008484083912&g_mp=Cidnb29nbGUubWFwcy5wbGFjZXMudjEuUGxhY2VzLlNlYXJjaFRleHQQAhgEIAA`. The `g_mp` part is about 70 characters, and the link works without it. Every search result and `read_place` reply shows the link, so a `search_along_leg` reply of 20 places carries about 1,400 characters of it. Found in PR #159, while checking the place searches against Google.

## Design

- [Google design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/google.md), section 2.2 (`googleMapsUri`).

## Open questions

- Drop the `g_mp` parameter when a place is parsed, so it's never stored, or only when a tool shows the link? Places stored before the change would keep it.
- Is it worth doing at all? It's tokens in the workers' context, not a bug.
- Should the search replies be trimmed more widely? A real `search_along_leg` reply of 20 places ran to about 19,000 characters, and `search_near`'s 10 places to about 10,000 (PR #159). The leg scout may run several queries per leg, so this adds up in its context. Each place carries Google's summaries, its hours, and two links, and the summaries are likely the largest part. Look at which fields help a worker choose, and cut the rest. Best judged once the stay researcher (#60) and the leg scout (#61) exist, so their real use shows what they read. Added on 2026-10-26.

## Do

- Decide, and if it's worth it, drop the parameter from the links the agents see.

## Done when

- A search's reply shows each Google Maps link without `g_mp`, and the link still opens the place.

## Ends in

A PR, or a decision not to.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Shorter Google Maps links in place replies

body:
## Why

During the chat checks for #56 (PR #162), the coordinator added the Pulgas Water Temple as a waypoint on San Francisco Day 1 on its first turn, without the user asking. It took the waypoint off when the user said to. The user's message asked for a 3-day trip from San Francisco. We don't know yet whether the coordinator followed its instructions, such as the skeleton rule on scenic waypoints or a must-see, or added a waypoint the instructions don't call for. If it's the instructions, a rule may be too eager. If not, it's model behavior worth knowing about before the evals.

## Where to look

The chat ran locally against the local Postgres, with the Phoenix tunnel up (DEVELOPMENT.md section 2):

- Phoenix project: `road-trip-agent-local`.
- Phoenix session ID (the Agent SDK's session ID): `0458e3f3-2dc2-41ce-8f19-1c6ca0fa11f4`.
- App session: `session_acehc3te`, trip `trip_gybnhkaj`, in the local database.

The waypoint was set with `set_waypoints` on the first turn.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (route preference and must-sees) and 5.2 (the coordinator's instructions).

## Open questions

- Why did the coordinator add the waypoint? Read the first turn's trace: the user's message, the trip brief's route preference and must-sees at that point, and the coordinator's reasoning before the `set_waypoints` call.
- If an instruction led to it, should that instruction change, or was the waypoint a fair call that the coordinator should have explained to the user?

## Do

- Read the trace and answer the open questions.
- If an instruction should change, make the change in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2, and commit the coordinator's view file with it (`npm run agent-views`).

## Done when

- The cause is written in this issue.
- Any instruction change is merged, or the issue says why none is needed.

## Ends in

A decision, or a PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

nodes.body:
## Cause

The coordinator followed the scenic rule in its instructions. The brief had `routePreference: scenic`. The must-sees, Hangar One and the Boardwalk, fixed most of Day 1's road, but not the stretch from San Francisco to Mountain View. So the rule ("set waypoints on scenic legs where no stop the user chose already decides the road") applied there. Its reasoning before the `set_waypoints` call was "I'm considering I-280 as the scenic freeway option from SF toward Mountain View." Steering onto I-280 was a fair call.

The waypoint it picked was the mistake. The Pulgas Water Temple sits off I-280 on Cañada Road, so the route left the freeway to pass through it: Day 1's road time went from 2 h 29 m to 2 h 48 m. Its reply then called the temple "a quirky little spot," which read as a stop the user hadn't asked for. The instructions don't say a waypoint should be a point on the road itself, or that a waypoint isn't a stop.

The same session's empty `set_waypoints` call on Day 3 came from the instruction to clear waypoints when fastest is approved. The day had none, so the call did nothing.

Both changes are in #166, so this issue closes with no change of its own.

title: Find out why the coordinator added an unasked waypoint on San Francisco Day 1

body:
## Why

Two chat sessions showed the coordinator using waypoints in ways that are hard to trace or that the user didn't want. A waypoint is a place a day's drive passes through without stopping, to steer the route (the coordinator's itinerary terms, technical spec 5.2).

1. **Empty `set_waypoints` calls that do nothing.** The coordinator's instructions say: "When the user approves fastest on a day, also clear the day's waypoints with set_waypoints and an empty list, in the same turn." The coordinator follows this even when the day has no waypoints, so the call changes nothing. Both cases below were like that. Code already removes a day's waypoints when the day is marked a rest day (domain model 4.5). If approving fastest did the same, the coordinator couldn't forget the step, and wouldn't make calls that do nothing.
2. **A waypoint picked as a sight, not as a point on the road.** With `routePreference: scenic`, the coordinator wanted San Francisco Day 1 on I-280 rather than US-101. It picked the Pulgas Water Temple as the waypoint. The temple sits off I-280 on Cañada Road, so the route left the freeway to pass through it: road time went from 2 h 29 m to 2 h 48 m. Then the reply told the user "We take I-280 past the Pulgas Water Temple, a quirky little spot," so it read as a stop the user hadn't asked for. The user had it taken off (#163). The domain model already says a waypoint sits on the road the coordinator wants (3.6 and 4.7). The coordinator's instructions don't say so, and don't say a waypoint isn't a stop. By contrast, in a later session it picked Belfast and Wiscasset, towns US-1 runs through, which added 3 minutes and 0 minutes.
3. **A waypoint holds no reason.** Waypoints are set for different reasons: to steer onto a scenic road, to make sure the route reaches a must-see area or road, or because the user asked for a road. Nothing on the waypoint says which. So when waypoints are cleared, the coordinator can't tell which ones it still needs without matching them against the trip brief's must-sees, and in a later session it has no memory of setting them. Someone reading the itinerary can't tell either: the Pulgas Water Temple waypoint would have shown "steer onto I-280", which makes the bad pick plain without reading the trace. Approvals and tier rules already carry their reasons this way.

## Where to look

Traces in Phoenix (DEVELOPMENT.md section 2):

- Live site, project `road-trip-agent`, session `12e986d6-2433-4e8d-b6ba-7ed2e4625c7b`. The empty call is span `6cdca9c8fb609fa8` (tool call `toolu_01SocX9RYr5ad1RoQG4qa7sB`), on Day 1, right after `update_day` approved fastest. The Belfast and Wiscasset waypoints are in the same turn.
- Local, project `road-trip-agent-local`, session `0458e3f3-2dc2-41ce-8f19-1c6ca0fa11f4`. The empty call is span `dd56be8d3fc8447d`, on Day 3, right after `update_day` approved fastest. The Pulgas Water Temple waypoint is set in the first turn, after the coordinator's reasoning "I'm considering I-280 as the scenic freeway option from SF toward Mountain View."

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 4.2 (must-sees that aren't one place, and the route preference), section 5.2 (the itinerary terms, and the rule for approving fastest), and section 8 (route type).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.6 (Day: waypoints), 4.5 (`DaysService.approveRouteType()`), and 4.7 (how a leg is routed).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`update_day`, `set_waypoints`, and `read_itinerary`).
- [Persistence](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 1 (migrations).

## Open questions

- ~~Clearing waypoints in code when fastest is approved also clears one set for a must-see area or road on that day. What does the coordinator do about those?~~ Settled 2026-10-27 in chat with Joe: each waypoint carries a reason, and `update_day`'s reply names each waypoint it cleared, with its reason. After approving fastest, the coordinator puts back, with `set_waypoints`, each cleared waypoint whose reason is a must-see or a user's request, and drops the ones that only steered toward the scenic road. It tells the user in one line what it dropped. See Do.

## Do

- **Each waypoint carries a reason.** `set_waypoints` takes each waypoint as a place ID and a reason, both required, such as "steer onto US-1", "must-see: Capitol Reef", or "the user asked: the Golden Gate Bridge". The day stores the reason with the place. `read_itinerary`'s leg line and `set_waypoints`' reply show each waypoint with its reason. The leg's `routedWaypoints` stays places only, since it records what Google was asked. Add a migration that gives waypoints in saved trips a reason that says none was recorded. Change domain model 3.6 (Day: waypoints, and its sentence "Users don't pick waypoints", since a user can ask for a road), tool design 2.1, and the coordinator's itinerary section in technical spec 5.2 to match. The downloads in `src/api/plan-downloads.ts` show the stored shape, so check they still read well.
- **Approving fastest clears the day's waypoints in code.** In `DaysService.approveRouteType()`, approving fastest clears the day's waypoints. Approving scenic leaves them alone. The leg is re-routed at the end of the write, as usual. `update_day`'s reply names each waypoint it cleared, with its reason, and gives the leg's new road time. Say so in `update_day`'s description, and change domain model 4.5, tool design 2.1, and technical spec section 8 to match. Replace the instruction to clear them with `set_waypoints` in the coordinator's instructions and technical spec 5.2 with the rule from the settled open question. Add tests with fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).
- **Say how to pick a waypoint.** In the coordinator's instructions (the itinerary terms or the waypoint rules), and in technical spec 4.2 and 5.2, say:
  - A waypoint is a place on the road itself, such as a town or a junction the road runs through, not a sight beside it.
  - A waypoint isn't a stop. A place worth seeing becomes a stop the user agrees to. Don't describe a waypoint to the user as a sight.
  - Check the road time in `set_waypoints`' reply. A waypoint that adds much more than a few minutes is a detour: pick another point on the road. One that adds nothing isn't needed, since the route already takes that road.
- The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- `set_waypoints` refuses a waypoint without a reason, and `read_itinerary` shows each waypoint's reason. Tests show both.
- Approving fastest on a day with waypoints clears them, and the reply names each one with its reason and gives the leg's new road time. A test shows it.
- The migration runs locally on a trip with waypoints, and the trip still loads.
- The coordinator's view file has no instruction to clear waypoints with an empty list, and has the rule for putting waypoints back and the waypoint guidance above.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Waypoints: a reason on each one, clear them in code when fastest is approved, and say how to pick one

body:
**Starts** once #53 and #245 are merged.

## Why

When the user's answer about driving hours was vague, the coordinator raised `comfortableDrivingInHours` to cover the trip's one long day, instead of approving that day on its own. The user had to push back before it set the plan up the way it had first suggested. The instruction change that should fix this is small and clear. This issue checks that the change works, with an evaluation run before and after it: a baseline on the current instructions, then the change, then the same evaluation again. It's a good early case for evaluations, since the setup is one situation and the result can be scored from what was saved.

## What happened

Live site, Phoenix project `road-trip-agent`, session `12e986d6-2433-4e8d-b6ba-7ed2e4625c7b`. The trip is Natick, MA to Bar Harbor and back over four days. Day 1 is the long drive, about 5 h 33 m with the drive buffer. The other days are about 2 to 3¼ hours.

1. **Turn at 12:57 UTC.** The user implied a long Thursday and short days after it, but gave no number. The coordinator asked, and suggested 4 hours as the everyday limit with Thursday marked as the long day. That is the setup we want.
2. **Turn at 13:30 UTC.** The user said: "The first day is the longest drive, then it sounds like the rest of the legs are pretty short, so I think whatever the other lets turn out to be will be ok." The coordinator's reasoning was: "I think I'll just set the comfortable threshold at 6 hours, which covers that without needing a separate approval step." It set `comfortableDrivingInHours` to 6 (span `8b73ba77a8f93dd7`), and told the user "nothing is flagged." With a 6-hour limit, a 5½-hour Saturday would never be flagged either.
3. **Turn at 13:32 UTC.** The user said: "Ok, but we only really want to drive that amount on Thur, the rest should be much shorter drive times, right?" The coordinator set the limit to 4 (span `bfc7dfda2e38e5ef`) and approved Day 1 at 6 hours with `update_day` (span `6a606bf772d5ca6d`).

**It happened again in Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30,** agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, turn 5 (turn span `6c2d643f61c8165e`; the `update_trip_brief` call is span `d7e40f940adba3b6`). It's the same trip shape: Day 1 is 5 h 45 m of driving with the drive buffer, and the other days are about 3 to 3½ hours. The user said: "our longest drive is going to be [Natick] to Bar Harbor, and that's fine. So that's like, you know, we expected a kind of long day that day. The rest are shorter. So, you know, I think everything looks fine there. So I think we're good on driving." The coordinator set `comfortableDrivingInHours` to 6, which covers Day 1, and approved nothing on Day 1 for driving. It did approve the fastest route on Day 1, with the reason "need to reach Bar Harbor for the 6 p.m. event", which was right. Joe's read: the plan worked out for this trip, but raising the trip default to cover the long day isn't the behavior we want.

**Why it happened.** The coordinator's instructions say `comfortableDrivingInHours` is "a default for the trip, not a hard limit: a day can go over it when the user agrees," and how to approve a longer day with `update_day`. Nothing says not to raise the default to cover one long day.

## The fix to test

Add to the coordinator's comfortable driving hours section, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2: set it to what a normal day of the trip should be, not to cover one long day, and approve the long day on its own with `update_day`. Add an example close to this session: the user says the first day is long and the rest are short, so the coordinator sets the normal-day hours and approves Day 1. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (comfortable driving hours, and days and approvals) and section 8 (the daily driving check).
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- ~~How is the situation set up? Two ways: replay the session's turns up to the vague reply, or start from a saved trip with the four days and no `comfortableDrivingInHours`, and send one message that is just as vague. Proposal: the saved trip and one message, since it's shorter to run and the earlier turns don't change the choice.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat: start from the Bar Harbor session's turn 5, with #245. The coordinator gets turns 1 to 4 as they were recorded, the trip version from the start of turn 5 (#244), and the recorded turn 5 message. Only the Bar Harbor session is used. The first session above ran on instructions and tools that have changed too much since to count as a baseline.
- What counts as a pass? Proposal, scored from what was saved: a pass is `comfortableDrivingInHours` less than Day 1's driving, with a drive hours approval on Day 1. Asking the user for a number again also passes, since nothing was set to cover the long day. A fail is `comfortableDrivingInHours` at or above Day 1's driving.
- How many runs before and after? Proposal: 10 each, so a change from, say, 4 fails in 10 to 0 is clear.

## Do

- Before writing the evaluation, check whether #230 has merged. It gives comfortable driving hours a default of 4 hours, so a new trip's trip brief no longer starts with none, and the coordinator asks only once a day goes over it (settled 2026-10-30, in #230's first open question). Recheck this issue's setup, its pass rule, and the fix to test against that, and settle any change in chat before going on.
- Write the evaluation, and run it on the current instructions for the baseline. Record the results in this issue.
- If the baseline passes almost every run, the change still goes in, since the gap in the instructions is clear. The evaluation then catches it if it comes back.
- Make the instruction change. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with it.
- Run the evaluation again, and record the results in the PR.

## Done when

- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with how many runs passed in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Comfortable driving hours: set a normal day, approve the long one, checked with an evaluation

body:
## Why

A day's schedule puts any wait before a stop's set time before the drive to it. On a day whose first selected stop has a set time, that puts the wait before the day's first drive. So the schedule says to leave hours after the day's start time, and shows the free time where the party slept, or at home. That goes against the rule in domain model 4.1: "On a day with a leg, the party leaves where it slept at that time." The start time is when the user said they want to leave. The coordinator reads this same schedule (`read_itinerary`), so it can pass a wrong departure time on to the user.

Waits later in the day stay before the drive, where the party is. Free time is time nothing is planned for, worked out from the gap before a set time. When the party does something specific with it, such as checking in at the hotel or walking around town, that's a stop. #169 adds a stop for checking in at the stay, and with this rule, the free time after a check-in shows at the hotel, before the drive out.

## What happened

Live site, session `session_5hf47qpn` (the Natick to Bar Harbor trip). Day 1 starts at 10:00 a.m. Its only selected stop is the College of the Atlantic alumni event, set for 6:00 p.m. A lunch stop along the leg has no place yet, so it takes no time. The drive is 5 h 25 m with the buffer. The itinerary view shows:

- 10:00 a.m. to 12:35 p.m.: free time, 2 h 35 m.
- 12:35 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.: drive.
- 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.: the event.

It should show the drive from 10:00 a.m. to 3:25 p.m., then free time from 3:25 to 6:00 p.m., then the event.

## Where it comes from

Domain model 4.1, "How the schedule is worked out": "The party waits before driving, not after, so the wait shows as free time before the drive." The code is `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`, which works each drive's start back from the arrival. Arrival times don't change with this issue, so the late check, the opening hours check, and the other check results stay the same (technical spec section 8). Only where the first drive and its free time sit in the schedule changes.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out, including the stops with no selected place).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's itinerary section, which says what free time is).

## Open questions

None.

## Do

- **The day's first drive leaves at the day's start time.** When the party arrives before the first selected stop's set time, the wait shows as free time after that drive, before the stop. Every later wait stays as it is: free time before the drive on. Change `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`.
- **A stop with no selected place still goes where its time falls,** so the schedule stays in time order. When its set time falls within the free time after the first drive, it splits that free time. Work out where one goes when its time falls during that drive, and say so in domain model 4.1.
- Change domain model 4.1 to match, and check that its examples still hold.
- Change the coordinator's line "Free time is a wait before the party drives on" in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and technical spec 5.2 if it says the same. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Add a schedule test for a day like Day 1 above, and change any existing ones that this changes. Tests use fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A test shows a day like Day 1 above: the drive starts at the day's start time, and the free time comes after it, before the set time.
- A test shows a later wait in the day still comes before the drive on.
- Check results for the same trip are unchanged.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Schedule: the day's first drive leaves at the day's start time

body:
**Starts** once #176 is merged.

## Why

A day reaches its stay only at the end, so the itinerary can't show the party checking in at the hotel before a later stop. Users plan days that way: check in, freshen up, then go out to an evening event or dinner. The coordinator can say so in chat, but the schedule and the route don't show it, so the times and the drive are wrong for the day as the user will live it.

Free time is time nothing is planned for, worked out from the gap before a set time. What the party does with time, such as checking in or walking around town, is a stop. So checking in becomes a stop at the stay. After #176, every wait comes after the drive, just before the stop with the set time. So the free time after a check-in shows before the next stop with a set time, and the coordinator works out with the user what to do with it (see Decided).

## What happened

Live site, session `session_5hf47qpn` (the Natick to Bar Harbor trip). The user said: "We would want to ideally check into our hotel before going to COA." Day 1 is Natick to Bar Harbor, with lunch on the way and the College of the Atlantic alumni event set for 6:00 p.m. The coordinator told the user "That gives you time to check in and freshen up before the College of the Atlantic event at 6:00," but the schedule drives straight to the college, then 8 minutes to Bar Harbor at 9:08 p.m.

The day the user wants: leave at 10:00, lunch on the way, check in at the hotel, free time there, drive to the college for 6:00, then drive back to the hotel after.

Domain model 4.7 already notes the same gap for a late-night stop: "Moab Day 4 is routed Capitol Gorge → Panorama Point → Torrey hotel, though the party really checks in first and drives out again at night."

## Decided

- **Check-in can happen at any time.** Hotels have check-in times, such as 3:00 or 4:00 p.m., but nothing checks them. Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27, to keep the change small.
- **The free time after a check-in follows #176's rule,** so it comes after the drive to the next stop with a set time. On Day 1 above, the day reads: the drive to the hotel, a 30-minute check-in, the 8-minute drive to the college, then about 2 hours of free time before the 6:00 event. The coordinator raises that time with the user, and suggests something that fits it and the way from the hotel to the college, such as a stop in Bar Harbor itself, coffee, or a walk around the campus. A suggestion the user agrees to becomes a stop. If the user would rather stay at the hotel until it's time to leave for the event, the coordinator gives the check-in a longer visit time, such as 2 hours to check in, freshen up, and rest, so the free time goes away. Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3 (Stay: `sleepsAt`; Stop), 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out), 4.6 (`StopsService`), and 4.7 (how a leg is routed, and the Moab Day 4 note).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (laying out days), section 6 (the workers that fill stops), and section 8 (the checks).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`add_stops` and the other stop tools).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 9 (the itinerary view).

## Open questions

- ~~How is a check-in held? Proposal: a stop of a new kind, beside meal and attraction, so it takes part in the day's order, `move_stop`, set times, and the schedule like any other stop. Its place is the stay's `sleepsAt`: the lodging once one is selected, and the town until then. So selecting a hotel moves it, and it never has candidates.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: a stop of a new kind, `checkIn`, beside meal and attraction. It has no search area, since no worker searches for it, and no candidates. Its place is worked out by the calendar, not stored: the `sleepsAt` of the stay the party sleeps at that night (`endStayOf()` for its day). So selecting a hotel moves it, and moving it to another day with `move_stop` takes it to that night's stay. It has a place from the moment it's added, so it counts as selected, and `add_stops` re-routes the leg when it adds one. Code that routes, schedules, checks, or shows a stop reads its place from the calendar, in place of `selectedPlace`. `add_stops` takes only its kind, purpose, and set time.
- ~~Which stay can it be at? Proposal: only the stay where the party sleeps that night, so never on the last day.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: it follows from the answer above. The last day has no stay to sleep at, so adding or moving a check-in there is refused. A stay can't be removed while a stop is on its days, so a check-in's stay can't go away under it. A day holds at most one check-in, so adding or moving a second one onto a day is refused. Joe couldn't think of a day that needs two that's worth supporting.
- ~~How long is its visit? Proposal: the coordinator sets it, as for an attraction the user names, such as 30 minutes to check in and freshen up.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: a new setting, the check-in visit time, of 30 minutes (technical spec section 10). Every check-in starts with it, the way a meal gets the meal visit time, so `add_stops` takes no visit time. The coordinator changes it with `update_stop` when the user wants longer, such as 2 hours to rest at the hotel until the event (see Decided).
- ~~What do the workers and checks do with it? Proposal: no worker fills it, and the opening hours check skips it.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27:
  - **Workers:** none fills it. A worker gets a stop only through its search area, and a check-in has none.
  - **Opening hours:** the three opening hours checks skip it. Google often has no hours for a hotel, so every check-in would get the "not known" note. Check-in times aren't checked (see Decided).
  - **Stop order:** a check-in splits the day into two parts for the check, like two short days. Google can't hold one stop in place while it reorders the rest, and it would nearly always move the check-in to the end, next to the hotel. On Day 1 that order saves about 16 minutes, over the 15-minute stop-order minimum saving, so every day like it would get a note to check in after the event. So the check-in stays where the coordinator put it. Google picks the best order of the stops before it, from where the day starts to the check-in's place, and of the stops after it, from there to where the day ends. Each part is ordered only when it has two or more selected stops, so Day 1 needs no call. `timeSavedInMinutes` is the two savings added, and `stopsInBestOrder` is the two parts joined, with the check-in in its place.
  - **The other checks** need nothing new. Daily driving counts the drives to and from the hotel, since the party drives them. Weather activities hold only attractions, and a check-in has no search area to not fit its day.
- ~~When does the coordinator add one? Proposal: when the user asks to check in before a later stop, or when the day has a stop near the stay after the party would have arrived, such as Moab Day 4's stargazing.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: when the user asks to check in before a later stop, the coordinator adds one. When the day has a stop after the party reaches the stay's town, such as Moab Day 4's stargazing at 1 a.m., the coordinator suggests checking in first, and adds the check-in once the user agrees, as in #176. It doesn't add one as the day's last stop, since the day already ends at the stay. That's guidance in the coordinator's instructions, not a rule in code. After a check-in, the free time handling in Decided applies: on Moab Day 4, the coordinator raises the long evening before the stargazing, and suggests dinner or a longer check-in visit time.

## Do

- Write the answers to the open questions into the design docs.
- Build it in the domain, the tools, and the itinerary view, with tests using fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).
- Add the coordinator's rule for when to add one, and how it handles the free time after one (see Decided), in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- A test shows a day like Day 1 above: the drive to the stay, the check-in, the drive to the event, free time before its set time, then the drive back to the stay.
- A test shows the same day with a longer check-in visit time: the party leaves the hotel just in time for the event, with no free time before it.
- Selecting a lodging for the stay moves the check-in to it, and re-routes the leg.
- A test shows the stop-order check splits a day at its check-in: the check-in keeps its place, and only the stops before it, or after it, are reordered.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Check in at the stay before a later stop

body:
## Why

Three small changes put each part of the web app where it belongs, before its look is redesigned. They change what is on each page, not how it looks.

1. **The plan downloads should show what the coordinator sees.** Today "Download plan" saves the trip brief and the itinerary as JSON, with each place's name and address in place of its ID, and no route lines. "Download plan as stored" saves the same data as the database holds it, plus every stored fact about each place the plan links to. Neither one is the text the coordinator reads, so neither helps trace why the coordinator did something. The stored one shows little that the readable one doesn't.
2. **"Delete trip" belongs on the trips list,** next to each trip, not inside the trip. Deleting is about the trip as a whole, so it sits with the other trips, the way a file is deleted from its folder.
3. **The health line shrinks to the Phoenix check, on the trips list only.** Today, at the foot of every page, it says whether the API and the database can be reached, then whether turn traces reach Phoenix. The API and database part was there to show the pages worked. A problem there is plain anyway, since sign-in or the trip list fails. Whether traces reach Phoenix isn't plain, since the chat works the same either way and the traces are lost, so that part stays. Once is enough.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.1 (the trip's sessions, "Delete trip", the health line, and the downloads).
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 10 (the Phoenix check on the health line).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`read_itinerary`, and what a whole read gives).
- [Persistence](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), `readPlaces(tripId)`, which only the downloads use.

## Decided

Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27:

- **Two downloads, both text the coordinator could read, with no JSON download.** Each starts with what `read_trip_brief` returns, then the itinerary.
  - **"Download plan"** gives the itinerary exactly as `read_itinerary` returns it for the scope "all", the read the coordinator gets at the start of each session. Its stays and days are at the "slim" detail (`wholeLines()` in `src/tools/itinerary-lines.ts`).
  - **"Download full plan"** gives the same layout with every stay and day at the "full" detail, as a read scoped to a stay gives them: every candidate, with its rationale. The coordinator never gets the whole trip at this detail in one read, but each part matches what it sees when it reads that stay or stop.
  - **No size limit.** A whole read the coordinator asks for is refused when it's too large, but a download never is.
  - **A download saves nothing.** A read marks each check result new or already known. A download marks them the same way, but doesn't change what's saved, so the coordinator's next read is unchanged.
- **"Delete trip" moves to the trips list,** one control per trip, and leaves the trip's page. It still asks first, and it's still refused while a reply in one of the trip's sessions is coming in.
- **Only the Phoenix check stays, on the trips list only.** It says whether turn traces reach Phoenix, with the green check or red X. The words about the API and the database go. `/api/health` stays as it is, since the deploy calls it (systems design section 7), and the page still reads the Phoenix check from it.

## Open questions

- ~~Does the health line also show on the sign-in page?~~ Settled 2026-10-27 in chat with Joe: no. Only the Phoenix check is left, and traces matter only once the user is signed in and chatting.

## Do

- Replace the two JSON downloads with the two text downloads, in `src/api/plan-downloads.ts`, `src/api/plan-download-routes.ts`, and `web/src/plan-downloads.tsx`, reusing the functions `read_trip_brief` and `read_itinerary` use. Remove `readPlaces()` if nothing else uses it.
- Move "Delete trip" from the trip's page to the trips list, in `web/src/trip-page.tsx` and `web/src/home-page.tsx`.
- Cut the health line to the Phoenix check, and show it only on the trips list (`web/src/health-status.tsx` and where it's placed).
- Change functional spec 10.1 and systems design section 10 to match, and persistence design if `readPlaces()` goes.
- Add or change tests with fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5), such as that "Download plan" gives the same text as a whole read.

## Done when

- In the browser, on the live site or locally: each download saves a text file, and "Download plan" matches what the coordinator's whole read returned in the session's trace. Each trip on the trips list has a delete control that asks first, and the trip's page has none. Only the trips list shows the Phoenix check, and no page shows the API and database line.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Web app: plan downloads as the coordinator sees them, delete from the trips list, and only the Phoenix check, there

body:
## Why

In the chat view, the second plan download from one page didn't save in Chrome. Seen in the browser check for #170 (PR #172), on the local site. "Download plan" saved a file. Then "Download full plan" sent its request, which returned 200, but no file was saved. Reloading the page didn't help. A new tab saved it at once.

This is most likely Chrome's limit on a page starting more than one download. Chrome then asks in the address bar whether the site may download several files, and holds the download until the user allows it. The page starts each download itself, with a link it clicks after the fetch (`downloadFile()` in `web/src/api-client.ts`), so Chrome may count it as a download the page started, not the user. The two JSON downloads before #170 worked the same way, so this isn't new.

In the check, the first two downloads were started from a script, not a real click, which may be what set the limit off. So it isn't known yet whether a user who clicks both buttons hits it.

## Open questions

- Does a user who clicks "Download plan" and then "Download full plan" get both files, or a prompt? Check by hand in Chrome, with real clicks.
- If they get a prompt, is that fine as it is, since the user can allow it once for the site?

## Do

- Check the open questions in Chrome. If a fix is wanted, settle it here first.

## Done when

- The open questions are answered here.

## Ends in

A decision, or a PR if a fix is wanted.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Web app: check whether Chrome holds a second plan download from the same page

body:
## Why

A day's schedule has to put each wait for a stop's set time somewhere: before the drive to the stop, where the party already is, or after it, at the stop. Today it depends on the drive. #168 made the day's first drive leave at the day's start time, so the first wait comes after that drive, and later waits still come before the drive on. Then a fix during #168's review added an exception: an empty stop near where the day starts, such as a breakfast near the hotel with no place picked yet, comes before the first drive (domain model 4.1, "The party doesn't drive away from a stop near where the day starts"). An empty stop is one with no selected place, so it takes no time.

Where a wait is best spent is a judgment call. After a long drive, the party may want to arrive early and spend the time at the destination, such as checking in and walking around Bar Harbor. Before a short hop, such as to breakfast, it would rather wait at the hotel. Rules in code that tell these apart get fiddly, and the near-start rule is one of them. Even so, a picked café still looks odd: on a day that starts at 7:00 a.m., with a café 6 minutes from the Portland hotel and breakfast set for 8:00, the schedule drives at 7:00 and then waits 54 minutes at the café.

So code keeps one simple rule, and the coordinator makes the judgment with levers it already has: the day's start time (`update_day`, which needs the user's agreement), a stop's visit time (`update_stop`), and adding a stop. Free time is a signal. When a day has a lot of it before a set time, the coordinator raises it with the user and suggests concrete choices. Example, for a day from Natick to Bar Harbor that starts at 10:00 a.m., with a 5 h 25 m drive and an event at 6:00 p.m.: "If you leave at 10:00, you'll reach Bar Harbor at 3:25 and have about 2½ hours before the event. You could stay home longer and leave at 12:30, stop for lunch and a walk in Camden on the way, or keep the plan and have the time in Bar Harbor." For the café day, the coordinator offers a 7:50 start, so the party leaves the hotel just in time for breakfast.

Arrival times don't depend on where a wait goes, so the check results don't change.

## Decided

Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27:

- **Every wait comes after the drive,** just before the stop with the set time. The party arrives early, and spends the free time there. This holds for every drive in the day, not only the first.
- **The near-start rule goes.** An empty stop near where the day starts goes where its time falls, like any other empty stop, even when that's after the day's first drive. Example: on a day that starts at 7:00 a.m. in Portland with a 5 h 25 m drive, an empty breakfast set for 8:00 shows after the drive that leaves at 7:00. A schedule can look odd while a place isn't picked, since an empty stop has no place to drive to and takes no time. That's accepted.
- **No new tool and no new stored setting.** The coordinator shapes free time with the day's start time, visit times, and stops.
- **The coordinator suggests, not just asks.** When a day has free time, it says how much there is and where it falls, and offers concrete choices, with times and places from the trip:
  - **Leave later.** Give the new start time. The party spends the time where it slept.
  - **Fill the time.** Suggest one or two things to see or do that fit the user's interests, such as coffee or a walk downtown before leaving, or a stop on the way.
  - **Arrive early.** Keep the plan, and say when the party would arrive.

  Example: "You don't need to leave Portland at 8:00. You could leave at 10:00 and still make it, which gives you two hours. Would you like to stay at the hotel and start at 10:00? Or get coffee or take a walk downtown first? Or are you fine leaving at 8:00 and getting to Bar Harbor two hours early?" It changes the start time, or adds a stop, only once the user agrees.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's itinerary section, which says what free time is, and days and approvals, for a start time for one day) and section 8 (the checks).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`update_day` and `update_stop`).

## Open questions

- ~~How is the coordinator's handling of free time evaluated? Whether it raises free time, and which lever it offers, is a judgment call, so only an evaluation shows whether it does it well. Three parts:~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: this issue makes the change without an evaluation, and #177 adds it once #53 and this issue are merged. #177 holds the situation and what counts as a pass.
  - ~~**When does it run?** In this issue, before and after the instruction change, as #167 does, or in a later issue? #167 waits on #53, which sets up how evaluations run. Proposal: this issue makes the change without an evaluation, since the rule and the guidance are clear, and a later issue adds the evaluation once #53 is merged. Then #169 doesn't wait on #53.~~
  - ~~**What's the situation?** Proposal: a saved trip with the Natick to Bar Harbor day above laid out and the event selected, and one message from the user asking to go over that day.~~
  - ~~**What counts as a pass?** Proposal: the reply says how much free time there is before the event, and offers at least one choice: a later start, a longer stop, or another stop. The day's start time is unchanged, since the user hasn't agreed to a new one. A judge scores the reply, with the saved trip to check the start time.~~

## Do

- **Every wait comes after the drive.** Change `src/domain/day-timeline.ts` so each wait for a set time shows after the drive to that stop, as free time, before the stop. That's every drive in the day, not only the first.
- **Remove the near-start rule:** the near-start part of `#addFirstDrive()`, `#lastNearStartBefore()`, the `isNearStart` input that `Calendar` passes to `timelineOf()`, and their tests in `src/domain/calendar-first-drive.test.ts`.
- **Rewrite domain model 4.1 to match.** Change the free time bullet and "A stop with no selected place goes where its time falls", and remove "The party doesn't drive away from a stop near where the day starts". Say that an empty stop can look odd until a place is picked, and that this is accepted, with the Portland breakfast as the example. Check that its examples still hold.
- **Rewrite the coordinator's free time line** in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2, and add the guidance: free time comes after the drive, before the stop with the set time; when a day has a lot of it, raise it with the user, say how much there is, and suggest concrete choices: leave later, with the new start time; fill the time with one or two things that fit the user's interests, such as a longer stop or a new one; or arrive early, with the arrival time; change the start time or add a stop only once the user agrees. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Change the schedule tests this changes, and add the ones below. Tests use fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A test shows a later wait now comes after the drive. Example: lunch ends at 1:00 p.m., and the next stop is set for 6:00 p.m., 2 h 30 m away with the buffer. The schedule reads: the drive from 1:00 to 3:30, then free time from 3:30 to 6:00.
- A test shows the day's first drive still leaves at the day's start time, with the wait after it, as on the Natick to Bar Harbor day.
- A test shows the empty Portland breakfast set for 8:00 comes after the first drive.
- Check results for the example trips are unchanged.
- The coordinator's view file has the new free time line and the guidance, and no near-start exception.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. The wording is drafted by the implementer and reviewed in the PR.
title: Schedule: every wait comes after the drive, and the coordinator shapes free time

body:
**Starts** once #53 and #176 are merged.

## Why

Free time is time in a day's schedule that nothing is planned for, such as a wait for a stop's set time (domain model 4.1). #176 makes every wait show after the drive, just before the stop with the set time, so the party arrives early. It also tells the coordinator to raise free time with the user, and to suggest ways to use it. Whether the coordinator does that well is a judgment call, so only an evaluation shows it. This issue writes that evaluation and runs it.

## Decided

Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27, while settling #176's open question:

- **The coordinator suggests, not just asks.** When a day has free time, it says how much there is and where it falls, and offers concrete choices, with times and places from the trip:
  - **Leave later.** Give the new start time. The party spends the time where it slept.
  - **Fill the time.** Suggest one or two things to see or do that fit the user's interests, such as coffee or a walk downtown before leaving, or a stop on the way.
  - **Arrive early.** Keep the plan, and say when the party would arrive.
- Example: "You don't need to leave Portland at 8:00. You could leave at 10:00 and still make it, which gives you two hours. Would you like to stay at the hotel and start at 10:00? Or get coffee or take a walk downtown first? Or are you fine leaving at 8:00 and getting to Bar Harbor two hours early?"
- **It changes the start time, or adds a stop, only once the user agrees.** A new start time needs the user's agreement (technical spec 5.2, days and approvals).

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's itinerary section, which says what free time is and how the coordinator handles it, once #176 is merged).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out).
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- What's the situation? Proposal: a saved trip with one day that has a lot of free time, and one message from the user asking to go over that day. The day leaves a stay at 8:00 a.m., with a drive that reaches an event set for later in the day about two hours early. The trip brief names interests, such as coffee and walkable towns, so the judge can tell whether a suggestion fits them.
  - **A second situation, added by Joe on 2026-10-27: Moab Day 4** (domain model 5.2). Capitol Gorge ends at 4:40 p.m., the drive to Panorama Point ends at 5:05, and then there are about 8 hours of free time before the stargazing at 1:00 a.m. This wait comes after a later drive, not the day's first. So a later start for the day isn't the natural choice, since it pushes Goblin Valley and Capitol Reef later too. A pass offers a longer visit at Capitol Gorge or the stops before it, something to do in the evening that fits the interests, such as dinner in Torrey, or arriving early. The saved trip is checked the same way: no visit time changed and no stop added.
- What counts as a pass? Proposal: a judge scores the reply against the three choices above. A pass says how much free time there is, and offers a later start with its time, at least one named thing to do that fits the interests, and arriving early. A reply that only asks what the user wants, with no suggestion, fails. The saved trip is checked too: the day's start time is unchanged, and no stop was added.
- How many runs? Proposal: 10, as in #167.
- ~~Should "arrive early" be saved to trip memory? #176 added this to the coordinator's free time guidance: "When the user chooses to arrive early, save that to trip memory, so it isn't raised again." Joe questioned it on 2026-10-27: it may be a band-aid for something the trip itself should hold. The risk it covers is a later session, where a read shows the same free time and the coordinator raises it again. Options: keep it; store the choice on the day, like an approval, which #176 ruled out as a new stored setting; or drop it, and say to raise free time only while laying out or going over a day, not at the start of a session. Proposal: drop it, with the "only while laying out or going over a day" rule. Going over a day again is a fair time to mention the free time again, and nothing needs to be stored.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-10-27: dropped, and the coordinator raises free time only while laying out or going over a day. It's done in PR #179, not in this issue, so this issue stays on the evaluation.
- Does a pass on Moab Day 4 accept a suggestion to check in first? Added on 2026-10-27 by #169's PR. #169 adds a check-in: a stop at the stay where the party sleeps that night. Its coordinator guidance says that when a day has a stop after the party reaches the stay's town, such as Moab Day 4's stargazing at 1 a.m., the coordinator suggests checking in first, and raises the long evening after it, with dinner or a longer check-in visit time. So on Moab Day 4 the reply may offer "check in at the Torrey hotel, then dinner" rather than the choices above. Proposal: a suggestion to check in first counts as a way to fill the evening, and the saved trip check also fails if a check-in was added without the user agreeing.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the coordinator's instructions as #176 leaves them. Record the results in this issue.
- If runs fail, change the coordinator's free time guidance in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2, and run the evaluation again. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change. Record the results before and after in the PR.

## Done when

- The results are recorded, with how many runs passed. If the guidance changed, the results before and after are both recorded.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Free time: the coordinator suggests ways to use it, checked with an evaluation

body:
## Why

#60 adds the first worker, the stay researcher. A **worker** is a subagent the coordinator starts with its `Agent` tool (technical spec section 6). Several of #60's open questions are about what Agent SDK 0.3.301 does, not design choices. This spike answers them in a small project of its own, outside the app. So #60 starts with a pattern that's known to work, and a short example to follow.

The pattern proposed for #60's first open question, on 2026-10-27:

- **The worker's result goes through a tool.** The worker ends by calling a tool, such as `report_result`, whose input schema holds the problems it found and its questions for the user. Its candidates already go through the candidate tools. A `SubagentStop` hook refuses to let the worker finish until it has called it. A `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` then replaces the worker's last message with a result code builds: the candidate lines from the worker's candidate tool calls, plus its problems and questions. So no free text from the worker reaches the coordinator.
- **The worker reads its brief's facts from code.** The `Agent` tool takes only a free-text prompt, so the worker brief (technical spec 5.3) can't have a schema. Most of it is facts code already has: dates, nights, each stop's purpose, set time, and tier, the day's other stops, and the candidates already offered. A worker tool returns those for the stay and stops in its brief. The coordinator writes only what needs its judgment: which stay and stops, roughly when each stop falls, the interests that apply, and what to avoid.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 5.3 (worker briefs) and 6 (workers).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 3 (which agent gets which tool).
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 6 (the `TranscriptAdapter`, for the SDK's `sessionStore` option) and 7 (a restart in the middle of a turn).
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.7: what #136 found about workers, including that they run in the background unless the coordinator says not to.
- The SDK's types for 0.3.301, in `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts`: `AgentDefinition`, the `SubagentStop` and `PostToolUse` hook types, and `AgentInput` in `sdk-tools.d.ts`.
- The SDK docs: [Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) and [Hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), the `SubagentStop` and "PostToolUse decision control" sections. The hooks page says a `SubagentStop` hook that blocks "keeps the subagent running and delivers reason to the subagent as its next instruction", and that `updatedToolOutput` "replaces the tool's result" and "must match the tool's output shape".

## Open questions

None of its own. The checks below answer the SDK side of #60's open questions on the worker brief and result, on resuming after a cut-off worker, on background workers, and on how workers get their place searches. #60 settles them, from what this spike finds.

## Do

Build the spike in `scratch/worker-spike/`. `scratch/` is gitignored, so the code never reaches the repo, and it doesn't need to pass `npm run check`. What the next session needs goes in the research doc.

When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

- **Set up a small TypeScript project** with `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` pinned to exactly 0.3.301, the app's version. Sign in to Claude the same way the app does. Give it a coordinator with a short system prompt, on the app's coordinator model (`claude-opus-5-5`), and one worker, on `claude-haiku-5-5`. Give the worker a few fake in-process tools that keep their state in memory: a read of its brief's facts, an add tool that takes a stop ID and one to three items, and `report_result`. No trip data, Postgres, or Google.
- **The result pattern.** Add the `SubagentStop` hook and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent`, as in the pattern above. Show:
  - that a worker that tries to finish without calling `report_result` is sent back, and then calls it.
  - the output shape `updatedToolOutput` needs for `Agent`, and that the coordinator sees only the replaced result.
  - how code ties each worker's tool calls to its own `Agent` call, so it can build that worker's result. Check this with two workers running at once.
- **Workers in the foreground.** With two workers sent in one turn, find the setting that keeps both in the foreground, so the coordinator's turn waits for both, and the SDK starts no second turn on its own. Try the definition's `background: false`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` in the Claude Code process's environment. Say whether the two still run at the same time.
- **Each worker's own tools.** Give the worker its own in-process MCP server through its definition's `mcpServers`. Show which tools the coordinator sees, and that it can't call the worker's. Show that the worker doesn't see the coordinator's own tools, or only the ones its `tools` list names.
- **Only our own workers.** Make the `Agent` tool offer only our worker. The SDK docs name `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` for the built-in agents, and an `Agent(fork)` deny rule for forks. Show what the tool's description lists, and what happens when the coordinator is asked to start `general-purpose`, `Explore`, `Plan`, `claude`, or `fork`.
- **Resume after a cut-off worker.** Give the spike a `sessionStore` that writes each line to a file, so a resume takes the same path as the app's `TranscriptAdapter` (persistence design section 6). Stop the process while a worker is running, after it has called a tool. Then resume the session with a new message. Say whether the resume works, and what the coordinator sees for the unfinished `Agent` call. If it doesn't work, try leaving the unfinished lines out of what the store hands back, and say which lines those are.
- **Write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`,** as a new section under Results, after section 2.7. Give each answer with the output that shows it, and a short code example of the pattern that works, with the hooks and the agent definition. Then say, for each of #60's open questions above, what the spike found, so #60 can settle it.

## Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it, and a code example of the working pattern.

## Ends in

A PR with the research doc change.

## Settled in

The PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
title: Spike: worker brief, result, and tools in the Agent SDK

body:
## Why

Today a budget tier is a **target**. The coordinator turns the user's budget rules into a tier, value, mid-range, or posh, for each stay's lodging and each meal stop, and stores it with the rule that produced it. A worker then searches at that tier, and code copies the tier onto each candidate (technical spec section 9). Real budget rules don't fit three boxes. On Joe's Natick to Bar Harbor trip (session `session_5hf47qpn`), the budget rules were:

> "Meals: upscale or posh, we are foodies and willing to splurge on good food, especially lobster when we are in Maine. Something mid-tier for the hotel in Bar Harbor. OK to do upscale for hotel in Camden and Portland, a B&B could be a good option in one of them."

The coordinator stored posh, with the rule "meals upscale or posh", on every meal stop, the 7 a.m. coffee stops included. It stored "upscale hotel or B&B" as the rule for both Camden and Portland. Each of those lost what the user meant:

- "Foodies willing to splurge on good food" is about quality, not how fancy a place is. The best lobster roll in Maine likely comes from a shack with counter service, which is value. A worker told to search at posh would skip it.
- What the coffee stops need is good espresso, open by 7 a.m. A tier says neither.
- "A B&B could be a good option in one of them" became a B&B target for both stays.

So the tier becomes a **label**: what a place is like, judged by the worker for each candidate and shown on its card. What a worker aims for comes from the user's own words in its worker brief. The budget item goes too. That text was really two things: how the user likes to eat, spending included, and what they want from places to stay. So it becomes a **lodging preferences** item, beside meal preferences. That drops the stored target tiers and their rules, which are mostly deterministic code with fiddly rules, and keeps the part that shows agent behavior: reading the user's messy budget words. Decided by Joe in chat on 2026-10-27, while settling #60's open question on budget tiers.

The top tier is also renamed from posh to **upscale**, the word users say. Otherwise the user, the cards, and the coordinator's tools would use two names for one tier, and the trace would too.

## Decided

Decided by Joe in chat on 2026-10-27:

- **A tier says what a place is like,** not how it compares with its neighbors. Value is simple and clean: a budget chain motel, such as a Super 8, or a basic independent motel; counter service, a diner, or a food truck. Mid-range is comfortable, with more service: a mainstream chain hotel, such as a Hampton Inn or a Courtyard, or a well-reviewed independent inn; a typical sit-down restaurant. Upscale: a boutique hotel, a resort, or a top-rated inn or B&B; a chef-driven restaurant where a reservation is wise. For restaurants, Google's price level is a guide, not a rule: $ usually means value, $$ mid-range, $$$ or more upscale. When it's missing, or disagrees with what the place is like, the description decides.
- **Each lodging and meal candidate a worker finds carries its own tier,** judged by the worker. The card shows it. A place the user names has none, and its card shows "your choice", as now. Attractions have no tier, as now. #60 adds the worker tools that take it: `add_lodging_candidates` and `add_stop_candidates`, with a required tier for each lodging or meal candidate.
- **Stays and meal stops no longer have a tier or a tier rule.** That removes: the tier and rule inputs on `add_stay`, `update_stay`, `add_stops`, and `update_stop`; the rule that every meal stop needs a tier; copying the tier onto candidates; "a tier already set isn't revisited"; and `select_candidate` changing the stop's or stay's tier.
- **The trip brief's budget item is replaced by a lodging preferences item.** `defaultTier` and `budgetRulesText` go away, and the trip brief gets `lodgingPreferencesText`: what the user wants from places to stay, in their words, required, like meal preferences. Spending on food goes in meal preferences. On the Bar Harbor trip, "foodies, willing to splurge on good food, especially lobster" is a meal preference, and "something mid-tier for the hotel in Bar Harbor, upscale OK in Camden and Portland, a B&B could be a good option in one of them" is a lodging preference. A preference for free activities goes in interests, since attractions have no tier. A total trip budget, such as "under $3,000", has no item: the app never shows prices (functional spec 7.1), so the coordinator says it can't plan to one. A lodging wish that comes up later in chat, after discovery, goes in trip memory, and a standing one in user memory, as usual.
- **"Higher tier" and "Lower tier" on a card become requests to the coordinator,** such as "something nicer than these." The coordinator reads the stop or stay, and sends a worker with that ask. Nothing is stored. The option cards aren't built yet, so only the docs change for them.
- **The worker brief carries the user's words that apply,** in place of a tier and a rule (technical spec 5.3): the meal or lodging preferences, the interests, and any trip or user memory that fits the stop or stay. The coordinator can add its own reading where a preference is clear, such as "the user wants mid-range for stays of 2+ nights, and this stay is 3 nights." It also keeps track of a wish that covers more than one stay. Example: "a B&B in one of them" goes to both the Camden and Portland researchers, until the user picks a B&B in one of the towns.
- **"Hotels only" means lodging businesses listed on Google,** B&Bs and inns included (functional spec 7.2). It rules out private rentals and campgrounds, which the user can still name (functional spec 7.6).

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md) 5.2 (the trip brief's items), 7.1 (budget tiers and rules), 7.2 (lodging), 7.5 (option cards), and scenario S6.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md) sections 2 (the decision that a worker gets a tier, never the rule text), 4.2 (the refine round), 5.2 (the coordinator's instructions on budget tiers), 5.3 (worker briefs), and 9 (budget tiers).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md): the trip brief, stay, stop, and candidate, and the services that set tiers. The tier comes up in about 45 places, including the class diagram and the example trips in section 5.
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md) 2.1, for the tools above, and what a read shows of a tier.
- `src/domain/tier.ts` holds the tiers, `TIERS`, and how people say each one, `TIER_WORDS`. `grep -rli tier src web/src` lists the code that uses them.

## Do

- Change the design docs above to the decisions. Don't change `plan/`, `research/`, or `reviews/`, which are records.
- Change the code to match: the domain objects and services, the tools and their input schemas, the itinerary reads, the persistence schemas, and the itinerary view's budget line. Rename the tier `posh` to `upscale`. Fix the tests and the fakes.
- Change the coordinator's prompt: the trip brief's items, and the stay and meal guidance on tiers. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- **No migration.** Saved trips start over instead. Joe decided on 2026-10-27 that the trips saved so far, his own test trips, aren't worth carrying over. Once the PR is merged and deployed, delete every trip, on the server and in the local database, so its transcripts, sessions, trip memory, and places go with it ([persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 6, which says what deleting a trip removes. `TripWriter.deleteTrip()` does it). User memory stays, since it isn't part of any trip. On 2026-10-27 the server had three trips: Natick to Bar Harbor, San Francisco to Los Angeles, and one with no focus yet. The Bar Harbor budget text is quoted above, so nothing this issue needs is lost.

## Done when

- `npm run check` passes.
- `grep -rni posh src design web/src` finds nothing.
- No trips are left on the server or in the local database, and a new trip can be started on the server.
- In a chat with the coordinator, it asks about lodging preferences in discovery, saves them and meal preferences in the user's words, and adds stays and meal stops with no tier.

## Ends in

A PR.

## Settled in

The PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
title: Budget tiers: a label on each place, not a target, and posh renamed upscale

body:
**Starts** once #53 and #60 are merged.

## Why

#184 makes a tier a label on each place, not a target, and #60 has the stay researcher give each lodging and meal candidate its tier: value, mid-range, or upscale (upscale is the tier #184 renames from posh). The card shows that tier, so a wrong one misleads the user. Example: a Super 8 shown as upscale. The tier is the worker's judgment, and Joe doesn't want to label hotels and restaurants by hand to make a list of right answers. So this evaluation checks whether the worker's tiers are consistent, which needs no hand labels, rather than whether each one is right.

## Decided

Decided by Joe on 2026-10-27, while settling #60's open question on budget tiers:

- **The checks score consistency, in code, with no judge model.**
  - **Price level.** A restaurant's tier agrees with its Google price level, where it has one: $ usually means value, $$ mid-range, $$$ or more upscale. #184 makes the price level a guide, not a rule, since the description can overrule it, such as a chef-driven place listed at $$. So mismatches are reported as a rate, not as failures.
  - **Order within a town.** In one stay's candidates, no upscale place has a lower price level than a value place.
  - **The same place gets the same tier** in every run where it's offered. This is the only check for hotels, since Google gives hotels no price level.
- **The user's "Higher tier" and "Lower tier" clicks aren't used.** They do show a tier that missed, but with Joe nearly the only user there are too few to measure.
- **The stay researcher runs on its own,** from a fixed worker brief, without the coordinator, so its tiers are all that's scored.

## Design
