- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md) 7.1 and [technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md) section 9, for what each tier means, once #184 is merged.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md) 5.3 and 6.1, for the worker brief and the stay researcher.
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- What's the brief? Proposal: the Moab stay from domain model 5.2, with the user's words asking for each tier, such as "a comfortable mid-range hotel", "a quick, cheap breakfast", and "a special dinner, we'll splurge". Moab has places at all three tiers, so the worker shouldn't need to fall back to the closest it finds.
- How many runs? Proposal: 5. Each run makes several searches, so 5 runs is about 50 Google searches, within the free tier.
- Should hotels get a second check, from a short list of chains with a known tier? Example: Super 8 and Motel 6 are value, and Hampton Inn and Courtyard are mid-range. A candidate from a listed chain at another tier fails. That labels a few brands by hand, not single places. Proposal: leave it out at first, and add it if the same-tier check shows hotels moving between tiers.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the stay researcher's instructions as #60 leaves them. Record the results in this issue.
- If the checks show a problem, change the tier guidance in the stay researcher's instructions, and run the evaluation again. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Record the results before and after in the PR.

## Done when

- The results are recorded, with each check's score. If the guidance changed, the results before and after are both recorded.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

body:
## Why

Each agent's view file, such as `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`, is meant to hold what its model sees on every turn (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). The spike in #182 logged the Messages API requests that Agent SDK 0.3.301 sends, and found text the view file doesn't show. With a custom `systemPrompt` string, as the app uses, the coordinator's first user message is followed by a block from Claude Code that starts with `# Environment`. It holds the working folder, whether it's a git repository, the platform, shell, and OS version, a rule about downloaded files and running Python with `-I`, the model's name and knowledge cutoff, the list of agent types for the `Agent` tool, and today's date. So the model reads instructions we didn't write, and a trace or a view file doesn't show them.

## Design

- DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, on view files.
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8 (once the #182 PR merges), which shows the agent-type list from this block.
- The SDK's `systemPrompt` option in `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts`, which documents `excludeDynamicSections` for the preset prompt only.

## Open questions

- ~~Is the block on the app's coordinator too, and on its workers? The spike ran outside the app, in a git repository. On the server the working folder is the container's.~~ Answered on 2026-10-27, in research section 2.9: yes. It's on the app's coordinator from the first turn of each session, and on every worker, and the same when the coordinator runs from an agent definition. On the server it says `/app`, not a git repository, and a date in UTC.
- ~~Can it be turned off, or cut down, with an SDK option or an environment variable? If not, should the view file show it?~~ Answered on 2026-10-27, in research section 2.9: no setting found turns it off and keeps the plan's sign-in. Whether the view file shows it moved to #194.
- ~~Does its date or its rules ever conflict with the coordinator's own instructions?~~ Answered on 2026-10-27, in research section 2.9: its date does. It's in the server's time zone, UTC, and the app's is at the trip's start place, so they differ each evening in the US. The rest doesn't conflict. How to handle it moved to #194.

## Do

- Log one coordinator turn's request in the app, as the #182 spike did, and record what the block holds.
- Answer the open questions, and propose a change if one is needed.

## Done when

- The open questions are answered, with the logged block.

## Ends in

A decision, or a PR.

## Settled in

Chat.
title: The Claude Code environment block in each agent's context

body:
## Why

#60 adds the first worker, the stay researcher, and #61 the leg scout. A **worker** is a subagent the coordinator starts with its `Agent` tool (technical spec section 6). #182's spike found how Agent SDK 0.3.301 passes work and results between the coordinator and a worker, and which settings and hooks hold each rule ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8). None of it is in the design docs yet. This issue writes it in, so #60 and #61 build from one design rather than from the research doc.

## Design

- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8: what the spike found, with its output and a code example of the pattern that works. Its code is in `worker-spike/` on the [`spike/worker-182`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/worker-182/worker-spike) branch, which never gets a PR. The branch's `worker-spike/README.md` says how to run each check.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 2 (each agent sees only its own tools), 5.3 (worker briefs), and 6 (workers).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1 (how tools are grouped into MCP servers), 3 (who gets which tool), and 4.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 6 (the `TranscriptAdapter`) and 7 (a restart in the middle of a turn).
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 2 (the server).
- DEVELOPMENT.md section 5: each agent's view file.

**Already settled,** on 2026-10-27 in PR #189, from what the spike found. Write these into the design docs as they are:

- **The worker's result goes through a tool.** The worker ends by calling `report_result`, whose input holds the problems it found and its questions for the user. Its candidates go through the candidate tools, saved to the stop or stay.
- **Hooks in our code hold the pattern.** A `PostToolUse` hook on the worker's tools records each call under the worker's `agent_id`. A `SubagentStop` hook sends back a worker that tries to finish without calling `report_result`, at most twice, and only for our worker types. A `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` replaces the worker's last message with a result code builds: one line per candidate from the recorded calls, plus the problems and questions. It returns the whole `Agent` output object with its `content` replaced, since a string is ignored. It acts only on our worker types. So no free text from the worker reaches the coordinator.
- **Every worker runs in the foreground.** `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` goes in the Claude Code process's environment. A background worker's own text reaches the coordinator in a task notification, which skips the hooks. Two workers still run at the same time.
- **The `Agent` tool offers only our workers.** `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` goes in the same environment. No `Agent(fork)` rule is needed.
- **Each worker's definition lists every tool it gets.** Left out, a worker gets the `Agent` tool and every tool the coordinator has.
- **A session resumes after a cut-off worker with no change to the transcript adapter.** The SDK adds a result saying the `Agent` call was interrupted and its outcome is unknown.

## Open questions

- **The worker brief: what goes in the `Agent` prompt, and what a worker tool reads from code?** The `Agent` tool takes only a free-text prompt, so the worker brief (technical spec 5.3) can't have a schema. The proposal from #182: most of the brief is facts code already has, such as the dates, nights, each stop's purpose, set time, and tier, the day's other stops, and the candidates already offered. A worker tool returns those for the stay, day, and stops in its brief. The coordinator writes only what needs its judgment: which stay or day and stops, roughly when each stop falls, the user's words that apply, and what to avoid. Settle the tool's name, input, and return, and which items of 5.3 stay in the prompt. Moved from #60.
- **What `report_result` takes, and the exact text the `Agent` hook builds.** Example from the spike: one line per candidate, as `stop ID: place name (tier)`, then a line of problems and a line of questions. Technical spec 6.1 and 6.2 say what each worker returns. Moved from #60.
- **How a worker gets its own tools.** An in-process MCP server can only go in the query's own `mcpServers`, and everything there is the coordinator's too (research section 2.8). Only a server Claude Code reaches over a connection, such as HTTP, can go in one worker's definition. Proposed on 2026-10-27, to weigh:

  > One HTTP listener in the app's process, on 127.0.0.1, serves every session's worker tools. When a turn starts, the app makes a random key, and keeps it in memory with that turn's trip and session. Each worker's definition is built for the turn, and sends the key in `headers` with every call: `{ type: "http", url, headers: { Authorization: "Bearer <key>" } }`. On each request, the listener looks up the key, builds the worker's MCP server for that trip with `createSdkMcpServer()`, as the coordinator's servers are built today, and handles the request. A missing or unknown key gets a 401. When the turn ends, the key is deleted. So two users' workers reach servers built for their own trips, and another process on the server can't call the tools without a live key. If a server ever needs to know which worker type is calling, each definition can get its own key.
  >
  > A stdio server would also keep users apart, one process per turn, but it's a separate program. It can't use the app's Postgres pool, writers, readers, and settings, and it starts a new process each time. The other choice is an in-process server on the query, with a `PreToolUse` hook that refuses any call with no `agent_id`. That's less code, but the coordinator sees the worker's tools and pays for their descriptions on every call, and it breaks technical spec section 2's rule that each agent sees only its own tools.

  Settle where the worker tools' servers go, how a request is tied to its trip, and how tool design section 1 groups the workers' tools, such as `find_place` and `search_near` for the stay researcher. Moved from #60, where it was the question of how workers get `search_near` and `search_along_leg`.
- **Do workers get the built-in `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`?** Both workers need web search (tool design section 3). The coordinator's `tools` option is `["Agent"]`, which sets the built-in tools for the session. The spike gave its worker no built-in tools, so it didn't check whether a worker can still get one by naming it in its definition. If it can't, the design changes, so check it first.
- **Does the key reach the server on every call?** The HTTP config in 0.3.301 takes `headers`, but the spike sent none.

## Do

- Run the two checks above with the spike on the `spike/worker-182` branch. Push any change to its code to that branch, and add the results to research section 2.8.
- Settle each open question.
- Write the design in: the settled items above, and each answer. Technical spec section 6 for how a worker is started, its brief, its result, and the hooks. Tool design sections 1 and 3 for the workers' servers and tools. Persistence design section 7 for the resume. Systems design section 2 if the app gets a listener. Say each worker's view file in DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 if it needs anything new, such as the tools on its HTTP server.
- Change #60 and #61 so they build from the design.

## Done when

- The design docs say how a worker is started, what its brief and result hold, which hooks and settings hold the pattern, how it gets its own tools, and how a request reaches the right trip.
- Research section 2.8 has the results of the two checks.
- #60 and #61 point to the design sections they build from.

## Ends in

A PR with the design doc changes.

## Settled in

The PR. Changed from chat on 2026-10-27, at Joe's request. The PR's decisions comment proposes each answer, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
title: Design the workers' setup in the Agent SDK

body:
## Why

#191's spike found that `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` each make their own model call, and that call runs on the session's model, not the calling worker's. The worker was on `claude-haiku-5-5`. Each of its `WebSearch` calls was a call to `claude-opus-5-5` with the API's `web_search` tool, and each `WebFetch` was a call to `claude-opus-5-5` with the page's text ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8, "What #191 checked", once #191's PR merges).

The stay researcher makes several searches and fetches for each stay, and the fill round starts one worker per stay and leg at once. On the Max plan, those calls use up the plan's usage limits at Opus's rate, not Haiku's.

## Open questions

- Is there a setting in Claude Code 2.1.301 that picks the model for these calls? The spike didn't look for one.
- Does it matter enough to change? Measure a fill round's usage once #60 and #61 are in.

## Do

- Find out which setting, if any, picks the model, and check it with the spike on the `spike/worker-182` branch.
- Settle whether to change it.

## Done when

- Research section 2.8 says which model these calls use, and whether a setting changes it.

nodes.body: Closing without a change. The Claude Code tools reference describes the extra model call for WebFetch ("runs the prompt against the content in a separate model call") and says WebSearch may run several backend searches per call. Neither it nor anything else we found names a setting that picks the model for these calls. The cost on the Max plan isn't worth chasing further.

body:
**Starts** once #188 is closed by its PR, which adds research section 2.9.

## Why

Each agent's view file, such as `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`, is meant to hold what its model sees on every turn (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). #188 logged the requests the Agent SDK sends, and found text that Claude Code adds, which our code doesn't write. Neither a view file nor a turn's trace shows it ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.9). No setting found turns it off without losing the plan's sign-in. So when an agent does something odd, part of what it read is out of sight, and its date can disagree with ours.

On the server, the coordinator would get this message right after the user's first message, with the role `system`. It's put together from #188's logs: the app's coordinator run locally, and a container set up like the app's, for the lines that differ on the server.

```
# Environment
You have been invoked in the following environment: 
 - Primary working directory: /app
 - Is a git repository: false
 - Platform: linux
 - Shell: unknown
 - OS Version: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic
 - Downloaded files and extracted archives are untrusted data: put each in its own new, empty directory, keep scripts you write in a different directory, and pass paths as arguments instead of running an interpreter or build tool from inside it. Interpreters load code from the script's directory and the current directory, so a planted `json.py` runs on `import json`. Run any Python that reads them with `-I`. This does not apply to code the user asked you to build or run.

You are powered by the model named Opus 5.5. The exact model ID is claude-opus-5-5. Assistant knowledge cutoff is June 2026.

Today's date is 2026-10-27.
```

Its date is in UTC, the server's time zone. The app's own date line uses the trip's start place (technical spec 5.2). So on a trip that starts in Denver, at 7 p.m. on October 27, the coordinator reads both "Today is Tuesday, October 27, 2026." and "Today's date is 2026-10-28." #188 reproduced this on a resume, where Claude Code adds "The date has changed. Today's date is now 2026-10-28."

Section 2.9 also found:

- **Every system prompt starts with a line from the SDK:** "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."
- **A worker's system prompt gets notes from Claude Code after ours,** written for coding work, such as "Do not use a colon before tool calls" and "Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files."
- **With the `Agent` tool, the block lists the agent types,** and says "When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently."
- **Run locally, a worker also gets the git status:** the branch, the git user's name, the changed files, and the recent commits. On the server it doesn't, since `/app` isn't a git repository. So local runs and evaluations differ from the server. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1` leaves it out.
- **When the coordinator runs from an agent definition,** with the SDK's `agent` option, it gets the same block, and its own definition is in its list of agent types. It has run that way since b9d28af.

A turn's trace has gaps of its own (systems design section 10). It shows the coordinator's model and tool names, in the `started` event on `coordinator.turn`. It doesn't show any system prompt, Claude Code's added text, or the tools a worker was given. So a trace doesn't show the whole of what an agent read.

## Design

- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.9: each block as logged, and the settings that were tried. The scripts are in the gitignored `scratch/`, so they aren't in the repo, but the section says what each one set.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2: the lines the app adds, including "Today is".
- `src/agent/app-lines.ts` and `src/domain/today.ts`: how the app's date line is built.
- DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, on view files, and `src/agent/agent-views.test.ts`, which builds them.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 10: what a trace holds, and `src/agent/turn-trace.ts`, `src/agent/trace-spans.ts`, and `src/agent/worker-trace.ts`, which make it.
- #191, the workers' design, which may take the worker items below.

## Open questions

- ~~**How do the app's date and Claude Code's come to agree?**~~ Settled: on each turn, set `TZ` in the Claude Code process's environment to the time zone the app's date uses, the start place's, or UTC until there is one. Each turn starts its own process, and #188 found that `TZ` sets Claude Code's date. The app's own line stays as it is, since Claude Code's has no weekday, and the weekday matters for things like opening hours.
- ~~**What should each view file show of Claude Code's text?**~~ Settled: a note at the top of each view file, next to the line that says `npm run agent-views` wrote it. The note says the file leaves out text Claude Code adds, lists the three parts with an example of each (the SDK's first line of the system prompt, the environment block after the user's first message, and a worker's notes after its prompt), and links to research section 2.9. It's a reminder for when an agent does something odd. No copy of the text, since what Claude Code adds is harmless apart from the date, which the first question settles.
- ~~**Should workers run with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1`,** so a local run matches the server?~~ Settled: yes. `claudeProcessEnv()` sets it for every Claude Code process the app starts. Workers run inside the coordinator's process, so it covers them, and on the server it changes nothing. Local runs and evaluations then match the server.
- ~~**Do Claude Code's notes to workers, or its line about starting agents in one message, conflict with our instructions?**~~ Settled: the line about starting agents in one message matches technical spec section 1, where workers run in parallel. One worker note pulls against `report_result`: "Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create." The stay researcher's instructions already answer it, by saying nobody reads its own messages. #61 now says the leg scout's instructions do the same. #191 closed without taking this up.
- ~~**Does it matter that the coordinator is offered itself as a worker?**~~ Settled: no, and nothing changes. A later spike (research section 2.8) found that the coordinator's `Agent(stay-researcher)` entry limits what it's told about and what it can start. It refused a coordinator with "Agent type 'coordinator' not found. Available agents: stay-researcher". #61 adds `leg-scout` to that entry, and a second type didn't change this in the spike.
- ~~**Should a turn's trace show each agent's system prompt?**~~ Settled: no, it shows the app's commit instead. Each `coordinator.turn` span gets the git SHA of the code that ran, as an attribute. The view files at that commit show every agent's system prompt and tools, and `settings.json` is committed, so the SHA covers its numbers too. It goes on the turn, not the session, since a deploy can land partway through a session. A worker's spans are under its turn, so the turn's SHA covers them. On the server, the SHA comes from the deploy, which already tags each image with it. Locally, the app asks git when it starts, and adds `-dirty` when there are uncommitted changes, so the trace says the view file at that commit may not match. The full text was the first answer, but a view file reads better than a span attribute, and one value covers both prompts and tools. Phoenix's prompt registry is left to #53, as one of its open questions.
- ~~**Should a turn's trace show Claude Code's added text?**~~ Settled: no. On the server the block is fixed apart from the model, which the `started` event shows, and the date, which now matches the app's "Today is" line in the turn's input. Copying it from the transcript's `attachment` lines would mean reading lines whose shape the SDK doesn't document, for text the trace mostly has. The view file note is the reminder, and the logging proxy from #188 shows the exact request if it's ever needed.
- ~~**Should a worker's span list the tools it was given,** as the coordinator's `started` event does? And should either list hold each tool's description and input schema, not only its name?~~ Settled: no. The turn's commit SHA, from the question above, points to the view files, which list each agent's tools with their descriptions and input schemas.

## Do

- Settle each open question.
- Make each change: the app's date line and the coordinator's instructions, technical spec 5.2, the view files and DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, the Claude Code process's environment, and the traces and systems design section 10.
- Rewrite each changed view file with `npm run agent-views`.

## Done when

- Each open question is answered, and its answer is written into the doc it belongs to.
- The coordinator never reads two different dates for today.
- Each turn's span holds the commit SHA of the code that ran, with `-dirty` on a local run with uncommitted changes.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

## Settled in

Chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

Today the coordinator is sent every tool on our MCP servers that `allowedTools` lets it use. Workers will need tools on the same servers that the coordinator must not see, such as `search_near` on the `places` server. Running the coordinator as a named agent splits the two: the query's options say which tools exist in the session, and the coordinator's definition says which ones it's sent (technical spec 6.5). This is the one part of the worker setup that changes how the app runs today, so it's checked on its own, before any worker exists.

body:
**Starts** once #197 is merged.

## Why

Every worker is started and ends the same way, so this builds that once, before the first worker (#60). The coordinator starts a worker with the SDK's `Agent` tool. The worker ends by calling `report_result` with its problems and its questions for the user. Hooks record the worker's calls, and replace its last message with a result that code builds, so no free text from a worker reaches the coordinator (technical spec 6.5). It waits for #197, since until the coordinator runs as a named agent, it would be sent the worker tools this adds.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 6.5 (the settings, `report_result`, the three hooks, and the result's lines).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1 (the `worker` server), 2.3 (`search_near` and `search_along_leg`), 2.6 (`report_result`), 3, and 4.
- [Research doc](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8, for what was checked against Agent SDK 0.3.301, and the spike code on the [`spike/worker-182`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/worker-182/worker-spike) branch.

## Open questions

- ~~**What should the query's `allowedTools` list, now that the definitions set what each agent is sent?** `allowedTools` lets a tool run without asking, and with `permissionMode: "dontAsk"` any other tool call is refused. It applies to the whole session, workers too. Today (after #197) it allows `mcp__trip`, `mcp__memory`, `mcp__routing`, and only `find_place` and `read_place` on the `places` server. So a worker's call to `search_near`, `search_along_leg`, or `report_result` would be refused, and `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` aren't allowed either. One choice is to allow each whole server, plus the three built-in tools, since the definitions now keep each agent to its own tools (technical spec 6.5). The other is to name every tool one by one.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** allow each whole server, plus `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` by name. The list covers the whole session, so it can't let a worker call a tool and refuse the coordinator the same tool. Only the definitions can do that. And every tool in the session belongs to some agent, since the query's `tools` and `strictMcpConfig` keep out everything else. So a tool-by-tool list would always end up as every tool in the session, kept by hand as a second copy of the definitions. When that copy falls behind, a worker's call is refused, and the trace looks like an agent problem when it's an app bug. `allowedTools` now only lets our tools run without a prompt, and the definitions decide who gets which tool. Write it into technical spec 6.5.

## Do

- Add `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` to the query's `tools`. Only worker definitions list the web tools, so the coordinator isn't sent them (tool design section 1).
- Add the two settings to the Claude Code process's environment: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` and `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` (technical spec 6.5).
- Add the `worker` server with `report_result` (tool design 2.6), built for each turn like the other servers, and add it to the query's `mcpServers`.
- Put `search_near` and `search_along_leg` on the `places` server. The coordinator's definition doesn't list them, so it isn't sent them.
- Set the query's `allowedTools` to each of our servers, plus `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch`, and write the reason into technical spec 6.5 (see the settled question above).
- Add the three hooks from technical spec 6.5: the `PostToolUse` hook that records each worker's calls by `agent_id`, the `SubagentStop` hook that sends a worker back at most twice when it hasn't called `report_result`, and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` that replaces the worker's last message with the result code builds. Each acts only for our worker types (technical spec section 1).
- Draft the result's wording (technical spec 6.5), for Joe to review in the PR.

## Done when

- Tests with fake SDK messages show the `Agent` hook builds each kind of result: candidate replies in call order, a "No candidates added for:" line, a "No weather saved for:" line, problems and questions or "none", the last `report_result` call counting when there are two, and the line for a worker that stopped without reporting.
- Tests show the `SubagentStop` hook sends a worker back at most twice, and ignores agent types that aren't our workers.
- The coordinator's view file still shows no worker tool, such as `search_near` or `report_result`.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
