title: The leg scout checks its Atlas Obscura finds, without digging too deep, checked with an evaluation

body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

Each waypoint carries a reason, in the coordinator's own words, such as "steer onto US-1", "must-see: Capitol Reef", or "the user asked: the Golden Gate Bridge" (domain model 3.6). #166 added it. The reason shows in every itinerary read, and in the replies of `set_waypoints` and `update_day` (tool design 2.1). It has two readers:

- **The coordinator.** When the user approves fastest on a day, code clears all of the day's waypoints, and `update_day`'s reply lists each one with its reason. The coordinator puts back the ones for a must-see or the user's request, and drops the ones that only kept the drive on a scenic road (technical spec 5.2). In a later session, the reason is the only record of why a waypoint is there.
- **A person reading the itinerary,** who can spot a bad pick without opening a trace. Example: the Pulgas Water Temple waypoint (#163) would have read "steer onto I-280", though the temple sits off I-280.

The reason was added on reasoning, not measured. It costs context in every read, a few words per waypoint, on every turn. Nobody knows yet whether the coordinator uses it well, or whether it would do as well without it. An evaluation should show whether the reasons earn their place, and if not, what to change.

There's also a design choice to weigh. The design names exactly three kinds of reason: a scenic road, a must-see, and the user's request. A set fixed by the design could be an enum on the waypoint, beside the free text. Then code could clear only the scenic waypoints when fastest is approved, and the coordinator's put-back step would go away. Today code clears them all "because a reason is the coordinator's own words, which code can't sort" (technical spec 5.2).

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), 4.2 (how a waypoint is picked) and 5.2 (approving fastest).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), 3.6 (Day: waypoints), 4.5 (`DaysService.approveRouteType()`), and 4.7 (how a leg is routed).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), 2.1: `set_waypoints`, `update_day`, and `read_itinerary`.
- #163 and #166, for how reasons came about, with the traces that showed the problem.
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- What does the evaluation measure? Proposal: whether, after the user approves fastest on a day in a new session, the coordinator puts back exactly the must-see and user-asked waypoints, and drops the scenic ones. Code scores it from what was saved. A second question, whether having to write a reason leads to better picks (a place on the road, not a sight beside it), needs a judge or a road-time rule, so it waits until the first results show whether reasons matter.
- What's the comparison? Proposal: run the case as the design stands, then with the reasons left out of `update_day`'s reply and the reads. If the coordinator keeps the right waypoints just as well without them, the reasons serve only people, and could be stored but not shown to the model.
- Is the reason-kind enum tried here? Proposal: decide after the first results. If the coordinator often keeps or drops the wrong waypoints, the enum lets code do it instead.
- How many runs? Proposal: 5 for each variant.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, with a trip whose day has one scenic waypoint, one for a must-see, and one the user asked for. Run it as the design stands, and with the reasons hidden. Record the results in this issue.
- Look at the results and traces with Joe, and decide: keep the reasons as they are, keep them but hide them from the model, or add the enum. If the design changes, the implementer drafts the change, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Done when

- The results are recorded for each variant.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A decision, or a PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
title: Waypoint reasons: who they're for, checked with an evaluation

body:
## Why

The coordinator asks for comfortable driving hours and rest days during discovery, before the trip has a shape. On a short trip, the answer often doesn't matter yet, and the user has nothing to judge it against until they see each day's drive. So the question feels out of place, and asking it again each turn makes that worse. The answer starts to matter once a day's drive gets long, which the sketches' road times and the daily driving check (technical spec 8) show.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip is a 4-day loop from Natick, MA to Bar Harbor, with one long drive up on Day 1 and short drives home.

- The coordinator asked about driving hours, scenic or fastest, and a day with no driving in turns 1, 2, 3, and 4. Joe left them unanswered on purpose. It didn't hold up the plan to get an answer, which was better than in earlier sessions.
- In turn 5 the user said: "our longest drive is going to be [Natick] to Bar Harbor, and that's fine. So that's like, you know, we expected a kind of long day that day. The rest are shorter. [...] So I think we're good on driving."

Joe's read: on this trip the answer should have been worked out from the plan, not asked up front. By turn 4 the user had seen the sketches and agreed to the route with each day's drive time, so asking for hours was only ticking a box. It's the second session where the question felt unnatural. The coordinator also asked about rest days four times, and then dropped it. Asking again and again, then giving up, isn't a good way to find the answer. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

- In turn 12 the user picked Pemaquid Point for Saturday, knowing it added about an hour. Saturday became 5 h 36 m of driving with the drive buffer (turn span `a524f4d65cf4c50d`). The coordinator said "That's about 5½ hours of driving with breaks, a long day but under your 6." The 6 was the number it set itself in turn 5 to cover Day 1 (see #167). The user never said 6 hours was normal, and had expected the days home to be about 3½ to 4 hours. Under a 4-hour default, Saturday would have warned, and the coordinator would have asked whether 5½ hours is OK.

#167 is about what to set once the user answers vaguely. This issue is about when to ask.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 5.2: comfortable driving hours is required, and rest days aren't.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's instructions for the trip brief and comfortable driving hours), section 8 (a check that compares against a trip brief item is skipped while that item is empty), and section 10 (the recommended daily driving, 6 hours).

## Open questions

- ~~How does the coordinator find out the comfortable driving hours? Joe's idea: never suggest a day over 6 hours of driving on its own. When a day goes over 4 hours, ask the user whether that's OK, and whether it's a normal amount for them. If they want 8 or 10 hours, that's fine, up to the maximum of 12. So it comes up only when a day needs it. Proposal: make 4 hours the default for comfortable driving hours, as 8:00 a.m. is for the usual start time. The daily driving check then runs from the start, and its warning on a day over 4 hours is the cue to ask. A yes approves that day (as in #167), or raises the default when it's normal for them. The recommended daily driving, 6 hours, becomes the most the coordinator suggests without the user asking. On this trip, the user would have been asked twice: about Day 1's 5½ hours, and about Saturday's 5½ hours once Pemaquid Point was added.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat, as proposed:
  - Comfortable driving hours starts at 4 hours, as the usual start time starts at 8:00 a.m. The 4 is a new setting in technical spec section 10, the default comfortable driving hours. The trip brief shows it as the default until the user says otherwise.
  - So the daily driving check runs from the start. Its warning on a day over the comfortable driving hours is the coordinator's cue to ask whether that day is OK, and whether that much driving is normal for the user.
  - "That day is fine" gives the day a drive hours approval. "That's normal for us" raises the trip brief's comfortable driving hours, and is saved to user memory as a standing preference.
  - The coordinator never suggests a day over the recommended daily driving, 6 hours, on its own. The user can ask for more, up to the maximum daily driving, 12 hours.
  - The coordinator doesn't ask about driving hours during discovery.
- ~~Should rest days leave the trip brief? Joe's idea: they should come up in the conversation when they fit, not as a question every trip gets. The trip brief acts as a checklist the coordinator works through. On a 5-night trip with 5 stays, asking for a day with no driving makes no sense. Proposal: remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief. A wish such as "one day off in Moab" goes in trip memory. Marking a day as a rest day with `update_day` stays as it is.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat, as proposed:
  - Remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief: the domain code, `update_trip_brief`'s input, the coordinator's instructions, and the saved form.
  - A wish such as "one day off in Moab" goes to trip memory, like any other wish for this trip. A standing habit, such as "we always take a day off mid-trip", goes to user memory.
  - Marking a day as a rest day with `update_day` stays as it is.
  - The coordinator offers a rest day only when the trip calls for one: a trip of about a week or more, or several long driving days in a row. Otherwise it comes up only when the user raises it.
  - Every saved trip holds `restDaysText`, empty or not, and the saved form is checked strictly, so a one-line migration removes the key from every saved trip, as `migrations/0008_drop_stay_tier_nights.sql` did. Nothing is carried over: the one trip Joe cares about, Bar Harbor, has no rest days.

## Do

- Change functional spec 5.2, technical spec 5.2 and 10, and the domain model to match the answers. Remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief's code, its tool input, and its saved form.
- Add a migration that removes `restDaysText` from the trip brief in every saved trip's plan, as `migrations/0008_drop_stay_tier_nights.sql` does for its keys.
- Add the default comfortable driving hours setting, 4 hours, to the settings and technical spec section 10. A new trip's trip brief starts with it, as it starts with the usual start time.
- **Ask first the questions the trip sketches need.** In turn 1, the coordinator's reply asked 7 numbered questions, though the instructions say "Ask a few questions at a time." Joe answered the ones the sketches needed, and the sketches in turn 2 came out well. Have the coordinator ask first the few questions it needs to offer the trip sketches, and the rest later. Raised by Joe. Moved here from #231 on 2026-10-30, since it also decides which questions discovery asks, and when. Write it together with dropping driving hours and rest days from discovery, so the two read as one rule.
- Change the coordinator's instructions in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and the `update_trip_brief` description if the default changes what it says. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- The coordinator's instructions say when to raise driving hours and rest days, and to ask first the questions the trip sketches need. The design docs match.
- A trip saved before the change loads after `npm run migrate`, run locally.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Ask about driving hours and rest days only once they matter

body:
## Why

Joe planned a whole trip on the live site on 2026-10-30, and then went through it turn by turn. Some of what came up are clear gaps in the agents' instructions, with a fix small enough to make without an evaluation first (unlike, say, #209). This issue collects them, so they go in together in one PR. Add to it as the rest of the session is reviewed.

The session: Joe's Bar Harbor trip, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip is a 4-day loop from Natick, MA to an alumni event at College of the Atlantic in Bar Harbor, and a slow drive home down the Maine coast through Portland.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's instructions), and the stay researcher's instructions.

## Do

- **Say why each town in a trip sketch fits this user.** In turn 2, Camden was in both sketches, and the only reason given was "one of Maine's prettiest harbor towns." Joe rated the turn down: "Route includes stay or stop in Camden, but doesn't mention why we would consider it. hard to choose the two options it laid out since we don't know anything about Camden." The instructions ask for "a few sentences on why someone would pick it", which the model read as a line per sketch. Have each sketch say why each town on its path fits the user, not only why the sketch as a whole does. Raised by Joe.
- **Say when a place the user agreed to was the coordinator's suggestion.** In turn 2 and turn 3, the coordinator's own sketches named Portland Head Light. In turn 4 the user agreed to the plan, and the coordinator selected the lighthouse with `select_user_place`, with the reason "lighthouses, quintessential Maine; on the way out of Portland." The stop now reads "Named by the user", though the user never named it. Asked later why it was picked, the coordinator could tell the user they chose it. Selecting it this way is fine, and Joe was happy with the pick. But the reason should say it was the coordinator's suggestion, such as "suggested in the plan; the user agreed." Raised by Joe.

- **Let breakfast and coffee stops in one town share places.** In turn 5, one stay researcher filled both Bar Harbor breakfast stops, "espresso and a café breakfast" on Friday and Saturday. Its instructions say "When you fill several meals, give each its own places, since a party rarely eats at the same place twice. Offer a place for two meals only when too few places fit, and then report it as a problem." Only two downtown cafés opened at 7:00, Choco-Latte Cafe and The Early Bite. It gave both to Friday, and Saturday got places that open at 7:30. It reported: "Choco-Latte and Early Bite open at 7:00 but were used for Day 2." Change the stay researcher's instructions so that for breakfast or coffee stops in the same town, offering the same places on each day is fine, and better when few places fit the hours. Lunches and dinners keep their own places. Raised by Joe.
- **Check the same kind of stop on the stay's other days before saying what the options allow.** In turn 12, the coordinator looked only at Saturday's breakfast candidates, told the user "your days usually start at 7, but the Bar Harbor cafés don't open until 7:30", and offered to start Saturday at 7:30. Two of Friday's candidates opened at 7:00. The user caught it in turn 13, and from there the coordinator handled it well, offering Friday's cafés for Saturday too. Add to the coordinator's instructions: before telling the user what a stop's options allow, check the same kind of stop on the stay's other days, since a place offered for one day can be picked for another with select_user_place. Raised by Joe.

- **Tell the user when two stops are a short walk apart.** In turn 15, the coordinator read Sunrise Cafe's place and its thinking said: "It's also at 1 West St, the same address as the whale watch dock, which could suit Friday." The reply left it out. The schedule shows every move between places as a drive, so the user saw a drive and free time between the café and the boat (turn 23). In turn 6 it also told the user they'd drive from the Highbrook Motel (94 Eden St) to the event at College of the Atlantic (105 Eden St), which is across the street. Showing walks in the schedule would mean tracking where the car is, so it stays out. Add to the coordinator's instructions: when two stops, or a stop and the lodging, are at the same address or a short walk apart, tell the user, and say the schedule shows it as a short drive. Raised by Joe.

- **Let a meal take a set time at the user's usual time for it.** In turn 18, the user picked Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound for Friday's dinner, and the coordinator gave it a set time of 6:00, "your usual dinner time", which user memory holds. The rule says: "Give a stop a set time only when it's fixed at that time, such as a dinner reservation or a sunrise hike. Most stops have none." A walk-in lobster pound isn't fixed at 6:00. But a stop with no set time follows the one before it, so without one, dinner would have come at 4:35 p.m., right after the rest at the motel. The design already gives meals set times in its examples: "dinner set for 7:00 p.m." in technical spec 5.2's free time example, and "dinner is set for 6:30" on San Francisco Day 2 in domain model 4.1. Change the rule so a meal can also take a set time at the user's usual time for that meal. #234 changes the same rule for timetable stops, so whichever lands second keeps both. Raised by Joe.

The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Done when

- Each item above is in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` or `src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts`, and technical spec 5.2 matches where it covers it.
- `npm run agent-views` was run, and the changed view files are committed with the change.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Small fixes to the agents' instructions, from the Bar Harbor trip

body:
## Why

Each worker ends with a closing message that nobody reads. A `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` replaces the worker's last message with a result code builds from its tool calls (technical spec section on worker results), so the coordinator never sees it. The worker's instructions already say "Nobody reads your own messages [...] So keep your messages short." Workers still write a summary after `report_result`. Those are output tokens paid for and thrown away. It's small for one trip, but cutting it is good practice.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. Eight workers ran. Each one's last model call, after `report_result`, wrote a closing message of about 750 to 1,900 characters, such as the Bar Harbor stay researcher's in turn 5: "I added three candidates each for the Bar Harbor lodging and the three meal stops, and filed the report. A few of the picks are weaker than I'd like. [...]" Those eight last calls came to about 3,400 output tokens, thinking included. `report_result` replies "Result recorded. You're done." (`src/tools/worker-server.ts`), which doesn't say not to write anything more.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), the worker result hook (`PostToolUse` on `Agent`).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), `report_result`.

## Do

- Change `report_result`'s reply to tell the worker to reply with only the word "done", since nobody reads its message. Change the tool design doc to match, and `OWN_MESSAGES` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts` if it needs it. Decided by Joe on 2026-10-30, over structured output: the SDK's structured output is an option for the whole session, and a worker's definition has no field for it. A one-word message also keeps the hook working as it does today, since the worker still ends with a message. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the workers' view files with the change.
- Run a worker once by hand (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5), and confirm in its trace that its last message is only "done".

## Done when

- A worker's last message after `report_result` is only "done" in a hand run.
- The coordinator still gets the code-built result.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Workers end their turn with only "done"

body:
## Why

`search_near` sends the worker's query to Google Text Search with a location bias around the stop or stay, not a limit ([tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md) 2.3). That's on purpose: a query that names a farther place, such as "restaurants in Tuolumne Meadows", searches there. But a query about a style, with no place in it, such as "historic bed and breakfast inn Victorian house", can come back with places across the country. Those results are useless, and they cost the worker tokens to read. A search near a stay never needs a place hundreds of miles away.

Adding the town to every query isn't the fix. Around a stay, the best place is often in the next town: in the same session, "lobster pound lobster shack" near Bar Harbor found Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound in Trenton and Beal's Lobster Pier in Southwest Harbor, both about 9 miles out. With "Bar Harbor" in the query, Google would likely rank places in Bar Harbor itself first.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. Of the 14 `search_near` calls, 6 returned places more than 100 miles away:

- Turn 7, Portland lodging, "historic bed and breakfast inn Victorian house": 6 of 10 results were over 100 miles away, such as B&Bs in St. Augustine, FL, and Sioux Falls, SD, the farthest 2,704 miles.
- Turn 5, Bar Harbor lodging, "retro motel motor court inn": its only result was 1,397 miles away.
- Four more had one or two results 143 to 213 miles away, such as "espresso cafe breakfast" near Portland, and "whale watch cruise" near Bar Harbor in turn 15.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.3 (`search_near`, and "The near distance biases the search. It doesn't limit it.").
- [Google data source](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/google.md), the Text Search row for places near a stay.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 10 (settings, such as the near distance).

## Open questions

- ~~How far is too far? Proposal: 100 miles, as the crow flies from the search's center, as a setting in technical spec section 10. A search near a stay never needs a place that far, and it still lets through a query that names a nearby town, such as one 30 miles off.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat: 100 miles, as the crow flies from the search's center, as its own setting in technical spec section 10, apart from the near distance. In the Bar Harbor session, every useful result was within about 35 miles, and every useless one was 143 miles or more. 100 miles still leaves room for a query that names a specific place an hour or more away in a remote area.

## Do

- In `search_near`, drop results farther than the cutoff, 100 miles, before building the reply. A call whose results are all dropped says it found nothing near, as a search with no results does today.
- Change `search_near`'s description to say results that far away are left out, and that a query about a style alone, such as "Victorian house", can find little nearby, so naming the area can help. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Update tool design 2.3 and the Google data source to match, and add the setting to technical spec section 10.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the workers' view files with the change.

## Done when

- A test with a fake Google reply shows a far result dropped and a near one kept.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: search_near drops places hundreds of miles away

body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

A stop that runs on a timetable, such as a boat or a tour, is fixed at a time even before its timetable is published. The coordinator's instructions don't say so. They say: "Give a stop a set time only when it's fixed at that time, such as a dinner reservation or a sunrise hike. Most stops have none." So when the departure time isn't known, the coordinator leaves the stop with no set time. The schedule then puts it wherever the day has room, as with any stop that follows the one before it. The result looks like a plan but protects nothing: other stops can push the boat around, and workers read its made-up time as real.

The fix is small and clear: have the coordinator propose a likely time and length for a timetable stop, ask the user, give the stop that set time, and say it's a placeholder to check once the timetable is out. This issue checks that the fix works, with an evaluation before and after it. Joe picked it as an easy case to learn evaluations on.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip is a 4-day loop from Natick, MA, with two nights in Bar Harbor. A whale watch on Friday, Day 2, was one of the things the user wanted most.

1. **Turn 4** (turn span `d166ae54f4b36d18`). The coordinator added a "whale watching cruise" stop, and selected Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co with `select_user_place`, a 4-hour visit time, and no set time. Google had no hours for it. Day 2 starts at 7:00 a.m., so the schedule put the boat at 7:03 a.m. The reply said: "I don't know the 2027 departure times yet, so the schedule has the boat leaving right after breakfast. Once the company posts its spring schedule, we can set the real time."
2. **Turn 5.** A stay researcher filling Friday's breakfast read the 7:03 time as real. It ruled out one café as "impractical before a 7:03 whale watch", and noted another's "sit-down service may be slow before a 7:03 tour."
3. **Turn 14.** After breakfast was picked, the boat moved to 8:05. The user asked: "When would the whale tour be on Friday, it says 7:05? [...] wouldn't it be at 7am or not 7:05?"
4. **Turn 15** (turn span `82d5c767c99ad6c5`). The user asked: "Can't we base the whale watching on this year's departure time/schedule? [...] For now it seems like we are just hoping it works out based on what time we end up having free." The coordinator sent a stay researcher to look for past schedules. It found none, but found the season start, trip lengths of 3 to 5½ hours, and summer departures around 8 a.m., noon, and 4 p.m. Only then did the coordinator propose planning Friday around a set departure. In turn 16 the user chose the 8 a.m. boat, and the coordinator gave the stop a set time.

Joe's read: the whale watch was an undefined block with a label on it, not protected and not representing anything. The coordinator should have proposed a block in turn 4, such as "I can't find the departure times until they're posted. What if we block out 4 hours from 8:00 to 12:00, and adjust when the schedule is out?"

## The fix to test

Change the set time rule in the coordinator's instructions, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2: a stop that runs on a timetable, such as a boat or a tour, gets a set time even when the timetable isn't out yet. Propose a likely time and length from what's typical, ask the user, set it once they agree, and say it's a placeholder to check later. Saving that it's a placeholder to trip memory may fit too. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (laying out days: set times).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), a stop's `setTime`.
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- How is the situation set up? Proposal: start from a saved trip like this one after turn 3: the Bar Harbor stay, Day 2 staying put in Bar Harbor, and no whale watch stop yet. Send one message that asks for a whale watch with Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co on Friday, with no time given. The company's place has no hours on Google, as here.
- What counts as a pass? Proposal: a pass is the whale watch stop with a set time, or a reply that proposes a time and length and asks the user, without leaving the boat to follow the stop before it. A fail is a selected whale watch with no set time and no question about the time. Checked from what was saved, plus a judge model for the reply.
- How many runs before and after? Proposal: 10 each, as in #167.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the current instructions for the baseline. Record the results in this issue.
- If the baseline passes almost every run, the change still goes in, since the gap in the instructions is clear. The evaluation then catches it if it comes back.
- Make the instruction change. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with it.
- Run the evaluation again, and record the results in the PR.

## Done when

- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with how many runs passed in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Timetable stops get a set time, checked with an evaluation

body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

When the user picks lodging that serves breakfast, such as a B&B, the next morning's café breakfast stop may no longer be wanted. The coordinator's instructions say to add a breakfast stop only when the meal preferences ask for local breakfast, not hotel breakfast. They say nothing about going back to that stop once the lodging is chosen. So the coordinator keeps planning a café breakfast the user may skip, and the user has to notice and say so.

The fix is small: once lodging that serves breakfast is selected, and the next morning has a breakfast stop, ask the user whether they'll eat breakfast there instead. This issue checks that the fix works, with an evaluation before and after it. Joe picked it as a simple case for evaluations.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip spends Saturday night in Portland, ME, and drives home on Sunday.

1. **Turn 2.** The trip brief's `mealPreferencesText` was saved as "[...] Breakfast from cafés or coffee shops, or get nice coffee and come back for hotel breakfast if there is one."
2. **Turn 4.** Before any lodging was chosen, the coordinator added an "espresso and a café breakfast" stop on Sunday, Day 4, near the Portland stay. A stay researcher filled it in turn 5 with three Portland coffee shops.
3. **Turn 9** (turn span `a7f6d63b6476a10a`). The user selected The Chadwick Bed & Breakfast for Portland. Its rationale, which the coordinator had read, says "An 1891 house in the West End with fireplace rooms and a creative homemade breakfast." The coordinator said nothing about Sunday's breakfast stop.
4. **Turn 19.** The coordinator still listed "Sunday's breakfast" as one of the picks left to make.
5. **Turn 21** (turn span `fba07788ec3d875c`). The user said: "Also for Sunday May 23, I think we would just have breakfast at the B&B." Only then did the coordinator remove the café stop.

The Bar Harbor stay went better. When the user picked the Highbrook Motel in turn 6, whose notes say "Free breakfast delivered to the door", the coordinator said "breakfast is brought to your door, so you could get good coffee in town and bring it back." It didn't ask about the breakfast stops, though.

## The fix to test

Add to the coordinator's meal guidance, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2: when the user selects lodging that serves breakfast, such as a B&B or a hotel whose notes mention breakfast, and a morning at that stay has a breakfast stop, ask whether they'll eat breakfast at the lodging instead. Remove the stop if they will, and save the answer to trip memory. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (laying out days: meals).
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- How is the situation set up? Proposal: start from a saved trip like this one after turn 8: the Portland stay with lodging candidates that include The Chadwick, a café breakfast stop on the next morning, and the same `mealPreferencesText`. Send the user's turn 9 message, "Lets go with the Chadwick and twelve for dinner. I'll look through the other options."
- What counts as a pass? Proposal: the reply asks whether they'll have breakfast at the B&B, or mentions it in a way that invites the choice. Removing the stop without asking is a fail, since the user's meal preferences allow either. Checked by a judge model on the reply, plus code that the stop wasn't removed unasked.
- Should a second case cover a lodging whose breakfast is only in its notes, such as the Highbrook Motel's "Free breakfast delivered to the door"? Proposal: yes, since a B&B is the easy case.
- How many runs before and after? Proposal: 10 each, as in #167.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the current instructions for the baseline. Record the results in this issue.
- If the baseline passes almost every run, the change still goes in, since the gap in the instructions is clear. The evaluation then catches it if it comes back.
- Make the instruction change. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with it.
- Run the evaluation again, and record the results in the PR.

## Done when

- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with how many runs passed in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Breakfast at the lodging: ask about the morning's breakfast stop, checked with an evaluation

body:
## Why

An option card shows only the newest set of options for a stop or a stay's lodging. Once the user asks for more options, or for a higher or lower tier, the earlier set is gone from the page. And once the user picks an option, the card closes for good. To look at the options again, the user has to ask the agent.

In Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30 (agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`), he was on the fence between Twelve and Fore Street for the Portland dinner. He picked Twelve in turn 9. To compare the two again later, he would have had to ask the agent, since there was no way to bring the card back. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

The data is already there, so this is a change to the API's view and the page, not to the trip:

- Every candidate is saved with a set number, and asking for more options adds a new set without removing the old ones (domain model 3.9).
- Selecting an option removes no candidates. Only turning one down does.
- The newest-set filter is in `optionCardOf()` in `src/api/itinerary-view.ts`. A stop or stay with a selection gets `card: null`.

The agent needs no change. Selecting from an older set, or from a reopened card, sends the same message as today, such as "Select Twelve for dinner in Portland." The agent already handles switching a pick by name in chat (functional spec 7.5).

A turned-down place is removed, so it won't show when looking back. That's fine, since the user said no to it.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 7.5 (option cards). Its rules change: the card no longer closes for good once an option is selected, and the user can step back through earlier sets.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.9 (candidates and set numbers).

## Open questions

- ~~What does the card show for a stop or stay with a selection? Proposal: no card by default, as today, plus a "See options" button that opens it. The open card marks the pick, and its newest set shows first.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat:
  - The card still closes when the user picks, as today. A stop or stay with a pick shows the pick, plus a "See options" button.
  - The button opens the card in place, with the newest set first and the pick marked in it. Another button closes it again.
  - Selecting another option from a reopened card sends the same message as any card's Select, such as "Select Fore Street for dinner in Portland." The agent handles the switch, as it does when the user asks in chat.
  - The button shows only when the stop or stay has a candidate other than the pick. One whose only candidate is the pick, such as a place the user named, gets none.
  - As with every card, it shows only in a session's itinerary view, not on the trip page.
- ~~How does the user move between sets? Proposal: back and forward arrows on the card, with "Set 2 of 3" or similar. The newest set shows first.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat:
  - Back and forward arrows on the card, with "Set 2 of 3" between them. The newest set shows first. The arrows show only when there's more than one set.
  - The count goes by position, not by the saved set number. A set whose candidates were all turned down is gone, so set numbers can skip.
  - "More options", "Higher tier", and "Lower tier" show only on the newest set. An older set shows only Select on each option. Their messages say "these", such as "Show me something nicer than these for dinner in Portland", and the agent reads "these" as the newest set.
  - When a new set arrives, the card goes back to the newest set.
- Do "More options", "Higher tier", and "Lower tier" stay on a reopened card for a selected item? Today, new options for a selected item get no card, and the agent names them in chat (functional spec 7.5). Proposal: keep the actions, and drop that rule, so the new set shows on the reopened card like any other.
- Should this come before "Redo the web UI with Claude Design" (#204)? Proposal: yes. That issue changes only how the app looks, and this changes what the page does. Built first, the redo then designs the arrows and the button along with the rest.

## Do

To be written once the open questions are settled. Already known:

- Update functional spec 7.5 to match, in the same PR.

## Done when

To be written once the open questions are settled.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

nodes.body:
Closed 2026-10-30 as not planned. Joe chose to keep the option cards as they are, and to go on with the redesign (#204) and evaluations instead.

The first two open questions were settled before that, and stay in the body in case this comes back. The third showed the change is bigger than the body says: the agent does need a change. The coordinator's instructions say a new set for a stop or stay with a pick gets no card, and that the coordinator names the options in chat instead. Their "Option cards" section also describes what the user sees. Both would change with reopened cards.

body:
## Why

A finding marked "fix" can be left unfixed, with the PR still getting the "ready for Joe" label. It happens when a push lands while the fix job for that finding's review is starting. The fixer stops, since the commit it checked out isn't the PR's head anymore (`src/code-review/fix-input-text.ts`). The push starts a new run, and its review doesn't post the finding again, since an earlier inline comment already makes it. Then `fixRound()` in `src/code-review/fix-round.ts` counts only "fix" findings from the review of the PR's head, so it counts 0. The fix job is skipped, and the ready job adds the label. A "fix it" reply from Joe doesn't bring the finding back either: `isAskable()` needs a fixer reply marked "needs attention" first, and the fixer never replied.

## What happened

PR #240 (#230), on 2026-10-30. Its first review, of `cb806e1`, posted one finding marked "fix", an F6 on `design/technical-spec.md` (comment 4428178492). Merges of `main` into the branch were pushed while its fix job was starting. The fix job stopped with "The checked-out commit, cb806e1..., isn't the PR's head, 5588e24...". The review of the next head, `f53320c`, posted only notes. Its count step printed `fix=0`, so the fix job was skipped, and the PR got the "ready for Joe" label with the F6 finding unreplied.

## Design

- [Code review design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/code-review.md), section 4.5 (the fixer) and 4.6 (the workflow, and "A new commit cancels the review of the one before it, but not a fix job").

## Open questions

- How should a "fix" finding from an earlier review, with no fixer reply, be handled? For example: count it as pending too, have the ready job refuse the label while one is left, or only tell Joe.

## Do

- Change the loop so an unreplied "fix" finding from an earlier review can't be left behind without anyone being told. Update code review design 4.6 to match.

## Done when

- A test with a fake PR state shows an unreplied "fix" finding from an earlier review is no longer dropped.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

nodes.body: Closed as won't fix by Joe on 2026-10-30. Work is focusing on the web UI redesign and on evaluations and simulations, not on more CI review work.

title: A "fix" finding is dropped when a push lands while its fix job starts

body:
## Why

An agent evaluation can start from a real conversation at a chosen turn. It needs two things: the conversation before that turn, and the trip as it stood when the user sent that turn's message. The coordinator then runs the turn on today's code, and the evaluation scores what it said and saved. Example: the Bar Harbor session's turn 5, where the coordinator raised `comfortableDrivingInHours` to cover one long day (#167).

The transcript already keeps the conversation (persistence design, section 6). Nothing keeps the trip. The database holds each trip only as it is now, after every later turn. So a past turn can't be set up again.

This issue saves a copy of the trip at the start of every turn, so every session from now on can be a starting point for evaluations. A later issue rebuilds these copies for the Bar Harbor session, which ran before they existed, and another starts a run from any turn.

A **trip version** is a copy of everything the coordinator reads about a trip, as it stood when one turn started: the plan (the trip brief and the itinerary, persistence design section 2), the trip's places, trip memory, and the user's memory.

It's also most of what #147 would need, if that idea goes ahead. #147's open questions note that the itinerary keeps no history today.

## Design

- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 2 (what is stored together), 6 (sessions and transcripts, and deleting a trip), 8.5 (sessions), and 8.8 (memory).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.5 (memory visibility, which covers forgetting an item).

## Decided

- **A version is saved when a turn starts, before the coordinator runs.** Not at the end of the turn before. The start includes changes made between turns, such as another session's edits, or a memory item the user forgot in the chat view's memory list. An evaluation needs the trip as the coordinator found it.
- **Each version is whole, not a list of changes.** A session has tens of turns, so the size is fine, and restoring one is a single copy.
- **Each version is tied to its turn's place in the transcript,** so a run can cut the transcript right before that turn's user message. The implementer picks how, such as the turn's number in the session, counted the way `src/agent/shown-messages.ts` counts user messages.
- **The app never reads versions.** Only evaluation tooling does. The coordinator never sees them.
- **Deleting a trip deletes its versions,** in the same transaction as the rest of the trip (persistence design, section 6).
- **A forgotten memory item stays in older versions.** "Forgotten items no longer influence recommendations" (functional spec 10.5) still holds, since the app never reads versions. The transcript already keeps the user's words, so versions keep nothing that wasn't kept already.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add a table for trip versions, with a migration: one row per turn, keyed to its session and its turn.
- Save a version at the start of every coordinator turn, in `CoordinatorTurns` (`src/agent/coordinator-turns.ts`), which both the app's API and `npm run chat` use. Save it after the checks that can refuse the turn, such as a closed chat or a turn already running, so a refused message saves nothing.
- Remove a trip's versions in `TripWriter.deleteTrip()`.
- Write trip versions into the persistence design: what a version holds, when it's saved, and that a trip's delete removes them.
- Add tests with fake repositories (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A session with three turns on the local stack (systems design, section 6) has three versions. Each matches the trip as it stood when its turn started. Check it by hand by forgetting a memory item between turns 2 and 3: the item is in version 2 and not in version 3.
- Deleting the trip removes its versions.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Save a trip version at the start of each turn

body:
**Starts** now. #243 and #247, which it builds on, are merged.

## Why

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30 (agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`) is the only past session close enough to today's instructions to evaluate on. Earlier sessions ran on instructions and tools that have changed too much. Several evaluation candidates come from it, such as #167, #209, #234, and #235.

It ran before trip versions existed (#243), so it has none. This issue rebuilds them from its transcript, so an evaluation can start from any of its turns (#245). The trip as it stands now is the end of the session. The trip at the start of each earlier turn has to be worked out from what the transcript recorded.

Later sessions get versions as they run, so this is a one-time job for this one session.

## Design

- #243, for what a trip version holds, and #247, which added the turn's user message to each version.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 8.9 (trip versions: what each holds, how turns are numbered, and how #245 finds a turn's message). The code is `TripVersionRepository` in `src/persistence/trip-version-repository.ts`, and `userMessageCount()` and `turnMessageIndex()` in `src/agent/shown-messages.ts`.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 2 (what is stored together) and 6 (sessions and transcripts, including workers' transcripts).
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 6 and 10, for reaching the server's Postgres through an SSH tunnel.

## Decided

- **The session's data stays in the databases.** Its transcript and trip hold personal details, and the repo is public. Nothing from them goes in the repo: not in code, tests, fixtures, or the PR. Tests use made-up data. The PR's results give counts, turn numbers, and tool names, not the content of the trip.
- **Mostly code, with Claude only where code can't decide.** Code reads the session's save calls in order, the coordinator's and each worker's, with the reply each one got. It runs them again through today's services, one turn at a time, starting from an empty trip, and saves a version at the start of each turn.
- **Each ID comes from the recorded reply.** Today's code makes a new random ID on each save. During the rebuild, each one is the ID the recorded reply gave, so the trip's IDs match the ones the transcript names.
- **Places are copied from the live trip's place rows,** not looked up at Google again. A version holds only the places saved before its turn started. The transcript shows when each was saved: from the call whose reply first gave its ID.
- **When today's tool doesn't take a recorded call,** Claude rewrites the call into today's shape. Tools have changed since 2026-10-30. Each rewrite is listed in the PR, by turn and tool, with what changed in the call's shape.
- **What the coordinator saw wins over today's code.** Where today's code would set the trip up differently, such as the comfortable driving hours default from #230, the rebuilt trip matches what the recorded reads showed.
- **A change made outside the transcript,** such as forgetting a memory item in the chat view, shows only as the app's line in the next message (technical spec 5.2). Apply it from that line, before that turn's version is saved.
- **Code checks the result at every checkpoint.** Each recorded reply from `read_trip_brief`, `read_itinerary`, and `read_memory` shows the trip at that moment. Code runs the same read on the rebuilt trip at the same point, and lists every difference. The trip after the last turn is also compared with the live trip now. Read replies may have changed format since 2026-10-30, so Claude sorts the differences: only format, or a real difference. Each real one is fixed, or listed in the PR with why it can't match.
- **The rebuild works in the local database, then writes the versions to the live one.** It reads the session from the server's Postgres through the SSH tunnel, rebuilds in the local Postgres, and adds the versions to the live database, on the same session. So they're in the nightly backup (systems design, section 9), and the session looks like any session recorded after #243. The only write to the live database is adding this session's version rows.
- **Each version is filled in the way the app fills it on a live turn** (persistence design, section 8.9), so #245 can use it like any other version:
  - **`turn`** counts the user messages the way `userMessageCount()` does. Turn 1 is the session's first message.
  - **`user_message`** is the user's own words from that turn's message, without the app's lines. Take it from the user messages `shownMessagesOf()` returns, in order. They're counted the same way, and the app's lines are already stripped. An empty message would make #245 refuse the version.
  - **`saved_date_time`** is the `timestamp` on that turn's user message line in the transcript. #245 runs the app's clock at this time.
  - **`session_id`** is the live session row's `id`, which starts with `session_`, not the agent session ID.
  - Saving the rebuilt local trip with `TripVersionRepository.saveFrom()` gives rows in the right shape, to copy to the live database.
- **The rebuild code is committed,** so the PR can be reviewed. It takes the agent session ID as an argument, and holds no data from the session.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Write the rebuild, and run it on the Bar Harbor session in the local database.
- Fix the rebuild until every checkpoint matches, or each difference left is listed in the PR with its reason.
- Write the versions to the live database.

## Done when

- The live database has a version for each turn of the session.
- Every checkpoint matches, apart from the differences listed in the PR.
- The rebuilt trip after the last turn matches the live trip, apart from the differences listed in the PR.
- `turnMessageIndex()` finds every version's turn in the live session's transcript, with no error.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Rebuild the Bar Harbor session's trip versions

body:
**Starts** once #244 is merged.

## Why

An agent evaluation sets up a real moment from a past session, and scores what the coordinator does next. This issue builds the setup: a command that starts a run from any turn of a recorded session, and runs that one turn on today's code.

With turn 4 as the example, a run gives the coordinator:

- **Turns 1 to 3 as they were recorded,** with every user message, reply, and tool call with its result. The SDK loads them from the copied transcript when it resumes the session, the same way every normal turn works. Nothing in them runs again.
- **The trip as it stood when turn 4 started,** from its trip version (#243).
- **A turn 4 message,** either the recorded one or a new one.

The coordinator does its turn 4 work, and what it says and saves can be scored. The conversation and the trip stay fixed, so only the instructions, the tools, or the model change between runs. Running turns 1 to 3 live instead would drift, since the coordinator answers a bit differently each time.

#53 builds the evaluations on this: the datasets, the scorers, and the experiments in Phoenix. This issue covers only the setup and the one turn.

## Design

- #243, for what a trip version holds, and #244, for the Bar Harbor versions.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 6 (sessions and transcripts), 8.5 (sessions, and the line the app adds on a resume), and 8.9 (trip versions, and how tooling finds a turn's message in the transcript).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, for the app's lines on each message.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 6 and 10, for reaching the server's Postgres and Phoenix through an SSH tunnel.
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.3, for how the #132 spike ran a conversation for a fresh user through the same code as `npm run chat`.

## Decided

- **The source is a session on the live database,** read through the SSH tunnel. The run itself is on the local stack (systems design, section 6), and its trace goes to the server's Phoenix, as for any local turn.
- **Personal data stays in the databases.** Nothing from a recorded session goes in the repo. Tests use made-up data.
- **The command takes the agent session ID, the turn number, and the message:** the recorded one, or new text.
- **Each run gets a fresh test user, trip, and session.** It copies the transcript lines before that turn's user message, workers' lines included. Workers run only inside a coordinator turn, so in `transcript_lines.id` order, every worker line from an earlier turn comes before the turn's message. So the cut is every row, coordinator or worker, whose `id` is below that message's row. It also copies the trip version from that turn's start: the plan, the places, trip memory, and user memory. IDs inside the trip stay the same, since the conversation names them. To find that turn's user message, use `turnMessageIndex()` in `src/agent/shown-messages.ts` (#247), on the coordinator's lines in `id` order. It gives the message's place in that list. It counts user messages the same way the trip version's turn number was counted. It throws if the message there doesn't end with the words the version saved. So a run can't pair a version with the wrong moment. Versions saved before #247 have no saved words, so the function refuses them.
- **A place's key is its trip and its ID, and a memory item's key is its user and its ID.** Decided by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat. Today `places.id` and `memory_items.id` are each unique in the whole table. A run keeps the recorded IDs, so its copy would clash with the recorded rows, and with any earlier run of the same session. In the local database, the Bar Harbor trip from the version rebuild (#244) already holds them. Every lookup already gives the trip or the user, apart from `PlaceRepository.fillNames()`, which gets the trip added. Sharing one place row between trips was the other choice. It would need a table linking trips and places, and memory would still need copying, since a run can change or forget a memory item. A migration changes the two keys, and the persistence design says so.
- **The turn runs through the same code as `npm run chat`,** with today's instructions and tools.
- **The command prints the new user, trip, and session IDs, and the reply,** so a scorer can read what was saved.
- **Each run leaves its test user's rows in the local database.** That's fine for a local database, as in the #132 spike.
- **The coordinator can't tell a run from a real session.** Nothing it sees may differ from what it would have seen in the recorded turn, apart from the turn itself and Claude Code's date (below). The message gets exactly the recorded turn's app lines, and the app adds none of its own, such as a resume line. A new message keeps the recorded lines, with only the user's words replaced.
- **The trip's date comes from the app's line, not from Claude Code.** Decided by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat, in place of running Claude Code with a fake clock:
  - **The app's date line names the trip.** Today it says "Today is Sunday, October 10, 2027." (technical spec 5.2), which reads like Claude Code's own "Today's date is 2026-10-27." It changes to something specific to planning the trip, such as "For planning this trip, today's date is Sunday, October 10, 2027." This changes the line on the live site too.
  - **The coordinator's instructions say to plan by that line.** Any rule that uses today's date, such as the start date, the forecast, or the trip's start, goes by the date in that line, even if another date shows up.
  - **A run's date line has the recorded turn's date.** Recorded messages have the old wording, so the copy rewrites each old date line into the new wording, with the same date.
  - **The app's own clock uses the recorded turn's time,** which is the trip version's `saved_date_time` (#244 sets it from the turn's message line), for code that uses today's date, such as the weather tools and the started-trip check. The tool servers already take a `now` function.
  - **Claude Code's date is left alone.** On the live site it already matches the app's line, since #194 runs the Claude Code process in the trip's time zone. In a run, it's today's date, and on resume Claude Code adds "The date has changed. Today's date is now ..." ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.9). That's the one accepted difference from a real session. If runs show the coordinator reacting to it, it gets looked at again.

## Open questions

- ~~Which app lines does the turn's message get? The app adds lines to each message, such as today's date (technical spec 5.2), and a line saying the session was resumed (persistence design 8.5). The recorded turn has the lines it ran with. A copied session looks like a resume to the app, so it would add a resume line the recorded turn may not have had, and today's date. Proposal: the recorded message is sent exactly as the model got it, app lines included, and the app adds none of its own. A new message keeps the recorded turn's app lines, with only the user's words replaced. Code that checks dates, such as a forecast window, still uses today's date. That's accepted, since the gap is a few weeks.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat: the coordinator must not be able to tell a run from a real session. So the message gets exactly the recorded turn's app lines, and the app adds none of its own. A new message keeps them, with only the user's words replaced. For the date, see Decided.

## Do

- Check first that the SDK resumes cleanly from copied lines. If the lines name the old agent session ID, or the copy needs anything else rewritten, rewrite it in the copy.
- Check whether the copied transcript names the old trip, session, or user ID anywhere the coordinator or its tools would use it. Rewrite any that would break the run.
- Change the app's date line, and add the rule to plan by it, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Update `withoutAppLines()` in `src/agent/app-lines.ts` to strip the new date line, and keep it stripping the old one. Live sessions recorded before this change keep the old wording, and the chat view still has to hide it. Add a test for each wording.
- Write the command, outside `npm run check`.
- Write how to use it into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5.

## Done when

- A run that starts the Bar Harbor session at turn 5, with the recorded message, gives the coordinator the same trip it saw in the recorded turn 5: its first read in the turn matches the recorded one, apart from format. The coordinator answers, and the turn's trace is in Phoenix.
- The same works with a new message.
- Nothing in the run tells the coordinator it isn't the recorded session. Check the run's transcript: after the copied lines, it has nothing the recorded turn didn't have, such as a resume line, apart from the turn itself and Claude Code's date change line. If needed, check a model call's full input with a logging proxy, as #188 did.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
title: Start a run from any turn of a recorded session

body:
## Why

A simulated user is a coding agent, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode, with a chosen model, playing a user who plans a trip (#66). It works from a shell, so it can't use the web page. `npm run chat` doesn't help: it runs the coordinator itself, on the developer's machine, against the local database. A session on the live site has to go through the app's API, the way the browser does, so its data is in the live database and its traces are in the server's Phoenix project, `road-trip-agent` (systems design, section 10).

This issue adds a terminal client that does what the browser does. It runs no agent. It signs in, sends the user's messages, and prints the replies, the option cards, and the itinerary. It also sends a card's buttons the way a click does. A simulated session then goes through the same path as a real one. Two things in `npm run chat` would make a session unlike a real one, and the client avoids both:

- Each `npm run chat -- --resume` adds the resumed line to the next message (technical spec 5.2), so driving it one command per message would make every turn look like a resume. Through the API, the server keeps a session's app lines between messages, as it does for the browser.
- `npm run chat` prints the coordinator's thinking, tool calls, and tool replies. A real user sees only the reply.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 3 (sign-in), section 4 (the API and its Server-Sent Events), and section 6 (local development).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 7.5 (option cards).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 7.2 (the option card's IDs line).

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add `npm run live-chat`, in TypeScript under `src/`, next to `src/chat.ts`. It talks to the app only through its API, never the database or the coordinator. Reuse what's in `src/shared/`, such as `messageRequestSchema`, `chatEventSchema` and `src/shared/chat-event-parser.ts`, and `src/shared/itinerary.schema.ts`, so `npm run check` catches the client breaking when the API changes.
- Run one command per action, and exit when it's done. A simulated user's harness runs one shell command at a time, so a long-running prompt like `npm run chat`'s won't work. It has to:
  - start a trip with a first message (`POST /api/trips`), and print the new trip and session IDs.
  - send a message to a session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/messages`).
  - start a new session on a trip (`POST /api/trips/:tripId/sessions`), and open an old session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/resume`), as a user does who comes back another day.
  - print the itinerary, as the itinerary view shows it.
  - print the open option cards, with a number on each option.
  - send a card's buttons: Select on an option, More options, Higher tier, and Lower tier. Send the same message and the same option card IDs a click sends (`web/src/option-card.tsx`). Move the words of those messages into `src/shared/`, so the web page and the client can't drift apart.
- Read the message from standard input, so it can be more than one line, and needs no shell quoting.
- Print only what the web page shows: the reply text, and while a turn runs, the name of each tool the coordinator calls, as the chat's "waiting on" line shows it. Never the thinking, the tool inputs, or the tool replies. After each reply, say how many option cards are open, so the simulated user knows to look, as a web user sees a card appear.
- Sign in with Supabase's email and password sign-in, as `web/src/sign-in-page.tsx` does. The site's address, the email, and the password come from environment values, checked with Zod when the command starts. Never take the password as a command-line argument, since a harness shows each command it runs. The Supabase URL and publishable key are already in `.env` as `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
- The site's address can be the local stack, `http://localhost:5173` with `npm run dev`, or the live site, `https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`. Both use the same Supabase project, so the same user signs in to either (systems design, section 6).
- Add a `whoami` action that signs in and prints the user's ID and email, from Supabase's sign-in reply. #66 uses it to list each bot user's ID with its harness and model, with no Supabase admin key.
- Add the command to DEVELOPMENT.md section 2.
- A turn can take minutes when workers run. The longest in Phoenix so far took about 4 minutes. Wait for the turn's end event, with no timeout of the client's own.

## Done when

- Against the local stack, with a Supabase user made for testing: a short chat starts a trip, gets an option card, selects an option with the client, and asks for a higher tier with it. Each turn's trace is in the `road-trip-agent-local` Phoenix project, under that user's ID.
- The client's output for those turns shows only reply text, tool names, and the card count.
- No check runs against the live site. Its first real use is #67.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
title: Chat with the app from the terminal through its API

body:
## Why

A write tool's reply lists its check results under one heading, "Check results:". The results a change made go away are in that list too, as lines starting "Gone:" (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`). Each gone line repeats the result's saved text, which reads like a problem that's still there. Example: "Gone: Twelve is closed for the whole visit, on Saturday, May 22, 2027. You'd get there at 10:47 a.m., with 1 h planned."

Joe's small evaluation on 2026-11-03 tested this on turn 10 of the Bar Harbor session, where `update_stop` moved dinner at Twelve to 6:00 p.m. and the closure warning went away. Two of Phoenix's built-in judges, completeness and tool response handling, read the turn on Haiku 5.5, 3 runs each, so 6 runs per wording:

- **The reply as it is:** all 6 runs read the gone line as an open warning.
- **"No longer applies:" in place of "Gone:":** all 6 runs read it as open. Some read it as the change not applying, such as "the time change 'no longer applies' and the stop was not successfully rescheduled."
- **"No longer applies:", with the text in the past tense:** all 6 runs read it as open.
- **A line that says what the change did:** "Fixed by this change: the earlier warning that Twelve would be closed when you arrived. Before this change, you'd have gotten there at 10:47 a.m. on Saturday, May 22, 2027, when it's closed." Completeness passed the turn in 3 of 3 runs. Tool response handling still failed it, for other reasons: it saw only this turn, so it flagged facts from earlier turns as made up. Its explanations read the line correctly, such as "the tool confirmed it fixed the closure warning."

The line that worked stayed in the "Check results:" list. A section of its own wasn't tested. The line also changed several things at once: it said this change fixed the result, called it the earlier warning, put the problem in the past, and left out the old text's caveats, such as "this time may be too early". Which of these did the work isn't known.

In that turn, the coordinator itself read the gone line correctly, and didn't raise the warning. But it reads the same replies as the judges, so it can make the same mistake, such as raising a warning the change just fixed. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat, while going through #65.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1, the paragraphs "Writing." and "The tool builds its reply from what the write hands back".
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, "How to handle broken feasibility rules", and section 8.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.8: what new, changed, already known, and gone mean.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- In `checkResultLines()` (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`), change each gone line to follow the line that worked. Start by saying this change fixed or cleared the result, call it the earlier warning or note, and give its saved text as what was true before the change, not as a problem that's still there. Keep the lines in the "Check results:" list, where the tested line was. Don't use "Gone" or "No longer applies", since judges read both as open warnings. The test rewrote the text by hand, but code can only wrap the saved text, such as `- Fixed by this change: the earlier warning "Twelve is closed for the whole visit, ..."`. Change the line for a reply with no results to match.
- Change what says "gone" to the coordinator to the new words: the line on check results in its instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`), and any tool description that mentions them. Then run `npm run agent-views`, so the view files show the new wording.
- Change tool design section 2.1 and technical spec 5.2 to describe the new wording. The domain model keeps its term "gone", and the code keeps `goneResults`, since neither is read by a model.
- The implementer drafts the exact wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Check the drafted wording with the turn 10 test: put a gone line in the new wording in `NEW_LINE` in `phoenix-tutorials/run-evals-with-built-in-evals/gone_wording_test.py`, and run it from that folder with the tutorials' Python (`../.venv/bin/python`). It needs the local Phoenix running. The folder is gitignored, so the test is only on Joe's machine. Put the results in the PR's decisions comment.

## Done when

- A test shows a write that fixes a warning lists it in the new wording, not as "Gone:".
- In the turn 10 test, completeness passes in 3 of 3 runs with the drafted wording.
- The view files show the new wording, and `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
title: Put gone check results in their own section of a write's reply

body:
## Why

The app plans trips only in the contiguous United States (functional spec sections 1 and 2). #65 told the coordinator not to offer, or add, a place outside it. But a leg between two US places can still run through Canada, since `compute_route` and the leg tools take Google's route, and no tool shows the road a route takes (technical spec 4.2). Example: the fastest drive from Detroit to Buffalo runs through Ontario, on Highway 401. The user would need a passport, and the trip would leave the area the app plans for, with nothing to tell them.

Found while working on #65, on 2026-11-04. Not seen in a recorded session yet.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 1 and 2.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 4.2, "How a waypoint is picked", and section 5.2, "Conduct".

## Open questions

- Is it worth handling at all? Few trips would cross, and the user can see the route on the itinerary view's map.
- If so, how? One way: the coordinator judges from its own knowledge of the roads whether a leg crosses the border, as it does for whether a leg reaches a must-see area, and adds a waypoint on the US side, with a reason such as "stay in the US". Another: code flags a leg whose route leaves the US, which needs the route's path, which no tool asks Google for today.

## Do

- To be settled.

## Done when

- To be settled.

## Ends in

A decision, and maybe a PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

nodes.body: Leaving this as it is, decided by Joe on 2026-11-04. The app is limited to the contiguous United States because of the Places API and different address formats. A route that crosses Canada between two US places doesn't run into either. Reopen it if it causes a problem in a real trip.

title: Keep a leg between two US places from routing through Canada

body:
## Why

`npm run check` fails in a checkout that has a `phoenix-tutorials/` folder, with 8 lint errors that have nothing to do with the code. Git ignores that folder, but ESLint doesn't: `eslint .` reads `phoenix-tutorials/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/urllib3/contrib/emscripten/emscripten_fetch_worker.js`. The pre-commit hook runs the same check, so no commit that changes code can go through from that checkout. Worktrees and CI don't have the folder, so they pass.

## Design

- DEVELOPMENT.md section 6: `eslint.config.*` changes only with Joe's approval.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add `phoenix-tutorials/` to the `globalIgnores` list in `eslint.config.*`, next to `scratch/`. This is a config change, so it needs Joe's approval first.

## Done when

- `npm run check` passes in a checkout that has `phoenix-tutorials/.venv`.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
