title: Keep ESLint out of the gitignored phoenix-tutorials folder

body:
**Starts** once #66 is merged.

## Why

When a user opens a trip again within a week of its start, the coordinator should offer to replace a stay's seasonal averages with a real forecast (functional spec, section 8; technical spec, section 5.2, the bullet "Today's date"). That's agent behavior worth having in the corpus for agent evaluations (#53).

The San Francisco and Moab trip files (#67, #68) can't cover it. Their start dates are fixed in 2027, and the app always uses the real date, so a run can't come back "a few days before the trip". Faking the date was ruled out in #66: Google gives forecasts only for the real next 10 days or so, and Claude Code's own date line would show the coordinator two different dates (technical spec 5.2).

A trip whose start date is set from the day the run begins can cover it. The simulated user plans the trip in a first session. A few real days later, Joe starts a second session in the same run folder. The trip is then within 7 days of its start, so the forecast is real.

## Design

- [The simulated user](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/issues/66): run folders, trip files, persona files, and `simulated-users/README.md`. Its struck-out open question on later dates says why the date isn't faked.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 8: weather, and the offer when a trip moves into the forecast range.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, the bullet "Today's date": the note in a new session's first read, the offer, and trip memory when the user turns it down. Section 8: a stay gets a forecast when every one of its dates is within 7 days.

## Open questions

- Which trip? A short one keeps the wait and the run small.

## Do

- Write a trip file whose start date is set from the day the run starts, such as "the first Thursday at least 9 days after you start". Its changes partway through end the first session once the trip is planned, and open the trip again in a new session on a later day. On that day, every date of at least one stay is within 7 days of today, and the trip hasn't started.
- The simulated user needs the trip ID in the second session. Have the instructions say to keep it in a file in the run folder, and add to `simulated-users/README.md` how to start a later session in a run folder that already exists.
- Run it on the live site (`https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`), signed in as the harness's bot user. Check the session as #67 does, and mark a failed run the same way.
- Check that in the second session's first reply, the coordinator offers to replace the seasonal averages with a forecast.

## Done when

- A simulated session is in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project in which the user comes back within 7 days of the start, and the coordinator offers the forecast.
- The app bugs found are filed as issues.

## Ends in

A PR, with the trip file and any changes to the instructions or the README.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
title: Record a trip that starts soon, for the forecast offer

body:
## Why

A new trip's usual start time is 8:00 a.m., and the coordinator no longer has anything telling it to raise that with the user. So a user can see 8:00 a.m. on their days without ever being asked, and not know where it came from. A user trying the app on the live site asked why the start time was set to 8 a.m.

## What happened

- Before #230, the coordinator's instructions said "Establish each item", which covered `usualStartTime`, though it wasn't required. In Joe's Bar Harbor session on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix, turn 1 asked: "Do you usually get going around 8 a.m., or later?"
- #230 changed that to "Establish each required item", and "leave every other question for later". It gives a later time for `routePreference`, `mealPreferencesText`, `lodgingPreferencesText`, driving hours, and rest days. It gives none for `usualStartTime` (`src/agent/coordinator-trip-brief-prompt.ts`). #230 didn't set out to change this: its open questions cover only driving hours and rest days.
- On the current instructions, the coordinator can still ask, but it isn't reliable. In Joe's Florida session on 2026-11-04, agent session `7b417a52-9ed3-46bb-8457-7705ac231aa8`, in the same Phoenix project, the user said in turn 2, "I'm really an early morning person". The coordinator then asked, "What time do you usually like to get going? You said you're an early riser, so maybe 7:00, or even earlier?" The user said 7 a.m., and the coordinator set `usualStartTime` to 7:00 a.m. One session can't show whether the user's remark is what prompted the question: the coordinator's thinking in that turn also lists the start time as still open.
- The session that raised this issue is agent session `f029cbae-16de-4ac0-882c-4469ccd71f54`, on 2026-11-04, in the same Phoenix project. The user said nothing about mornings, and had no user memory. In 8 turns the coordinator never asked about the usual start time. It first came up in turn 7, as "With the usual 8:00 start", when a stop didn't open until 9:00. The start time was then handled one day at a time, as each day's first stop raised it.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 5.2: the usual start time isn't required, and defaults to 8 a.m.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, "What to establish".

## Open questions

- When, if at all, should the coordinator raise the usual start time? Changing a day's start time as the plan needs it may be fine. In `f029cbae-16de-4ac0-882c-4469ccd71f54`, the session stopped before meals were added, so its start times weren't final. A smaller change than asking would be to say that 8:00 a.m. is a default the user can change, the first time it comes up.

## Do

- Change the coordinator's instructions and the design docs to match the answer. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- The coordinator's instructions say when to raise the usual start time, and the design docs match.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR, or a decision to leave it as it is.

**Settled in:** chat.
title: Nothing tells the coordinator to raise the usual start time

body:
## Why

The schedule treats every move between places as a drive (domain model section 4.1). When two places are a few blocks apart, such as a hotel on Cannery Row and a dinner up the street, a real party would walk. The coordinator knows this, and says so in its replies.

Found by the simulated user (#66), in three runs of the San Francisco trip on the local stack, on 2026-11-04. In each run, the coordinator added a line like this after most picks in Monterey and San Luis Obispo: "The Whaling Station is about a block and a half up the hill, an easy walk, even though the schedule shows it as a short drive." The same caveat came up four or five times a session. It makes replies longer, and the user has to work out that the schedule is a little off.

## Open questions

- Is this worth changing, or is the caveat fine as it is? The times are only a few minutes off, so the schedule is close enough either way.
- If it changes, which way? Options: a walking leg when two places are close enough, which is mostly deterministic code and new rules; or one line in the coordinator's instructions, saying the schedule counts short walks as drives and doesn't need a caveat each time.
title: Short walks show as drives in the schedule

body:
## Why

`npm run live-chat itinerary` prints a picked place's reason and its source on one line, with no break between them. When the reason has no period at the end, they run together, such as:

```
Why: the user's own plan: breakfast first thing You named this place.
```

A simulated user reads the itinerary through `live-chat`, so it reads this line as one sentence. The web page shows the reason and the source as two paragraphs (`web/src/itinerary-view.tsx`), and `live-chat`'s own option cards print "You named this place." on a line of its own (`src/live-chat/option-cards.ts`). Found in the San Francisco run on the live site (#67).

## Design

- `src/live-chat/itinerary-print.ts`, the function that prints a picked place, which joins `Why: ${selection.rationale} ${source}`.

## Open questions

None.

## Do

- Print the source, "You named this place." or `Source: <link>`, on its own line under the "Why" line, as the option cards do in `src/live-chat/option-cards.ts`.

## Done when

- The itinerary print shows the reason and the source on separate lines, and `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.

nodes.body: Won't fix. The app's agents never see this output. Only a simulated user reads it, and in the San Francisco run it didn't misread anything because of it.

title: live-chat prints a picked place's reason and source on one line

body:
## Why

In the San Francisco run on the live site (#67), the stay researcher's calls to `add_stop_candidates` and `add_lodging_candidates` were refused 7 times, and each time it fixed the call and tried again. Six were meal stops, where it sent `visitTimeInMinutes`, which only an attraction's candidates take. One was a lodging set, where it sent a `rating` key the tool doesn't have. Nothing was lost, but each refusal is a wasted call in a turn the user is waiting on.

`ADD_STOP_CANDIDATES_DESCRIPTION` in `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts` already says a meal's candidates each take a tier, and an attraction's each take `visitTimeInMinutes`. So the description alone doesn't stop it.

Most of the refusals came back as the MCP SDK's own input validation error, a raw Zod union dump (`MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... invalid_union ...`), not as the tool's own plain message ("... is a meal stop, so each candidate takes a tier, and no visitTimeInMinutes"). That's the reply the agent has to fix its call from.

The traces are in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project, on the `stay-researcher.turn` spans of 2026-11-04, from 20:03 to 20:10 UTC.

The Moab run with Claude Code (#68) had 2 more refusals of `add_stop_candidates`, both meal stops with `visitTimeInMinutes`. One came from the stay researcher and one from the leg scout, so it isn't only the stay researcher. Both fixed the call and went on. The traces are in the same project, at 22:17:45 and 22:17:46 UTC on 2026-11-04.

As of 2026-11-08, `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts` and both workers' prompts are unchanged since these runs, so the problem should still be there.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1: a meal's candidates take a tier, and an attraction's a visit time.
- `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts`, `src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts`, and `src/agent/leg-scout-prompt.ts`.
- [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), section 5: `npm run run-turn`, and how the grounded evaluator (#282) runs in Phoenix.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 8.9: trip versions, `run-turn`, and `rebuild-versions`.

## Open questions

- Is this frequent enough to fix? The count across the corpus, in the comment of 2026-11-08: 47 of 361 candidate calls refused, in 32 of 106 worker runs.
- ~~Which fix: make the schema's own refusal read like the tool's message, change the input schema so the wrong key can't be sent, or change the description or the workers' prompts? Joe said on 2026-11-08, in chat, that a fix in the tool is fine, and he'd almost rather it be one, since that's an interesting outcome.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: try three fixes, and compare them. See Do.
- ~~Does the split tools experiment start from the prompt change, or from today's prompts? Proposal: from the prompt change, so each experiment adds one change to the last. The cost is that the split isn't measured on its own.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: from today's prompts, so the split is measured on its own. The work is on two branches, each starting from the commit that gives a run with no candidate calls no score. `candidate-prompt-266` has the prompt change and the schema titles, in one commit. `candidate-split-266` has the split.
- ~~Should the fix be checked with an evaluation (#53)?~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-08, in chat: yes. It's one of the two behavior evaluations he's prioritizing, and the code-scored one.
- ~~How does a case run? No command runs a worker on its own today. Proposal: replay the recorded coordinator turns that sent out workers in the San Francisco and Moab sessions with `npm run run-turn -- <agent session ID> <turn> --recorded-message`, so the workers get real worker briefs. Code counts the refused candidate calls in each worker's spans, and the calls that went through, so the score is a rate. No judge. Building a command that runs a worker alone from a fixed worker brief, as #185 proposes for the stay researcher, would isolate the workers better, but it's more to build.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-08, in chat: each case runs one worker on its own, from a recorded worker run, with the coordinator stood in for by the test. The test sends the worker the worker brief the coordinator sent it, as `run-turn` does for a coordinator turn, and only the worker's spans are scored. Code counts the refused candidate calls and the ones that went through, so the score is a rate. No judge. See Do.
- Where does the trip come from? A trip version is the trip as it stood when the coordinator's turn started (persistence design, section 8.9). The coordinator can change the trip in that turn before it sends the workers, such as adding the stops they fill. So the worker may need more than the version. Proposal: restore the turn's version, then run again the coordinator's recorded save calls that came before its Agent call, as `npm run rebuild-versions` does. Where the coordinator made no changes before sending the workers, the version alone is enough. The count of 2026-11-08 found saves before the worker in all 32 worker runs with a refusal, so the replay is needed.
- ~~Which worker runs are the cases, and how many runs of each? Proposal: the worker runs that had refusals in the San Francisco and Moab sessions, plus any the count finds, with 5 runs of each. A stay researcher fills several stops in one run, so that's a few dozen candidate calls per case.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: all 32 worker runs with a refusal, 5 runs each. Two trial sets come first, as Phoenix splits, to check the setup: `trial-1` is 3 cases, and `trial-2` is 12, the 3 in `trial-1` among them. Each trial runs its cases once.
- ~~Should the `visit-time` split get its own score, counting only the `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals? Today's score counts every refusal, such as Google finding no driving route, which this fix can't change. Proposal: add a second code scorer for just that refusal.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: yes. The `visit time refusal rate` scorer counts the refusals whose reply names `visitTimeInMinutes` as the wrong key, as a share of all candidate calls, beside the other two scores.
- ~~What change for the `no-route` refusal? Joe has one in mind, likely a change to the tool's code (2026-11-09, in chat). It may not be worth making in the live app, but he wants to try it on the `no-route` split.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: a clearer reply, in its own PR after the split tools PR. See Do.

## Do

- Count how often the workers' candidate calls are refused across the corpus: the sessions with a `corpus` session annotation in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). Split the count by worker, by tool, and by what was wrong, such as `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop. Record it in this issue.
- Settle the open questions with Joe.
- Add a way to run one worker from a recorded worker run: its worker brief from the coordinator's recorded Agent call, the trip as the worker found it, and today's worker instructions and tools. Its trace goes to Phoenix, as a turn's does. Write how it runs into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, next to `npm run run-turn`.
- Write the evaluation as a Phoenix experiment in TypeScript, as the grounded evaluator is (`src/grounded-eval/`). Run it on the tools and prompts as they are, for the baseline.
- Fix the two notes the CI review left on #284 before the next experiment runs. Neither touched the baseline: all 160 runs made candidate calls, and all called `report_result`.
  - A run with no candidate calls gets the best score from both scorers, so it would pull a case's rate down. Give it no score, as a failed run gets none. A run without calls has no rate, which is the reason. A fix to `visitTimeInMinutes` could leave a worker making no candidate calls, so this matters for that fix.
  - The comment in `src/agent/solo-worker.ts` and the line in DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 say the worker hooks only build the worker's result. The `SubagentStop` hook also sends a worker back, up to 2 times, when it tries to end without `report_result`. A worker run alone isn't sent back. Fix both to say so.
- Fix `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop first. Run it on the `visit-time` split, then on the whole dataset. The `visit-time` split is the 25 cases that made this mistake in at least one baseline run, all stay researcher runs. Its baseline needs no new run, since the full baseline already ran those cases 5 times: 112 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals in 572 candidate calls, and 117 refusals in all. Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- The traces show the workers pick the right places, and get only the shape wrong. Of the 39 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals in the recorded runs, 31 sent a tier and a visit time, and 8 sent a visit time and no tier. Every retry sent the same places. Joe sees the cause as two keys that each apply to only some stops, which is close to an optional key. Try these two fixes, each from its own commit, each run on the `visit-time` split with 5 runs per case, and compare each with the baseline. Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
  - Prompt and titles: the workers' "What each candidate field means" section is split into fields for every candidate, fields for meal and lodging candidates only (`tier`), and fields for attraction candidates only (`visitTimeInMinutes`). Today it's one list, and says neither field's stop kind. Each of `add_stop_candidates`' two candidate shapes gets a title naming its stop kind. The field descriptions don't change. Joe changed this from two experiments, prompt only and then prompt plus schema hints, to one, on 2026-11-09, in chat.
  - Split tools: `add_meal_candidates` and `add_attraction_candidates`, each with one candidate shape.
- In the split tools experiment, the replay won't find `add_stop_candidates` for an earlier worker's recorded calls, and logs them as refused. Leave it so, with no translation to the new tools. It touches 6 of the 32 cases, where the coordinator was still sending workers while earlier ones added candidates. The only change the worker sees is a stop on the same day that another worker filled, which reads "No candidates yet." in place of "No place selected yet." Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- Then try Joe's change for the `no-route` refusal on the `no-route` split. It's the one leg scout case where Google finds no driving route from Port Angeles through Hurricane Ridge. Its baseline: 15 of 26 candidate calls refused, 11 of them for no driving route, in 4 of its 5 runs.
  - What goes wrong: the coordinator set a waypoint near the end of the dead-end Hurricane Ridge road. One candidate, a place named "Hurricane Ridge", gets no route, likely since its pin is off the road. The reply names the waypoint ("passing Hurricane Hill Nature Trial"), which the leg scout can't see, and says to try stopping at a pass-through point, which only the coordinator can do. It doesn't say which place failed, or that the others routed. In all 4 baseline runs with the refusal, the leg scout read the waypoint's name as one of its own candidates, tried subsets by trial and error, and saved a set of one while testing. All 4 ended with one candidate. The live run ended with 2.
  - The change: the add candidate tools route each candidate on its own, as they already do, and catch Google's no-route failure for each one, not only the first. When any candidate has no route, the call is refused, and the reply names every candidate with no route, whether one, two, or all three. It says the others have routes, when any do, and leaves out the waypoints. The coordinator's tools keep today's message, since they can change waypoints. The fake route finder gets a way to fail only the routes through a given place, for the tests. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- In the `no-route` PR, also fix the design doc lines that still name `add_stop_candidates`, from the CI review note on #285: `StopsService.addCandidates()` and `LegsService.detourTimesOf()` in the domain model (4.6 and 4.7), the `search_along_leg` row and its paragraph in tool design 2.2, and the along-leg search line in `design/data-sources/google.md`. Each should name `add_meal_candidates` and `add_attraction_candidates`, as tool design 2.1 does.
- Results on the `visit-time` split, 125 runs each (baseline, then prompt and titles at e2f6a14, then split tools at fc2047a): refused for `visitTimeInMinutes` 112, 11, and 1 of 572, 471, and 459 candidate calls. Refused of any kind 117, 16, and 4. Runs with nothing refused 46, 109, and 121. Each had the same 455 calls go through. The split added no call to the wrong tool. Joe picked the split tools on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- Results on the `no-route` split, 5 runs each (baseline, then #286 at a0b8db8): 15 and 2 of 26 and 12 candidate calls refused, 11 and 2 for no driving route. Runs with nothing refused 1 and 3, though 3 of the new runs never picked Hurricane Ridge. In the runs that got the no-route error, the Hurricane Ridge stop ended with 1, 1, 1, and 1 candidates in the baseline, and with 3 and 2 after. Each new refusal was followed by a call that went through. Joe accepted the reply's wording, and #286 merged on 2026-11-09.
- ~~After the `no-route` change, fix the `rating` key.~~ Joe decided on 2026-11-09, in chat, to leave it alone. All 10 refusals, across the baseline and the prompt and titles and split tools runs, came from the stay researcher, and each sent `"rating": ""`, always empty, on one candidate, right before `rationale`. That's 10 in about 1,640 candidate calls. They're spread over 8 cases, and no case hit it more than 2 times in 15 runs. Each time, the worker's next try sent the same places without it and went through. The reasoning before and after says nothing about a rating. Once, the model called it "the stray field". It looks like a random slip, likely toward `rating` while writing `rationale`, not something a case brings on, so a fix couldn't be shown to work without several full runs. Joe's ideas, places without hours (explained by hotels, which mostly have none) and the prompt's rationale line naming "the rating", weren't borne out or couldn't be tested.
- Run the whole dataset once, after the split tools and the `no-route` change are both in, not after each. If the results surprise, the run can't say which change caused it. Joe accepted that on 2026-11-09, in chat, to save the time of a full run after each change.
- Results on the whole dataset, 160 runs each (baseline at 6a99245, experiment RXhwZXJpbWVudDo5, then main at 524cffb, experiment RXhwZXJpbWVudDoxMw==): 132 and 5 of 713 and 585 candidate calls refused. 581 and 580 calls went through, so the drop in calls is the retries. Runs with nothing refused 77 and 157. By kind: `visitTimeInMinutes` 112 and 3, no driving route 11 and 1, `rating` 3 and 1, and 6 and 0 others (4 places already a candidate, from the leg scout's trial and error on Hurricane Ridge, a `tier` on an attraction, and a place ID with a stray comma). The 3 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals came in one stay researcher run, as 3 meal calls sent at once, each with a visit time and no tier. Its next calls sent the same places with a tier, and all went through. The 1 no-route refusal named Hurricane Ridge, and the leg scout's next call for that stop went through, with 2 candidates. No call went to the wrong tool.
- Make the fix. If it changes what an agent reads, run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the view files with it. The implementer drafts any wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run the evaluation again. Record the results before and after in the PR.

## Done when

- The count across the corpus is recorded in this issue.
- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with the refusal rate in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.

nodes.body: The Codex run of the San Francisco trip (#271) had 2 more: `add_stop_candidates`, refused by the input schema, at 21:31:30 and 21:31:32 UTC on 2026-11-04, in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project.

More counts, from the runs on 2026-11-04 in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project:

- **Route 66 with Claude Code (#272), 23:43 to 00:00 UTC:** the stay researcher's `add_stop_candidates` calls were refused 13 times out of 63, in 8 of its 15 turns. Most were meal stops sent with `visitTimeInMinutes`, and one sent `tier` where it wasn't wanted. 11 came back as the raw `invalid_union` dump, and 2 as the tool's own message. Each one was fixed on the next try. One leg scout call was also refused, for leaving out `notes`.
- **Colorado with Codex (#274), both runs:** 1 refusal in the first run and 2 in the second. All were the stay researcher sending `visitTimeInMinutes`.

The Codex run of the Pacific Northwest trip (#275) had 5 more, all the stay researcher's `add_stop_candidates` calls for meal stops with `visitTimeInMinutes`, from 01:34:19 to 01:34:42 UTC on 2026-11-05, in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project. 1 came back as the raw `invalid_union` dump and 4 as the tool's own message. Each was fixed on the next try.

The Claude Code run of the Montana trip (#273) had 1 more: the leg scout's `add_stop_candidates` for a meal stop with `visitTimeInMinutes`, at 01:37:00 UTC on 2026-11-05, in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project. It came back as the raw input validation error, and was fixed on the next try.

## The count across the corpus, 2026-11-08

From the traces of the 21 corpus sessions in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project. A refusal is a candidate tool span with an error status.

- **106 worker runs made 361 candidate calls, and 47 were refused (13%).** 32 of the 106 runs had at least one.
- **The stay researcher:** 57 runs, 27 with a refusal, 41 of 264 calls refused. **The leg scout:** 49 runs, 5 with a refusal, 6 of 97 calls refused.
- **What was wrong:**
  - 41 mixed up `tier` and `visitTimeInMinutes`. 33 came back as the MCP SDK's raw Zod union dump, and 8 as the tool's own message.
  - 2 sent a `rating` key to `add_lodging_candidates`.
  - 4 weren't a wrong key: 2 had no driving route Google could find, 1 named a place the trip didn't have, and 1 sent input that wasn't valid JSON.
- **The refusals came in 13 turns of 11 sessions.** 11 of the 12 corpus sessions that sent out a stay researcher or a leg scout had one.

**In every worker run with a refusal, the coordinator saved changes to the trip earlier in the same turn,** before it sent the worker. In 31 of the 32, that included changes to stops, such as `add_stops`, `update_stop`, or `select_user_place`. So the turn's trip version alone isn't the trip the worker found, and a case has to replay those saves first (the open question on where the trip comes from). Across all 106 worker runs, only 5 were sent with no save before them.

| Session | Turn | Started (UTC) | Workers with a refusal | Refused | Coordinator saves before the workers were sent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9` | 5 | 2026-10-30 15:38 | 1 stay-researcher | 3 of 7 | `set_waypoints` x2, `add_stops` x2, `update_stop` x1, `move_stop` x2, `add_memory_item` x2, `remove_stops` x1, `update_day` x1, `update_trip_brief` x1 |
| `7b417a52-9ed3-46bb-8457-7705ac231aa8` | 6 | 2026-11-04 18:28 | 2 stay-researcher | 2 of 27 | `add_memory_item` x2, `update_day` x1, `add_stops` x3, `remove_stops` x1 |
| `7b417a52-9ed3-46bb-8457-7705ac231aa8` | 11 | 2026-11-04 19:30 | 1 stay-researcher | 1 of 2 | `add_memory_item` x1, `select_candidate` x4, `remove_stops` x1 |
| `6a5a3840-2911-46d0-8579-aae28f06961b` | 5 | 2026-11-04 20:03 | 2 stay-researcher | 5 of 11 | `update_stop` x1, `select_user_place` x3, `add_stops` x2, `remove_stops` x1, `set_waypoints` x1 |
| `6a5a3840-2911-46d0-8579-aae28f06961b` | 16 | 2026-11-04 20:09 | 1 stay-researcher | 2 of 5 | `add_stops` x3, `move_stop` x4, `add_memory_item` x1, `update_memory_item` x1, `update_trip_brief` x1, `add_stay` x1 |
| `700f1751-d81d-4a6d-bad8-28a817585a6c` | 9 | 2026-11-04 21:31 | 2 stay-researcher | 2 of 6 | `select_user_place` x3, `add_stops` x4 |
| `7f9743d3-b36d-477a-a1f2-b605daedbf4d` | 5 | 2026-11-04 22:17 | 1 stay-researcher, 1 leg-scout | 2 of 8 | `move_stop` x1, `update_stop` x1, `select_user_place` x2, `add_stops` x2, `update_day` x2, `update_trip_brief` x1 |
| `30d5cb5b-1268-4de3-b9ca-bda17f574824` | 6 | 2026-11-04 22:31 | 1 stay-researcher | 1 of 5 | `update_stop` x1, `select_user_place` x2, `add_stops` x1 |
| `c6a920ff-5995-45c3-b8fa-6a36d521ac9b` | 8 | 2026-11-04 23:48 | 1 stay-researcher | 2 of 6 | `add_memory_item` x1 |
| `dd7cba36-d36b-49f0-9ede-210c11a2285a` | 7 | 2026-11-04 23:52 | 7 stay-researcher, 1 leg-scout | 12 of 37 | `add_memory_item` x1, `select_user_place` x1, `update_trip_brief` x1, `update_stop` x2, `add_stops` x1, `remove_stops` x1 |
| `856a680c-c793-42ae-a817-e0dea4837890` | 4 | 2026-11-05 01:34 | 3 stay-researcher, 1 leg-scout | 7 of 17 | `add_memory_item` x1, `select_user_place` x1, `add_stops` x1, `update_stop` x1 |
| `d765a372-acc4-4e2b-a93c-69a9dc74e537` | 10 | 2026-11-05 01:36 | 2 stay-researcher, 1 leg-scout | 3 of 13 | `update_stop` x2 |
| `f029cbae-16de-4ac0-882c-4469ccd71f54` | 11 | 2026-11-05 14:46 | 3 stay-researcher, 1 leg-scout | 5 of 19 | `select_user_place` x1, `add_stops` x1, `add_memory_item` x1, `update_day` x2 |

Turn numbers are by the order of the session's `coordinator.turn` spans, not checked against `run-turn`'s count of user messages.

The tooling to run a worker alone and the evaluation is in PR #284. Merging it doesn't close this issue. Its description lists what's left to test, in order, and what the testing needs: the two SSH tunnels, the local Postgres, and the `LIVE_POSTGRES_*` values in the local `.env`. After that, the open question on which cases and how many runs, then the baseline, the fix, and the run after it.

## Baseline, 2026-11-09

The candidate refusals experiment ran on the tools and prompts as they are, at commit 6a99245 on the PR branch (#284). It ran all 32 cases 5 times each, which is 160 worker runs. Both workers were on Sonnet 5.5. All 160 runs finished and were scored. It's `candidate refusals all 6a99245` in Phoenix, on the `candidate-refusals` dataset.

Before it, two trials ran each of their cases once: `trial-1` with 3 cases and `trial-2` with 12. Both were clean.

**Refusal rate: 132 of 713 candidate calls refused, 18.5%.**

| Worker | Runs | Candidate calls | Refused | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stay researcher | 135 | 652 | 117 | 17.9% |
| Leg scout | 25 | 61 | 15 | 24.6% |

77 of the 160 runs had no refusal. When they were recorded, the same 32 worker runs had 47 of 163 calls refused, which is 28.8%. They were picked for having a refusal, so that rate runs high.

**What was refused:**

| Reply | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop, as the schema's error | 97 |
| `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop, as the tool's own message | 15 |
| Google found no driving route to the place | 11 |
| The place is already a candidate for the stop | 4 |
| A `rating` key (2 on stops, 1 on lodging) | 3 |
| A `tier` key on a stop that doesn't take one | 1 |
| A place ID with a comma on the end | 1 |

`visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop is 112 of the 132. The 11 refusals with no driving route are the tool's true answer, not a mistake in the call, so a fix can't bring the rate to zero.

**Across cases:** 6 cases had no refusal in any of their 5 runs. 5 cases had a refusal in all 5.

**The setup:** 15 runs had a checkpoint that differed. They are all 5 runs of 3 cases from one session, where Google's route for Day 11 is now 0.8 miles shorter and 1 minute slower. That moves two stops 1 to 2 minutes later. The stops and places the worker sees are the same. No other run had a difference.

Done. The fixes went in through #285 (add_meal_candidates and add_attraction_candidates) and #286 (the no-route reply). Joe decided on 2026-11-09 to leave the `rating` key alone, since it's a rare random slip. On the whole dataset, refused candidate calls went from 132 of 713 to 5 of 585, and runs with nothing refused from 77 to 157 of 160. The details are in the Do list. The evaluation stays in the set as `npm run candidate-refusals`.

title: The workers send keys their candidate tools refuse, checked with an evaluation

body:
## Why

The app is meant to suggest unusual places from Atlas Obscura, but in real trips it never looks. Three sessions in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project had 28 stay researcher and leg scout runs and no Atlas Obscura search. None of the 274 candidates they added links to Atlas Obscura, and the workers' traced thinking never mentions it.

| Trip | Phoenix session ID |
|---|---|
| Bar Harbor | `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9` |
| Florida | `7b417a52-9ed3-46bb-8457-7705ac231aa8` |
| San Francisco to Los Angeles (simulated user) | `6a5a3840-2911-46d0-8579-aae28f06961b` |

The search itself works. A local run on 2026-10-30 searched "Cambria San Simeon Morro Bay unusual places" with `allowed_domains` set to `atlasobscura.com`, and got results. What stops it is when the workers are told to search:

- **The stay researcher skipped its rule.** Its prompt says to run both a general and an Atlas Obscura search when it fills attraction stops for a stay of two or more nights. That applied to three Florida stays: Titusville (later moved to Cocoa Beach), Miami, and Key West. It ran neither search for those stops.
- **The stay researcher's rule leaves out one-night stays.** That covers Portland on the Bar Harbor trip, and every stay on the San Francisco trip.
- **The leg scout searches only for a stop an unusual place fits.** The stops it got had narrow purposes, such as "a classic Maine lighthouse on the coast drive", or were only lunch. The Bar Harbor trip's Day 1 drive had only a lunch stop, so nothing led it to search.
- **The coordinator leaves no stop open for a surprise.** It picks the attractions itself and writes narrow purposes. A user who doesn't ask for odd places never sees one, even where they're close by. Example: a search from Claude Code, not through the app, for "Bangor Maine unusual places", limited to `atlasobscura.com`, listed Stephen King's former house and the Paul Bunyan statue.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), 6.1 (the stay researcher) and 6.2 (the leg scout).
- [Web search design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/web-search.md), sections 2 and 3.
- `src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts` and `src/agent/leg-scout-prompt.ts`, each in its `WEB_SEARCH` text.
- #223, the evaluation of how the leg scout checks its Atlas Obscura finds. It also counts the towns the leg scout searches. This issue is about whether the workers search at all, and whether the user sees what they find.

## Open questions

- How do Atlas Obscura finds reach the user? Proposal: each worker runs one Atlas Obscura search for each town it covers, whatever the stops' purposes, and hands the best finds to the coordinator, which offers them as extras. Fixing the stay researcher's skipped rule alone isn't enough, since it would still leave out one-night stays and drives with no attraction stop.
- Should the coordinator ask whether the user likes offbeat places, and search only if they do? Proposal: no. Offering one or two finds lets the user decide, and a user who wouldn't think to ask still sees them.
- How is it scored? Proposal: code counts the Atlas Obscura searches and the towns they name for each run, from the trace, and checks whether a find reached the coordinator's reply. A judge on Haiku says whether each find it offered fits the user.
- Which cases, and how many runs? Proposal: the Bar Harbor trip and the Florida trip, recorded above, from a turn that sends out workers (`npm run run-turn`, DEVELOPMENT.md section 5), with 5 runs for each case.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the instructions as they are now.
- Change the workers' and the coordinator's instructions as the open questions settle, and update the technical spec and the web search design to match. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run the evaluation again. Record the results before and after in the PR.

## Done when

- The results before and after the change are recorded for each case.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

Two deploys, from the merges of #278 and #280, restarted the app at 23:25 and 23:29. The first restart cut off the over-sharer's first message, which is the main thing this trip tests. The simulated user then sent it all again. The second restart cut off a later turn. Joe decided to stop the run partway and run it again. The session has a `not_for_evaluation` session annotation in Phoenix. The second run started at 2026-11-04T23:43:15Z, after checking that no deploy was running.

## Results, second run

Claude Code with Sonnet, as `claude-code-sonnet`, on the live site. Started 2026-11-04 23:43 UTC and ran about 17 minutes, with 23 tool calls. It cost $0.44 on the simulated user's side. No restarts and no cut-off replies. The run passes every check, with the slips below.

| | ID |
|---|---|
| Trip | `trip_nav4zqta` |
| Session 1 | `session_s7y4uxn2`, Phoenix `dd7cba36-d36b-49f0-9ede-210c11a2285a` (11 turns) |
| Session 2 (what's left to decide) | `session_rskn57ke`, Phoenix `bd9cf7d9-7b44-441f-acad-ab556793659c` (2 turns) |

**The first message gave nearly the whole trip at once, and the coordinator saved it in one turn.** It saved the start, end, date, 12 days, the interests, all eight must-sees, the four food places, the old-road preference, 5 hours of driving, 8:30 starts, meals, and lodging. In the same reply it drafted a 12-day plan. The bot user's memory said 4 hours of driving and 6:30 dinners, so the coordinator asked whether 5 hours was only for this trip, and checked the dinner time.

**The simulated user stuck to the trip file: pass.** It made up a few things that fit the trip: 6:30 dinners, a local diner breakfast most mornings, a Saturday-morning flight home, checking in before the neon walks, and a stroll around downtown Springfield.

**It acted like a user, as its persona says: pass, with slips.**
- It played the over-sharer well. It wrote long, excited messages. It added stories, like its dad stopping at the Cozy Dog. It said "I know I keep saying that" when it repeated itself. It held firm on the Cozy Dog when the planner offered to skip it.
- It made each change at a point the trip file allows. It asked for 16 days after the plan was drafted. The coordinator said 14 is the maximum, and the user took 14. The coordinator had already suggested the Wigwam Motel in its first draft, and the user asked to make sure of it. The user asked about the Grand Canyon after the Arizona days were laid out, and went with Day 11 and sunset at the rim. Then it started the new session and asked what was left.
- Slip: it never used a card's buttons. It named the 11 motels in chat. Then it asked the coordinator to pick all the diners and roadside stops, more than 70 cards, and the coordinator did. The instructions allow picking in chat, and an over-sharer who trusts the planner fits the persona. But this run doesn't test picking from cards.
- Slip: it broke the instructions on how to run `chat.sh`. It piped `itinerary` into `head` once and into `sed` and `cut` once. It used `grep` once on its own saved output from `cards`, which is outside the run folder. It also sent its last message and an `itinerary` in parallel. It saw nothing a user wouldn't see, since it only read the app's own output. The cause is a setup gap. `--allowedTools "Bash(./chat.sh:*)"` doesn't block read-only commands like `grep` or `head`, because Claude Code runs those without asking. So the simulated user could also have read other run folders.

**The trip brief matches the trip file: pass.** This is from the last `read_trip_brief`, at the start of session 2. It has the focus, 14 days after change 1, the interests with the old-road wish, all eight must-sees plus the start on Adams Street, the four food places, the Grand Canyon side trip, 5 hours of driving, a scenic route, 8:30 starts, diners and local joints with no chains, 6:30 dinners, and neon motels or mid-range. The four food places are saved twice, in both the must-sees and the meals. The itinerary has October 2 to 15, the first Route 66 sign in Chicago to the Santa Monica Pier, and the Wigwam Motel in Holbrook. There's no budget item, since the planner never asked.

**Refused calls:** 16, and each was fixed on the next try.
- The stay researchers' `add_stop_candidates` calls were refused 13 times out of 63. That's #266, and I added the counts there.
- One leg scout `add_stop_candidates` call left out `notes`.
- The coordinator's `select_user_place` gave "Google found no driving route from Pontiac through Cozy Dog Drive In, Old Chain of Rocks Bridge Parking to St. Louis."
- The coordinator's `add_memory_item` was refused for going over 300 characters, at 333.

**App bugs filed:** none.

Closing with no PR. The setup didn't change. The read-only commands only read Claude Code's own saved output, at the path Claude Code gave it, so no change is needed there. Joe decided the README doesn't need a note about waiting for deploys for now.

## Results

**The session is in Phoenix.** One run, on 2026-11-05 from 01:29 to 01:46 UTC, about 18 minutes. Claude Code with Sonnet, as `claude-code-sonnet`, with the `skeptic` persona. It ran at the same time as the Codex run of #275, which was a different bot user. Trip `trip_emnm5d8j`, with app sessions `session_fzfcvjf5` and `session_6hcgnrw3`. In the `road-trip-agent` project they're the Phoenix sessions `d765a372-acc4-4e2b-a93c-69a9dc74e537` (40 turns) and `849d0b8a-f5f2-4b4e-a321-3d4cc17c590c` (2 turns). It took 51 turns and cost $0.58.

**It stuck to the trip file: passed.** No fact it gave contradicts the trip file. All five changes were made:

- **One long day:** the planner's route put the long day from Virginia City to West Glacier, about 6 hours. It never split it. When dinner pushed it to 6 hours 6 minutes, the simulated user said that day was fine.
- **A night in the park:** asked when lodging came up. The planner offered Old Faithful or Canyon, and it took the Old Faithful Inn.
- **Wolves at dawn:** the planner set a 5:15 a.m. start for Lamar Valley before the simulated user asked. It agreed, "but just that one day".
- **A day shorter:** asked after all five hotels were picked. It took the planner's pick, dropping the West Yellowstone night.
- **New session:** asked what's left. The planner named only Logan Pass, which it couldn't add (below). The simulated user was happy to leave it.

Where the trip file has no answer, its choices fit the trip: a 2 p.m. flight home, 7:00 dinners, Mammoth Hot Springs, and the Ennis dinner.

**It acted like a user: passed, with two slips.**

- Three times it clicked five or six cards in one step, where the instructions say one `./chat.sh` command at a time. None was refused, and each reply came back in order.
- The cards output was long, so Claude Code saved it to a file in its own config folder, `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude/`, and the simulated user read it from there. That's outside the run folder, but it held only the output of its own `cards` command.

It played the skeptic well, and questioned five facts:

- where the 4 hours of driving came from
- the 5¼ hours from Virginia City to West Glacier
- whether the Old Faithful Inn is open in mid-September
- which closing time was right for Nevada City
- why Wonderland Cafe for dinner

It took each answer and moved on. On Wonderland, the coordinator said it hadn't recommended it: the user had picked it from the card. It was firm about Logan Pass, and asked to have it put in.

**The trip brief matches the trip file's facts: passed.** From the last `mcp__trip__read_trip_brief` span, at 01:45:58 UTC, on the new session's first turn: 6 days, 6 hours of driving, scenic, 7:00 a.m., the five must-sees plus the Roosevelt Arch and the huckleberry milkshake, the interests, early hearty breakfasts with a nicer dinner, and mid-range lodging with a night inside Yellowstone. The itinerary holds September 13 to 18, 2027, the Bozeman airport to the Missoula airport, and a 10:00 start on Day 1.

**The bot user's memory didn't match this persona.** User memory held 4 items from earlier runs: 4 hours of driving, dinner at 6:30, never eat at chains, and check in before the evening. The coordinator used the 4 hours in its first reply, and named the no-chains rule and 6:30 dinners in its fourth. The simulated user asked where each came from. The coordinator explained, set this trip to 6 hours, and saved a trip memory item not to use the four on this trip. In #68, #272, and #276 the memory matched the trip file. This is the first run where it didn't.

**Google routed on today's winter road closures.** It treated Yellowstone's inner roads and Going-to-the-Sun Road as closed. Days 2 and 3 showed 8 to 14½ hours of driving, and Logan Pass couldn't be added. The coordinator told the user each time and gave its own September times. Filed as #281.

**Refused tool calls:** 12, and each agent went on.

- 5 were the winter closures: 2 `compute_route` and 3 `select_user_place` calls. These are in #281.
- 1 was the leg scout's `add_stop_candidates` for a meal stop with `visitTimeInMinutes`, as in #266. A note is on that issue.
- 1 `update_memory_item` was over 300 characters, at 317, as in #272. It was cut and saved on the next try.
- 1 `look_up_stay_weather` got "Too many concurrent requests" from Open-Meteo. It worked on a retry 3 seconds later.
- The rest happened once each. The stay researcher sent `add_stop_candidates` input that wasn't valid JSON, and made up a place ID, `place_mercantile`. The leg scout called `search_near` for a stop along a leg.

**App bugs:** #281.

It asked for a brewery dinner after the hotels were picked, and the coordinator chose Glenwood Canyon Brewpub for Day 2. It asked about the cog railway, and the coordinator swapped it in. - It played the skeptic. It asked how sure the planner was that the other roads would be open. It asked whether the train time shown was a real departure. It never asked "why that one?" about a pick, which the persona says it should do now and then.
- Slip: it gave a lot in some messages. One message had both the evening soak and the cog railway, plus a go-ahead for the searches. Another had food, lodging, a request to add the whole loop, and Pikes Peak, which it named before being asked what places it had in mind.

**The trip brief matches the trip file: pass.** This is from the last `read_trip_brief`, at the start of session 2. It has the focus, 5 days, the interests, the four must-sees with the roads swapped in, 4 hours of driving, a scenic route, an 8 a.m. start, local food with green chile and breweries, and mid-range lodging except The Stanley. The itinerary has May 17 to 21 and Denver to Denver, which are the start date and the end place. It also has The Stanley on night 1, The Parkway Cafe in Boulder for breakfast on Day 1, and the cog railway up Pikes Peak on Day 5, getting home at 2:25 p.m. There's no budget item, since the planner never asked.

**Refused calls:** two, and the agent fixed both on the next try.
- The coordinator's `set_waypoints` gave "This trip has no place Nederland, CO."
- A stay researcher's `add_stop_candidates` was refused for an extra `visitTimeInMinutes` key.

**Codex read only its own files.** Its one command besides `./chat.sh` was `cat` on the three files in the run folder.

**App bugs filed:** none.

Joe decided on 2026-11-04 to run this trip again, without the restarts. Session 1's cut-off turn is where the evening soak and the cog railway were handled, and an evaluation can't see it. Both sessions above now have a `not_for_evaluation` session annotation in Phoenix. The second run started at 2026-11-04T23:43:15Z, after checking that no deploy was running.

Also, the stay researcher's refused `add_stop_candidates` call, for sending `visitTimeInMinutes`, is the same refusal as #266.

## Results, second run

Codex with gpt-6.1-terra, as `codex-gpt-terra`, on the live site. Started 2026-11-04 23:43 UTC and ran about 12 minutes, with 33 commands. No restarts and no cut-off replies. The run passes every check, and it's the one to evaluate.

| | ID |
|---|---|
| Trip | `trip_4qnvhw8d` |
| Session 1 | `session_z766nv4g`, Phoenix `c6a920ff-5995-45c3-b8fa-6a36d521ac9b` (10 turns) |
| Session 2 (what's left to decide) | `session_w5rnxsyd`, Phoenix `aed48550-a3fe-4bc9-b62b-3882576478b4` (8 turns) |

**The coordinator caught the seasonal closure without being asked.** In its first reply, before it knew the dates, it said Trail Ridge Road and Independence Pass close from about mid-October to late May. Once the user gave May 17, it said both would probably still be closed that week. That was before the user named either road. It offered to move the trip to June, or keep the dates and drive each road up to its winter gate, with other open roads around them.

**The simulated user stuck to the trip file: pass.** It made up a few things that fit the trip: 6:30 p.m. dinners, hotel or quick breakfasts on the other mornings, and checking in before dinner.

**It acted like a user, as its persona says: pass, with a slip.**
- It made each change at a point the trip file allows. For the closed roads, it asked what to do instead, and asked how certain the May 27 opening date was. It kept the dates and took the substitutes. It asked for the evening soak, 7 to 9 p.m., and it was set. It asked for a brewery dinner after the hotels were picked, and the coordinator put Glenwood Canyon Brewpub on Day 3. It asked about the cog railway, and the coordinator swapped it in. Then it started the new session, asked what was left, and picked from the cards there.

- Slip: when the planner asked how they like to eat, it said local, unfancy places and green chile, but left out "a brewery for dinner when there's a good one." That's why the brief's meal item has no breweries. Craft beer is in the interests, and the coordinator offered brewpub dinners anyway.

The meal item has no breweries, as the slip above explains. The itinerary has May 17 to 21, Denver to Denver, The Stanley on night 1, and The Parkway Cafe in Boulder for breakfast on Day 1. It gets home at 5:23 p.m. on Friday, in time for dinner. There's no budget item, since the planner never asked.

The 4 hours of driving came from the bot user's memory before the user said it. Memory held one item from an earlier run: "About 4 hours of driving a day is normally comfortable for them." It matches the trip file.

On 2026-11-04 from 22:44 to 22:58 UTC, about 14 minutes. The simulated user ran 47 commands and used about 7.2 million input tokens, almost all cached, and 7,700 output tokens. Codex logs no cost.

- Trip: `trip_5y2q49hg`
- Session 1: `session_xekkgnnu`, Phoenix session `52fad757-3acb-4660-a1e3-8d6beb20c720` (23 turns)
- Session 2: `session_zwr8vc8d`, Phoenix session `1f5e8cec-381b-44b3-b130-030ab8e9fa40` (3 turns)

The trip ended as 4 days, Monday October 11 to Thursday October 14, 2027, Grand Junction to Salt Lake City. It has 2 nights at Best Western Plus Canyonlands Inn and 1 night at Motel Torrey. `cards` shows none open.

**It stuck to the trip file: pass.** No fact contradicts the trip file.

- Changes 1 and 2 (Milt's, the pie): skipped. The planner never said either place was closed. It only said the pies often sell out.
- Change 3 (a longer day): it agreed, "keep the longer day for the hoodoos and capitol reef." It agreed again when stargazing took the day to about 5½ hours.
- Change 4 (a day later): made right after the weather and packing advice appeared.
- Change 5 (one night less): it cut Moab to 2 nights and dropped the rest day. Then it asked for the 5-hour hike, after the sunrise hike. It moved the Windows to Day 1, dropped Love Muffin and Corona Arch, and picked Devils Garden, 9:00 to 2:00.

- Some messages ran past one sentence and held several answers, such as "just capitol reef around 1 a.m. check in first. day 4 at 8, day 5 at 10. no salt lake dinner." The middle message was 14 words, and the longest 21. Most of it answered questions the planner had asked.

The only command other than `./chat.sh` was `cat instructions.md trip.md persona.md`. Nothing was refused. Its final note matches the log.

**The trip brief matches the trip file's facts: pass.** The last brief, read at the start of session 2:

```
focus: Utah red rock parks
tripLengthInDays: 4
interestsText: red rock parks, hiking, arches and dark skies
mustSeesText: delicate arch at sunrise, capitol reef and goblin valley
comfortableDrivingInHours: 4
routePreference: scenic
usualStartTime: 8:00 a.m.
```
